articles.title: Over 20,000 kg of fish die in latest Laguna de Bay fish kill
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — More than 20,000 kilograms of tilapia and bighead carp have died in another fish kill in Laguna de Bay, affecting more than 30 fish cages covering over 7 hectares in Jala-jala,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — More than 20,000 kilograms of tilapia and bighead carp have died in another fish kill in Laguna de Bay, affecting more than 30 fish cages covering over 7 hectares in Jala-jala, Rizal.

Fishers’ group Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas (Pamalakaya) said Tuesday that initial losses were estimated at P700,000, while local fishers and fish cage operators suspected chemical waste may have contributed to the “sudden and massive” fish kill.
Ronnel Arambulo, Pamalakaya vice chairperson, said operators and fishers noticed that the lake’s water had turned rusty in color before the fish began dying.
“Operators and fishers themselves said that the fish kill was unusual. Similar incidents have occurred in previous years, but what happened recently was more rapid and widespread,” Arambulo said.
“The affected fishers could not point to any other possible cause except the change in the color of the lake’s water that they had observed,” he added.
Pamalakaya described Tuesday’s incident as the second fish kill in Laguna de Bay, saying a similar incident occurred in Binangonan, Rizal, in July.
“Last July, the same incident happened in Binangonan town following the release of wastewater by a water concessionaire,” Pamalakaya said.
During its initial investigation in July, the Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) said it was still too early to determine the exact cause of the fish kill.
The agency noted that Laguna de Bay was experiencing a widespread algal bloom and that most of the affected fish came from commercial fish pens and cages.
The latest incident also came days after the LLDA warned of a continued risk of algal blooms and possible fish kills in the lake.

On Aug. 25, the agency said changes in weather and water conditions could trigger or intensify algal growth. It also explained that when algae die and decompose, they can reduce oxygen levels in the water, potentially stressing or killing fish.

The LLDA also urged residents and local officials to report unusual water discoloration, heavy bubbling or foaming, and foul odors that could indicate water contamination. The agency said such reports could help investigators trace pollutants to their source.
Pamalakaya called on the LLDA to investigate the latest incident, determine whether any companies discharged wastewater into the lake and hold those responsible accountable.
“Some companies must have discharged wastewater into the lake that caused the fish kill,” Arambulo said.

“We call on the concerned government agencies, especially the Laguna Lake Development Authority, to look into this matter, hold accountable the companies responsible, and compensate the affected fisherfolk and fish cage operators,” he added. /dm

articles.title: Sandiganbayan acquits ex-Plant industry execs linked to ‘garlic cartel’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division acquitted two former Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI) officials and several entrepreneurs of graft charges in connection with the alleged…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division acquitted two former Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI) officials and several entrepreneurs of graft charges in connection with the alleged manipulation of garlic prices.
In a decision promulgated on Tuesday, the court said the prosecution failed to prove the accused’s guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

Among those acquitted were former BPI Director Clarito Barron, former National Plant Quarantine Services Division (NPQSD) Chief Merle Palacpac, and Philippine Vegetable Importers, Exporters and Vendors Association Group of Companies (Philvieva) Director Lilia Cruz.
The NPQSD is a division under the BPI which is the Department of Agriculture’s regulatory arm for the importation, exportation and the domestic movement of plants and plant products.

Also acquitted were traders Rolando Manangan; Prudencio Ruedas; Ma. Jackielou Ilagan; Gaudioso Diato; Denia Matabang; Raffy Torres; Mary Grace Sebastian; Orestes Salon; Jon Dino de Veyra; Jose Angulo Jr.; Laila Matabang; Edmond Caguinguin; Napoleon Baldueza; Jose Ollegue; Rolan Galvez; and Renato Francisco Jr.
Fifth Division Chairperson Associate Justice Zaldy Trespeses noted that the P30,000 bonds each of the accused had posted will be released and the hold departure orders against them will be lifted.
He noted that Torres, Caguinguin and Ollegue were not present during the promulgation, but the decision was nonetheless promulgated.
Meanwhile, the decision said the same case against three other co-accused—businesswomen Rochelle Diaz, Shiela Mary dela Cruz and Angelita Flores, who all remained at large—was archived.
Cruz was appointed chairperson of the National Garlic Action Team (NGAT) by then-Agriculture Secretary Proceso Alcala in July 2013.
In November 2013, the NGAT recommended the importation of 58,240 metric tons of garlic to satisfy the local market’s requirements up until March 2014.
A total of 8,810 import permits were approved during the same period, of which 5,022 were issued to importers associated with Philvieva, according to the information filed by state prosecutors.
It added that, from January to July 2014, the price of imported garlic soared to between P260 and P400 per kilogram; from between P165 and P170 per kilogram from 2010 to 2013.

State prosecutors earlier pointed to Barron as the approving authority; and Palacpac and then-NPQSD chief Luben Marasigan as the recommending officers for the processing and release of the import permits.
The charge against Alcala was dismissed earlier this year due to insufficiency of evidence, while the charge against Marasigan was dismissed in 2021 due to his death. /jpv

articles.title: In Nepal’s flood zone, the second disaster is psychological
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — For four days, a couple in Nuwakot each believed that the other had been swept away by the flood. They were on opposite sides of the water, cut off, with no way to confirm the other…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — For four days, a couple in Nuwakot each believed that the other had been swept away by the flood. They were on opposite sides of the water, cut off, with no way to confirm the other was alive.

A psychosocial team from the Centre for Mental Health and Counseling Nepal finally reached both of them by phone and put them in touch. The moment they heard each other’s voices, they refused to wait any longer, not for the road to clear or for the river to calm.

They wanted to be reunited immediately, and were flown across by helicopter, according to Gopal Bohara, the psychologist who helped make the call. When they reached a holding centre set up to house flood survivors, their children ran to them, crying.

This was one small resolution inside a much larger crisis but a resolution nevertheless. A week into Nepal’s deadliest flood in a decade, the death toll has reached 951 as of Monday evening, with nearly 4,000 people still missing and over 11,000 people rescued. Alongside the massive casualty and physical destruction—with houses, roads, bridges and entire settlements gone—is a psychological toll that is harder to measure, one responders say is now only starting to surface.

The government’s mental health response has been scaling up quickly. Officials say around 50 psychiatrists, psychologists and psychosocial counsellors are currently deployed across Rasuwa and Nuwakot through the Epidemiology and Disease Control Division. A roster of 64 more trained counsellors are on standby in Bagmati Province. But for most survivors, that support is only just arriving. Typically, Psychological First Aid (PFA) is introduced a week after a disaster, according to mental health professionals involved in the response, which, in Rasuwa and Nuwakot, means now.

Pomawati Thapa, senior consultant and medical generalist at the Department of Health Service, said of the roughly 50 professionals currently deployed, about 10 are providing PFA directly, while a team of four is sent to Uttargaya in Rasuwa, a remote area without road access. Thapa said the department has drawn up a full deployment plan and is coordinating placements to all necessary locations.

The response was initially limited to PFA and volunteer mobilization as officials assessed the situation on the ground. As information on the scale and needs of affected communities became available, the Health Ministry expanded its deployment, Thapa said. The field response is being supported by partner organizations including the Nepal Red Cross Society, TPO Nepal, CMC Nepal, CWIN and Koshish.

The Ministry of Health and Food Safety Nepal is also providing psychosocial support through three hotlines, informed deputy spokesperson Samir Kumar Adhikari. The 1115 line, he said, handles overall coordination and general health-related counseling. Since the flood increased the need for mental health support, the ministry has also trained staff working on the 1115 line to provide basic psychosocial support.

blocks.caption: Usha Sibabhakti, a psychosocial counselor, waits at the help desk to assist flood survivors.

blocks.text: Dedicated psychosocial support, however, runs through a separate line, 1166, which is based at Patan Mental Hospital, Adhikari said. Calls to 1166 are routed there regardless of where they originate, and callers are connected with psychosocial counsellors. Seven psychosocial counsellors are currently working on rotation to provide round-the-clock services through the hotline. A third line, 1098, is a Child Helpline of a civil nature that the ministry is facilitating, Adhikari said.
On the ground, the stress is visible, with survivors showing signs of grief, anxiety and paranoia, Bohara said.

Bohara has been working with a psychosocial support team at Bhairum Secondary School, a holding centre in Bidur, Nuwakot. His four-member psychosocial team from CMC Nepal—comprising two psychologists and two psychosocial counselors—plans to stay 10 to 15 days, extending if necessary. They are working alongside medical teams and coordinating with local health authorities.
Bohara cited a case where two children have been repeatedly waking at night, having nightmares and crying out that the flood has come again.

“Most of them are currently in shock, unable to articulate their problems,” Bohara said. The team has not yet seen major signs of post-traumatic stress disorder among adults, but many are anxious, easily startled and frightened.

Yet formal counseling has barely begun for most survivors. In Nuwakot’s Bidur Municipality, psychiatrist Nirajan Bhattarai, who is part of a team deployed by the health ministry, said responders are currently prioritizing safety, basic needs and coordination.

“Safety and basic needs have to come first,” Bhattarai said. His team is currently providing emergency medication, including to people whose psychiatric treatment was disrupted and those experiencing severe sleep disturbances. Psychological First Aid and other interventions will follow as the immediate crisis stabilizes.

Although counsellors are present in the affected areas, much of their current work involves linking survivors with services, coordinating access to holding centres and helping with other immediate needs rather than conducting formal counselling sessions. Some holding centres have also not yet been able to accommodate everyone.

blocks.caption: In Nepal’s flood zone, the second disaster is psychological

blocks.text: Bhattarai said it is still too early to expect survivors to openly discuss what they have been through. What he has seen is that the adults are largely unwilling to interact with responders. “Even when people attempted to photograph or film the situation, some questioned why they were being recorded,” Bhattarai said. “Were they doing it to make money or get views?”
Children, meanwhile, appeared more willing to engage. But he cautioned that the psychological impact of the disaster may become more visible only after the dust settles.

That impact is already apparent in isolated but severe cases. In one case, a woman’s medication was washed away by the flood, after which her symptoms worsened. She had already been experiencing psychotic symptoms and was struggling with suicidal ideation, according to a member of Bohara’s psychosocial team. “She had attempted self-harm four times and was referred to Trishuli Hospital, where psychiatric care is available,” Bohara said.

Beyond individual symptoms, Bohara said, survivors are also dealing with a deeper loss: the loss of their community. He added that many displaced people are still moving between their homes and holding centers. Some whose houses remain standing are staying in the centers because they are afraid another flood could destroy them, while others return home during the day to collect food or check their properties. This constant movement has made it difficult for responders to maintain an accurate record of those staying at the centers.

Meanwhile, tensions are also emerging over relief distribution, particularly between people staying in rented rooms and those recognised as displaced. “As relief operations become more organized, providing primary psychological support in groups and making such services more accessible will be important,” Bohara said.

For now, both Bhattarai and Bohara say the priority remains keeping survivors safe, reconnecting those who have been separated, and providing PFA. And as the survivors begin to process what they have lost, they will need sustained psychosocial support. /dl

articles.title: Conservation drive intensifies to save rare Rafflesia in Samar town
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY— Conservation officials are stepping up efforts to protect one of Samar’s rarest treasures after signs of possible illegal timber poaching and other human disturbances near areas where…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY— Conservation officials are stepping up efforts to protect one of Samar’s rarest treasures after signs of possible illegal timber poaching and other human disturbances near areas where the endangered Samar rafflesia grows.

The Protected Area Management Office–Samar Island Natural Park (PAMO-SINP), in partnership with the local government unit of Basey, recently conducted a communication, education, and public awareness campaign to encourage residents to help protect Rafflesia manillana and its remaining habitat, which is mainly located in Barangay Guirang.

The Samar rafflesia is classified as endangered under Administrative Order No. 2026-20 of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, which places greater urgency on protecting both the species and the forest environment where it occurs.
The community campaign was conducted after conservation personnel saw signs of possible illegal timber poaching and other disturbances in and around areas known to support Rafflesia.

Officials explained to residents that protecting the plant is particularly challenging because the rafflesia has an unusual life cycle. Unlike ordinary plants, rafflesia has no stems, leaves, or roots, and cannot survive independently. It depends on a specific host vine for nutrients and requires an intact forest environment to complete its life cycle.

This makes the species especially vulnerable to activities that disturb or destroy its forest habitat. Even when the Rafflesia is not directly collected or damaged, removing trees and vegetation around its habitat can affect the conditions for the plant to survive and reproduce.
PAMO-SINP personnel pointed to the ecological importance of R. manillana, its endangered status, and the community’s role in protecting the forest ecosystem that supports it.
Residents were also encouraged to monitor their surroundings and report suspected illegal activities that could threaten the rafflesia or its habitat.

The orientation included discussions on Republic Act No. 11038, or the Expanded National Integrated Protected Areas System Act of 2018, which covers ecosystems and biodiversity within protected areas and prohibits unauthorized activities that damage, alter, or destroy protected habitats and wildlife.

For conservation officials, protecting Samar rafflesia is not simply about preserving a rare flower. Because the species is closely tied to its host vine and forest environment, its survival indicates the health and integrity of the wider ecosystem.

The forests of Samar provide habitat for numerous plant and animal species while also supporting communities that depend on forest resources. Protecting remaining Rafflesia habitat therefore forms part of a broader effort to conserve the island’s biodiversity./coa

articles.title: ChatGPT, Reddit, Roblox to adhere to EU’s ‘very large platform’ rules
articles.summary: ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox have four months to comply with additional obligations following their designation

blocks.text: ROBLOX. A boy poses for a photo while holding a game pad in front of a screen displaying the logo of the US children's gaming platform Roblox, in this illustration taken December 8, 2025.
Ramil Sitdikov/Illustration/Reuters
ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox have four months to comply with additional obligations following their designation
BRUSSELS, Belgium – The European Commission on Monday said ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox will need to adhere to the EU regulations for very large online platforms and search engines.
The services have declared that they reach at least 45 million monthly users in the EU.
This qualifies them for the “very large” designation under the bloc’s Digital Services Act, the Commission said.
ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox have four months to comply with additional obligations following their designation.

This includes assessing and mitigating risks of illegal content being disseminated through their platforms. They also need to mitigate the negative effects on minors, and on the physical and mental wellbeing of users.
Very large platforms and search engines also need to limit risks for fundamental rights, electoral processes and public security.
The Commission can supervise compliance with the DSA and will get investigative powers to assess functionalities behind the services.
AI-system ChatGPT qualifies as an online search engine under the DSA.
Gaming platform Roblox and discussion-based platform Reddit qualify as online platforms, as they enable users to disseminate third-party content to the public. – Rappler.com

articles.title: House panel ends OP budget briefing in less than an hour
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives committee on appropriations’ budget briefing on the proposed budget of the Office of the President (OP) in 2027 was terminated in less than an hour…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives committee on appropriations’ budget briefing on the proposed budget of the Office of the President (OP) in 2027 was terminated in less than an hour as part of parliamentary courtesy despite objections from some minority lawmakers.
Executive Secretary Ralph Recto presented the OP’s proposed budget of P10,156,000,000, which he noted is 64% lower than the budget allocated to the office this year.

“The substantial reduction reflects the lower operational requirements of our units and completion of our activities related to the hosting of the Asean [Association of Southeast Asian Nations] meeting for which no additional funding will be required next year,” Recto said.

“In short, we’re asking for less while we’re fully prepared to do more. We believe that this amount is sufficient for the presidency to meet the demands in leading the nation at the time of overlapping domestic and external challenges from geopolitical tensions and disruptions in the Middle East, typhoons, El Niño, and other calamities,” Recto added.
After Recto’s presentation, Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan made a motion to extend parliamentary courtesy to the OP by terminating interpellations, which was seconded by Rep. Ferdinand Hernandez.

Rep. Antonio Tinio, however, objected to the motion, stating that the tradition of parliamentary courtesy should be abolished by Congress in budget briefings to uphold transparency and accountability.
After the matter was put to a vote, 37 members of the committee voted in favor of the extension of parliamentary courtesy while five members from the minority voted in the negative.
Representatives Renee Co, Elijah Fernando, Sarah Elago, Iris Montes, and Tinio each explained their objections, emphasizing that the OP’s budget should be subject to scrutiny.

Rep. Albert Garcia, the committee’s senior vice chairperson, terminated the hearing as he shared that the questions on the OP’s proposed budget and other matters will be answered during or before the plenary session. /gsg

articles.title: Party-list solon pleads not guilty to graft raps
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Uswag Ilonggo party-list Rep. James “Jojo” Ang pleaded not guilty to two of the graft charges against him before the Sandiganbayan Sixth Division on Tuesday. Ang faces 14 counts…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Uswag Ilonggo party-list Rep. James “Jojo” Ang pleaded not guilty to two of the graft charges against him before the Sandiganbayan Sixth Division on Tuesday.
Ang faces 14 counts of violating Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act before the Sandiganbayan, two of which were raffled to the Sixth Division.

The information filed by state prosecutors as read during the hearing on Tuesday alleged that Ang had “direct and/or indirect financial interest” in contracts between the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) and Allencon Development Corporation.
The contracts in question were worth P8.18 million and P16.079 million.
Ang purportedly owned 500 shares in Allencon Development Corporation.

State prosecutors argued that Ang’s alleged acquisition of the shares violated Article VI, Section 14 of the 1987 Constitution, which prohibits lawmakers from being “interested financially in any contract with, or in any franchise or special privilege granted by the government.”
Before Ang’s arraignment, state prosecutors moved to amend the information filed to note that the amounts indicated in the charges were “more or less” P8.18 million and P16.079 million.
The prosecution cited “unquantifiable” differences between the amount stated in the contract and the budget approved by the DPWH.

However, Ang’s legal counsel, Luis Vera Cruz, argued that the motion to amend the information to include the phrase “more or less” would change the nature of the charges and affect the jurisdiction of the court.
Nonetheless, the Sandiganbayan Sixth Division granted prosecutors’ motion to amend the information.
The court set the preliminary conference on Monday afternoon, September 7 and the pretrial proper on Tuesday morning, September 8. /gsg

articles.title: Two dead after stabbing in New York’s Times Square
articles.summary: NEW YORK — A knife-wielding woman stabbed and killed a person and injured another in New York’s tourist-filled Times Square on Monday, before she was shot and killed by police. Mayor…

blocks.text: NEW YORK — A knife-wielding woman stabbed and killed a person and injured another in New York’s tourist-filled Times Square on Monday, before she was shot and killed by police.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the deaths in a press conference, saying that the second victim was in stable condition in a hospital.

The attacker, identified as 49-year-old Queens resident Pamela Cisneros, who was known to have mental health issues, pulled two large knives from a bag bearing the logo of a well-known supermarket chain before threatening passersby in broad daylight, New York Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said.
She then approached a 68-year-old man and stabbed him in the abdomen. Twenty seconds later, she attacked a 32-year-old woman, also stabbing her in the abdomen — wounds from which she later died.
The victims’ identities are not being released pending notification of their families.
Police quickly intervened and tried to persuade Cisneros to drop her weapons.
“The officers engaged the woman in dialog for four minutes and gave her numerous commands to drop the knives, which she refused,” Tisch said.
“During the encounter, she told the officers, ‘I’m not dropping anything. I would rather kill both of you,'” Tisch added.
One witness told local TV outlet PIX11 that the suspect had two knives in her hands and was tased by police before she rushed at officers.
“They shot her twice,” said the unnamed witness.
Police confirmed that they had unsuccessfully used a stun gun before firing their handguns.
Local news reports said the suspect was pronounced dead at hospital.
Tisch said that they do not believe the attack was terror-related.
“This was an extraordinarily dangerous situation unfolding in the heart of Times Square, the crossroads of the world,” the police chief said.
“At any given moment, there are 1000s of New Yorkers, commuters, tourists, families, workers moving through these streets.”
An AFP journalist at the scene saw a large emergency services presence and officials inspecting a patch of blood in Times Square. /dl

articles.title: Trump vows to hit Iran ‘hard’ after first exchange of fire in weeks
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — US President Donald Trump threatened on Monday to hit Iran “hard” after the two foes traded fire for the first time in weeks, as his Treasury secretary vowed to keep up…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — US President Donald Trump threatened on Monday to hit Iran “hard” after the two foes traded fire for the first time in weeks, as his Treasury secretary vowed to keep up a pressure campaign aimed at hobbling Tehran’s economy.
After six months of war, the foes remain at an impasse, with Iran keeping the strategic Strait of Hormuz closed and the US persisting with a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
On Sunday, the United States carried out strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran quickly retaliating by attacking US military targets in the Middle East.
The exchange raised fears of a return to major hostilities, with the US president vowing to respond.
“We’re going to hit them hard,” Trump said, according to a Fox News reporter who spoke to him briefly. “There will be a response.”
The United States said it attacked Iranian rocket launchers on the island of Larak to prevent Tehran planting mines in the key shipping lane.
Iran responded with missile and drone attacks aimed at Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, saying they targeted US forces there, but President Masoud Pezeshkian later on Monday called for dialogue.

“We continue to strive for a path of agreement and understanding, and we believe that continuing the war is neither in our interest, nor in the interest of the region,” he said at a summit in Kyrgyzstan, adding “the solution to the existing problems is dialogue and cooperation.”
Missiles, drones
State media reported that three people were killed in the US attack Sunday on Larak, with several others wounded.
Iran’s powerful Revolutionary Guards said the ballistic missile attack targeting two US air bases in Jordan caused “heavy damage”.

But Trump told Fox that all the missiles fired at US forces had been shot down, except for one that was determined not to pose a threat. Jordan’s army said it had intercepted eight missiles, without stating their origin.
Iran also said it targeted US personnel at an air base in the UAE, and shot down an American drone over Hormuz.
Abu Dhabi said it intercepted a drone over the country’s waters, but dismissed claims that Al Minhad Air Base had been targeted as “baseless.”

The Guards reported knocking out a second US drone over the Hormuz on Monday evening, and Iran’s armed forces central command reiterated a warning to its regional neighbours not to allow the US to use their territory to carry out attacks.

A tanker leaving the strait reported being hit by three “unknown projectiles” just off the northeastern edge of Oman, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said late Monday, noting that there were no known environmental impacts or casualties.
‘Continue exerting pressure’
The exchange of fire came after weeks of relative calm, with the Trump administration recently pivoting to “economic warfare”.
Earlier on Monday, Trump had called Iran “a Failed Nation”, saying on social media that its military was decimated, its finances were crumbling “and their leadership is in total disarray”.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent vowed to keep up the economic pain.
“We are going to continue exerting pressure, and we’ve had very good discussions here already,” Bessent told reporters at a G20 meeting in North Carolina.
He said a turning point in the pressure campaign could come “within weeks or months”.

Iran is exerting economic pressure of its own through its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, which has roiled global markets and driven up prices for American voters in a closely fought midterm election year.
One-fifth of the world’s oil passed through the strait before the war.
Hormuz flashpoint

Despite traffic remaining throttled six months on, Trump has claimed the US navy has “total control” of the strait, with Washington last week announcing it had completed clearing explosives from the waterway.

Iran, however, insists it is in charge of the sea lane. The Revolutionary Guards said Monday that a “rogue” oil tanker caught fire near the strait after it hit two mines while attempting to transit an “illegal route.”
The US military called the claim “disinformation,” saying: “No ships have hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz.”
Mediators have tried for months to broker an end to the war, but an earlier truce and memorandum of understanding fell apart.

Iran recently has been trying to push the US to return to the previous deal, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi telling state TV on Monday that “the solution is completely clear and straightforward: the United States must return to its commitments”.
“In that case, everything can be put back on the right track,” he said. /dl

articles.title: Sotto tells impeach court: Name is fake if there is no person behind it
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III reminded the Senate impeachment court on Tuesday that names could only be considered an alias if there is a person behind it, but…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III reminded the Senate impeachment court on Tuesday that names could only be considered an alias if there is a person behind it, but otherwise, it is fake.

In the last few weeks, as the court tackled Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds, acknowledgement receipts signed by several people with seemingly suspicious names resembling that of famous food brands, fruits, Filipino phrases and even local politicians surfaced.
The signatories included the likes of Mary Grace Piattos, Andy Lim, Miggy Mango, and Kristine Applegate Estrada.
“If there is a person behind the alias, then it is an alias. If there is no person behind the name, it is a fictitious name or a fake name,” Sotto said in a manifestation.
Sotto was citing Republic Act No. 6085, which regulates the use of aliases.

“For the public and for us, the general rule that she mentioned is Republic Act No. 6085, regulating the use of aliases, which only allowed in the Philippines [the use of] pseudonyms, solely for literary, cinema, television and other entertainment purposes,” Sotto noted.

It was counsel for the prosecution Mae Divinagracia who brought up the law on aliases, after Senator-judge Robin Padilla sought to justify the use of aliases by noting that even national heroes used them. /jpv

articles.title: Pilandok intensifies into tropical storm
articles.summary: Pilandok (international name “Krovanh”) intensified into a tropical storm on Tuesday morning, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA).

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 11:26am
Pilandok (international name “Krovanh”) intensified into a tropical storm on Tuesday morning, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA).
In its 11 a.m. tropical cyclone bulletin, PAGASA said Pilandok was located 1,060 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon. Despite its intensification, no tropical cyclone wind signal was in effect.
Pilandok was packing maximum sustained winds of 65 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 80 km/h. It was moving “almost stationary,” the state weather bureau said.
The tropical cyclone is forecast to move slowly east-northeastward over the next 24 hours and is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by Wednesday evening or Thursday morning.
“This tropical cyclone is less likely to make landfall over the country and will remain far from the Philippine landmass,” PAGASA said.
However, the state weather bureau warned of possible effects from the prevailing Southwest Monsoon or Habagat.

The Southwest Monsoon is expected to bring gale-force gusts over most of Luzon and Visayas, as well as Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental from Tuesday to Thursday.
In a separate advisory, PAGASA said it was also monitoring Tropical Storm Saudel (formerly “Obet”) outside the PAR.
Another tropical depression being monitored outside the PAR has weakened into a low-pressure area (LPA) and is not expected to re-intensify.

However, PAGASA said another LPA outside the PAR has a medium chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours. It was located 2,975 kilometers east of southeastern Luzon.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Ex-DOF chief Sonny Dominguez joins Megaworld as lead independent director
articles.summary: Andrew Tan-led top township developer Megaworld Corp. beefs up its board of directors by tapping former Department of Finance (DOF) secretary Carlos “Sonny” G. Dominguez as lead independent director,…

blocks.text: Andrew Tan-led top township developer Megaworld Corp. beefs up its board of directors by tapping former Department of Finance (DOF) secretary Carlos “Sonny” G. Dominguez as lead independent director, bringing his extensive experience in business, finance, corporate leadership, and economic policy.

Dominguez brings more than four decades of experience across the public and private sectors, having held leadership positions in various industries, including banking, power, aviation, agriculture, mining, hospitality, real estate, and investments.
He served as DOF secretary from 2016 to 2022, when he led the agency through major economic and fiscal reforms, while also serving as former president Rodrigo Duterte’s chief economic manager.

Earlier in his public service career, Dominguez served as secretary of the Department of Agriculture (DA) in the late 1980s, following his tenure as secretary of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR).
Before returning to government service, he held senior executive and board positions in several leading Philippine corporations.

His corporate leadership experience included serving as chairman and president of Philippine Airlines (PAL), as well as holding leadership roles in Philippine Associated Smelting and Refining Corp. (PASAR), BPI Agricultural Development Bank, and RCBC Capital Corp., among others.

Dominguez holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics and a Master’s degree in Business Management from Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) and attended the Executive Management Program at Stanford University.

“We are honored to welcome Secretary Sonny Dominguez to Megaworld’s board of directors. Throughout his distinguished career, he has helped shape the country’s economic landscape through principled leadership in government, finance, and business,” said Megaworld Chairman Tan.
Tan added that, “His depth of experience and strategic perspective will be invaluable as the company enters its next chapter of growth.”

Dominguez’s appointment comes as Megaworld continues to expand its presence across key economic and tourism destinations in the Philippines, with its integrated urban townships serving as platforms for business growth, tourism, employment, and community development.

Megaworld said, “The addition of Dominguez to the board also reinforces Megaworld’s commitment to strong corporate governance, board diversity, and independent oversight as the company continues to pursue its long-term growth strategy.”

His appointment further reflects Megaworld’s commitment to ensuring a strong, experienced, and forward-looking board capable of providing strategic guidance as the company continues to grow and create greater value for its shareholders, stakeholders, and the communities it serves across the Philippines.

articles.title: Kanda wins unanimous reelection as ADB president for fresh five-year term
articles.summary: Asian Development Bank (ADB) president Masato Kanda has secured a full five-year term at the helm of the Manila-based multilateral lender after winning unanimous support from its member economies. In…

blocks.text: Asian Development Bank (ADB) president Masato Kanda has secured a full five-year term at the helm of the Manila-based multilateral lender after winning unanimous support from its member economies.
In a statement on Tuesday, Sept. 1, the ADB said members of its board of governors unanimously reelected Kanda in a recently concluded election, with his new term to begin on Nov. 24, 2026.
Kanda was first elected as the ADB’s 11th president on Nov. 27, 2024, and assumed office on Feb. 24, 2025, serving the remaining term of his predecessor, Masatsugu Asakawa.

“I am deeply honored by the trust our members have placed in me at this critical moment in our region’s history. New shocks are striking Asia and the Pacific, even before economies have recovered from the last, and the international order is under its greatest strain in generations,” Kanda said.

“The ADB must be the region’s anchor of stability. But stability cannot mean standing still. We must mobilize with speed and at the scale our members need, to protect people today while helping build a brighter future for the next generation,” Kanda added.
Since Kanda assumed office, the ADB has expanded its financial support to its developing member countries (DMCs) amid what it described as a period of overlapping crises.
In 2025, the ADB provided a record $44 billion in support, comprising more than $29 billion from its own resources and nearly $15 billion in cofinancing.
An amendment to the ADB’s charter also paved the way for a 50-percent increase in the lender’s annual financing capacity, allowing financing from its own resources to exceed $36 billion annually.
Before joining the ADB, Kanda served as special advisor to Japan’s prime minister and finance minister from 2024 to 2025.

He was also Japan’s vice-minister of finance for international affairs from 2021 to 2024 and represented the country in major international forums, including the Group of Seven (G7) and Group of Twenty (G20).

articles.title: Security guard arrested for firing gun in Manila terminal
articles.summary: A 29-year-old security guard was arrested after he was seen firing a gun into the air and causing a disturbance at a bus terminal in Ermita, Manila, on Monday night, Aug. 31. The suspect was…

blocks.text: A 29-year-old security guard was arrested after he was seen firing a gun into the air and causing a disturbance at a bus terminal in Ermita, Manila, on Monday night, Aug. 31.
The suspect was identified as Carlo Marin y Atuel, a resident of Barangay 108, Tondo, Manila.

Police said personnel of the Lawton Police Community Precinct (PCP) were conducting a mobile patrol near the Multimodal Transportation Hub along Arroceros Street, Barangay 659-A, when a concerned citizen approached them and reported the disturbance at around 9:40 p.m.
Responding officers PSSg El-Ar Malonzo and PSSg Randy Quintal proceeded to the area to verify the report.
Upon arrival, police said they saw Marin holding a firearm and instructed him to surrender it. He reportedly complied and was immediately arrested.
Police recovered a Shooter Guardian short firearm with serial number GD903161996, along with a magazine and a spent cartridge believed to have been fired from the weapon.
Marin was unable to present documents authorizing him to possess or own the firearm, according to police.
He was brought to a hospital for a physical examination and underwent a paraffin test to check for possible gunpowder residue on his hands.
Police said Marin was later taken to the Ermita Police Station, where they informed him of his constitutional rights and the nature of the allegations against him. He opted to remain silent.

Authorities are preparing charges for violation of Article 155 of the Revised Penal Code, or Alarm and Scandal, and Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act.
The case will be brought before the Manila Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings.

articles.title: Vacant house collapses in Manila after heavy rains
articles.summary: A two-story wooden structure that had been left vacant collapsed in Sta. Cruz, Manila, on Monday evening, Aug. 31, following heavy rainfall that weakened the already deteriorated building. The…

blocks.text: A two-story wooden house that had been left vacant collapses along Tayuman Street in Barangay 353, Sta. Cruz, Manila following heavy rainfall on Monday evening, Aug. 31. (Photo courtesy of MPD)
A two-story wooden structure that had been left vacant collapsed in Sta. Cruz, Manila, on Monday evening, Aug. 31, following heavy rainfall that weakened the already deteriorated building.
The structure, located at a property along Tayuman Street in Barangay 353, collapsed at around 6:45 p.m., according to the Manila Police District (MPD).
Police identified the owner as 75-year-old Yolanda Lising, a resident of Quezon City.
The building, made of wood and galvanized light materials, was no longer occupied when it collapsed.
Police said the structure had already deteriorated and became weakened and structurally unstable following the previous heavy rainfall.
No one was reported injured in the incident.
The damage was estimated at around P50,000.
During the investigation, Lising reportedly told authorities that the structure had already been scheduled for urgent demolition and renovation.
Barangay 353 officials, led by Barangay Chairwoman Angelina Suansing Gorospe, were also at the site and advised to coordinate with the Manila City Hall Engineering Office for a structural assessment.

articles.title: Tired of playing the same games? TNT and Blacknut bring 1,000+ games to your phone
articles.summary: Let’s be honest: even the most die-hard gamers eventually hit that “What should we play next?” moment. You know the feeling. You’ve played your usual favorites, beaten the same levels, and settled…

blocks.text: Let’s be honest: even the most die-hard gamers eventually hit that “What should we play next?” moment.
You know the feeling. You’ve played your usual favorites, beaten the same levels, and settled the same friendly rivalries with your Katropa more times than you can count.
Sometimes, all you need is a fresh game to make gaming exciting again.
That’s where TNT and Blacknut come in.

The value mobile brand has teamed up with Blacknut to give TNT subscribers access to more than 1,000 premium video games streamed directly from the cloud without the hassle of downloading massive game files or investing in a gaming console.
And because the games are streamed from the cloud, all you need is a TNT-powered smartphone and a reliable connection to jump into a new gaming adventure.
Your next game night is on your phone
KaTropas nationwide can sign up for the Blacknut Cloud Gaming service at Blacknut Smart for as low as P145 per week, charged directly to their prepaid load.
There’s no credit card required. After a quick OTP verification, subscribers can start playing through their mobile browser.
No console. No high-end gaming rig. No waiting around for huge game downloads.
Just pick a game and play.
And with more than 1,000 titles in the library, finding something new to play with your Katropa suddenly becomes a lot easier.
From kitchen chaos to NBA showdowns
The best part? There’s something for practically every kind of gamer.

If your barkada thrives on chaos, Overcooked! & Overcooked! 2 is practically a recipe for disaster and in the best possible way. Players have to prepare, cook, and serve meals while racing against the clock. Between chopping ingredients, washing dishes, and trying not to burn everything, communication with your teammates is key. Expect plenty of laughter, shouting, and the occasional blame game.

Basketball fans can take the rivalry to the virtual court with NBA 2K23. Build your dream team, recreate iconic basketball moments, or challenge your tropa to a one-on-one showdown. With NBA stars and legends in the lineup, it’s an easy choice for settling those “Sino ang mas magaling?” debates.

For a healthy dose of nostalgia, Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl brings familiar cartoon favorites into one fast-paced fighting game. Whether it’s a free-for-all or a team battle, the game offers a fun way to revisit characters many grew up watching except this time, with everyone throwing punches.

Meanwhile, fans of old-school arcade action can revisit the legendary Double Dragon franchise with Double Dragon Gaiden: Rise of the Dragons. The modern take combines classic beat-'em-up action with tag-team gameplay and roguelite mechanics, giving players plenty of enemies to take down and combos to master.
When gaming becomes an adventure
Not every gaming session has to be about beating the highest score.

For those who prefer getting lost in a good story, Assassin’s Creed Unity takes players to revolutionary Paris, where up to four players can team up for co-op missions and heists while exploring the city and uncovering its secrets.

And if post-apocalyptic survival is more your thing, Far Cry New Dawn puts players in a world trying to rebuild after a global catastrophe. Once co-op mode is unlocked, friends can join forces and take on the campaign together because surviving the end of the world is arguably more fun with the whole tropa.
More gaming, more saya
TNT is also giving subscribers more ways to stay connected while gaming with SAYA All 109, which comes with 7GB of open-access data plus 10GB of 5G data.

For gamers, a good connection can make all the difference. TNT subscribers can tap into Smart’s network, which has recently been recognized by Ookla® for Best Mobile Latency and Best Mobile Video Experience.
With cloud gaming eliminating the need for massive downloads and TNT making access to data and gaming more affordable, trying something new no longer has to mean spending big.
So the next time the tropa starts complaining that “wala nang bagong game,” you already know what to do.
Grab your phone, pick a title, and let the gaming begin.

articles.title: Fire volunteer offers free eye checkups every Sunday
articles.summary: A fire volunteer is giving Manila residents, particularly the elderly, a clearer view of their health by offering free eye checkups every Sunday to those experiencing blurred vision, headaches, and…

blocks.text: A resident in Manila undergoes an eye examination during the Sunday free eye checkup program.

A fire volunteer is giving Manila residents, particularly the elderly, a clearer view of their health by offering free eye checkups every Sunday to those experiencing blurred vision, headaches, and other eyesight problems.
The initiative was spearheaded by civic leader and fire volunteer Jason Yu as part of an ongoing dental and medical mission in Manila.
Many of those availing of the service are elderly residents who experience age-related vision problems but may not have the financial means to seek regular eye care.
Yu organized a fundraising campaign to purchase an autorefractor machine and prescription eyeglasses for the program.
The equipment allows the mission to conduct faster and more accurate initial eye examinations, helping identify patients who may need corrective lenses.
Residents who require eyeglasses are also provided with prescription glasses free of charge.
For elderly beneficiaries, the assistance can make everyday activities such as reading, walking, and recognizing people easier, particularly for those who have long struggled with poor vision.
The program also aims to help residents who might otherwise postpone an eye examination because of the cost of consultation and prescription glasses.
The free eye checkups form part of the broader dental and medical mission, which provides basic health services to members of the community.
Through the weekly Sunday service, Yu and the organizers hope to make basic eye care more accessible to residents and encourage those experiencing vision problems to have their eyesight checked.

articles.title: NSW top prosecutor Sally Dowling and state attorney general discussed which barristers could review her office, estimates hears
articles.summary: Sally Dowling tells budget estimates that Michael Daley called to tell her he was appointing a senior counsel and ‘raised quite a number of names’

blocks.text: The top prosecutor in NSW says she discussed a list of barristers to lead an independent review into controversial findings against her office with the state’s attorney general, before he appointed someone she had known “professionally and socially” for nearly 30 years.

Last month, a state parliamentary committee voted 4-3 to find that the New South Wales director of public prosecutions (DPP), Sally Dowling SC, had given false evidence about the pitching of a story about an Indigenous child performing an acknowledgement of country at a sentencing hearing to radio station 2GB.
Dowling admitted her office had pitched the story, but denied she had authorised it. The NSW attorney general, Michael Daley, and the DPP rejected the committee’s findings.

At budget estimates on Monday, Dowling said that she and Daley had spoken before Noel Hutley SC was appointed to lead an independent review which found there was “no positive basis” to find she had given false evidence.
She said Dowling had “called me to tell me that he was appointing a senior counsel to review the evidence that was before the inquiry and its report of the majority”.

“He raised quite a number of [senior counsel’s] names that he was considering, including Mr Hutley’s name, and some of those people did have a conflict, they had acted for the ODPP (Office of The Director of Public Prosecutions), for me, and that was about the extent of the discussion.”
Dowling said Daley had not asked for “advice”. “He mentioned some names, and I responded to those names,” she said.

Dowling said of the list of eight to 12 people, she said two “would not be appropriate”, but she did not raise Hutley as inappropriate as she did not believe there was a conflict of interest. Under further questioning, Dowling said she had indicated to Daley that she knew Hutley, but had not given any further detail.
Dowling, who told estimates she first met Hutley when she came to the bar in 1997, said she knew “most of the senior members of the inner bar after 30 years in Sydney”.

Asked if she and Hutley were friends, she said: “I know him professionally and socially and have utter respect for his professionalism, and if Mr Hutley considered that he had some kind of conflict that meant that he shouldn’t accept that from the attorney general, I have total confidence that he would have informed the attorney general of that.”

Dowling said her signing a statement of support for Hutley’s candidacy for the NSW bar council in 2015 did not give rise to a conflict, saying she was one of 26 other barristers who signed the letter “ten years ago”.

She said none of the names she discussed with Daley were interstate lawyers. Asked if it would have been more appropriate for someone from interstate to write the review, she said: “It’s a matter for the attorney general whom he seeks advice from.”

On Monday morning, Daley told estimates he rejected the suggestion that Dowling and Hutley were friends. He said he had “full and absolute confidence” in Dowling and that Hutley’s review, in which Hutley was assisted by two other barristers, had provided “an objective and expert analysis of [the report’s] shortcomings”.
Hutley and Daley were contacted for comment.

Several areas in Metro Manila continue to record high concentrations of particulate matter (PM) 2.5., with "very unhealthy" and "acutely unhealthy" air quality levels logged on Tuesday, September 1.

According to the latest monitoring by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources - Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) as of 10 a.m., "acutely unhealthy" air quality is recorded in 11 stations in the capital region:

Manila
Marikina (Parang)
Muntinlupa (Filinvest City)
Parañaque (Don Bosco)
Quezon City (Ateneo)
San Juan City
Taguig (TUP)
Valenzuela

blocks.text: Meanwhile, "very unhealthy" air quality is recorded in Makati, Navotas, Pateros, and Quezon City (SMPH Commonwealth).
"The elevated PM2.5 may be associated with smoke and haze from ongoing fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, transported by prevailing winds toward the Philippines," said DENR-EMB in a statement.
The DENR-EMB added that it's been monitoring air quality as well in Central Luzon, Calabarzon, and Mimaropa.

Local government units have also urged the residents to use face mask when going outside. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos wants P4.58-B confidential funds for 2027 — almost half of proposed OP budget
articles.summary: Observing the long-held tradition of parliamentary courtesy, the House appropriations committee approves the proposed budget of the Office of the President

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. delivers his fifth State of the Nation Address at the House of Representatives on July 27, 2026.
RTVM Screengrab
Observing the long-held tradition of parliamentary courtesy, the House appropriations committee approves the proposed budget of the Office of the President

items: Malacañang is requesting a budget of over P10.158 billion for 2027, significantly lower than the 2026 budget due to the previous year's ASEAN chairmanship expenses being allocated under the Office of the President.

The budget includes P4.58 billion for confidential expenses, which has raised concerns among legislators regarding transparency and scrutiny, especially in light of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial.
Despite opposition from some lawmakers, the committee voted to waive questions on the OP budget, allowing for its quick approval with minimal discussion.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang is seeking over P10.158 billion for 2027 — an amount that’s just over a third of its current 2026 budget and over two-thirds of its 2025 budget.

The dramatic drop between 2026 and 2027 is because spending for the Philippines’ chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was lodged under the Office of the President (OP), and is broken down based on the various agencies involved in the preparations related to hosting different meetings and the summits under the regional grouping. The 2025 budget had also included allocations for ASEAN chairmanship preparations.

“We are asking for less while remaining fully prepared to do more,” Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, a former legislator himself, said during the OP’s budget briefing before the House committee on appropriations on Tuesday, September 1.

The OP budget, as usual, was not subjected to scrutiny at the committee level because of the long-standing tradition of extending “institutional and interbranch courtesy” to the OP as a co-equal branch. Scrutiny of the OP’s budget, if any, usually only begins at the plenary level.

House Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers Representative Antonio Tinio pointed out that over half of the OP’s budget, some P4.58 billion, is allocated for confidential expenses. Tinio, and later impeachment spokesperson House Assistant Minority Leader and Representative Renee Co, opposed the observance of parliamentary courtesy, citing public interest in the use of public, including confidential, funds.

Tinio noted that the OP’s confidential funds use should be scrutinized the same way that Vice President Sara Duterte’s past confidential funds use is being scrutinized, both in the public and before the impeachment court.

Within less than 16 minutes after Recto’s briefing, legislators from both the minority and majority voted to waive questions on the OP budget at the committee level, citing parliamentary courtesy. This was after a motion was made to terminate the hearing, with only five panel members voting in the negative.
At 10:29 am, the committee hearing for the OP’s budget officially ended, which means less than an hour had passed between the start of Recto’s briefing and the OP budget’s approval.
But what exactly are Marcos’ priorities for 2027 under his own office?

Based on the National Expenditure Program for 2027, some P4.58 billion is allocated for confidential expenses (P2.25 billion), extraordinary and miscellaneous expenses (P20.77 million), and intelligence expenses (P2.31 billion).
Confidential and intelligence funds (CIF) have been under the spotlight of late, especially in the context of erstwhile Marcos ally Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial.
The proposed OP CIF for 2027 is slightly lower — by a few million pesos — than in 2026.

The OP also wants over P1 billion for local/foreign missions and state visits, the same amount Marcos had asked in recent years. That budget covers both Marcos and his delegations’ trips overseas for official and working visits, and for hosting state visits in the country.

After the vote to terminate the hearing, legislators manifested either their opposition to the waiving of questions or unequivocal support for Marcos and the OP. Panel senior Vice chairperson Bataan 2nd District Representative Albert Garcia assured lawmakers as well as civil society organizations that their queries and concerns would be relayed to the OP by the time the plenary deliberates on its proposed budget. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Senate bill seeks to grant Ombudsman power to arrest, search and seize
articles.summary: Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson has filed a bill seeking to strengthen the Office of the Ombudsman by giving it authority to carry out arrests and detention, searches and seizures in accordance with…

blocks.text: Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson has filed a bill seeking to strengthen the Office of the Ombudsman by giving it authority to carry out arrests and detention, searches and seizures in accordance with the law.

Lacson said he is prepared to expedite its passage in solidarity with the Ombudsman which is struggling to carry out its mandate of probing various graft and corruption cases involving flood control, reclamation and other infrastructure projects.

Senate Bill No. 2394, which he filed last August 12, primarily seeks to give the Ombudsman its own law enforcement arm, by creating the Ombudsman Marshall Service that would conduct proactive inspections, inquiries and investigations to gather evidence and build up cases.

"The bill I filed gives the Ombudsman its own law enforcement arm focusing on graft and corruption cases under the mandate of the Ombudsman, to show my support for their work,” Lacson said in an interview on One News’ Storycon late Monday.
"With the law enforcement arm, it can apply for search warrants and serve arrest warrants to make its job easier,” he further said.

The former Philippine National Police (PNP) chief noted that the Ombudsman currently relies on law enforcement agencies such as the PNP and the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) to assist in serving warrants and carrying out other law enforcement functions.
"The Ombudsman needs its own law enforcement arm. It currently relies on help from the PNP and NBI," he said.

Lacson said he has already coordinated with Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan, chairman of the Senate Committee on Justice and Human Rights where his bill has been referred to, to priotize the hearings and sponsorship of the measure on the floor.
The senator also said he has asked Pangilinan to authorize the creation of a subcommittee and allow him to defend the measure in plenary in order to expedite its enactment into law.
At the same time, Lacson called on the counterpart in the House of Representatives, Rep. Gerville Luistro, head of the House Committee on Justice, to pursue the same measure.

"In order to strengthen the Office of the Ombudsman in the exercise of its power to investigate, it is essential to afford the Office of the Ombudsman the power to effect arrests, detention, searches and seizures in accordance with the performance of its mandate imposed by no less than the Constitution itself,” Lacson said in his bill.
He further said the proposed law enforcement service would make an "immense contribution" to empowering the Office of the Ombudsman in fulfilling its mandate.
Under the bill, Section 15 of RA 6770 or the Ombudsman Act of 1989, shall be amended with a provision creating the Ombudsman Marshall Service.
The service would be headed by a Special Investigator with the rank, salary, emoluments, benefits and retirement privileges of a Deputy Ombudsman.
These Ombudsman Marshalls would be authorized to make arrests and effect detention, searches and seizures and conduct various forms of investigation in accordance with the law.

They may be authorized to carry suitable firearms for their protection in connection with their duties and for the protection of witnesses and persons in custody without need for permit from other government agencies.

Also, under the measure, the Ombudsman Marshall Service may be called upon to enforce any order, writ or process of the Office of the Ombudsman, Sandiganbayan or any anti-corruption court, agency or unit.
Furthermore, the bill provides facilities for persons that the Ombudsman Marshalls will take into custody, including detainees under investigation, whistleblowers and witnesses.
