articles.title: GOSSIP GIRL: Kitkat’s royal journey
articles.summary: When you think of Kitkat, the first things that probably come to mind are comedy and that unmistakable energy that can turn even an ordinary conversation into a punchline. But these days, Kitkat…

blocks.text: Kitkat and her daughter Uno Favia

When you think of Kitkat, the first things that probably come to mind are comedy and that unmistakable energy that can turn even an ordinary conversation into a punchline. But these days, Kitkat Favia has added another title to her growing list: Mrs. Universe Philippines Queen Ambassador 2026. And fittingly, her advocacy is something very close to her heart: breastfeeding and HIV awareness.
Kitkat recently shared with me that she is still breastfeeding her four-year-old daughter, Uno Asher, whom she welcomed with husband Walby Favia in 2022.
When Uno was born, Kitkat famously wrote, “My life is COMPLETE,” thanking God for what she called her greatest blessing. Three years later, motherhood is still very much at the center of her life.
“I am still breastfeeding Uno at four years old,” Kitkat told me, and this time around, it wasn’t a punchline, she was dead serious.

“Breastfeeding is not simply about nutrition. It has become an advocacy for me. I want women to understand that breastfeeding can be a personal choice and that even mothers who have undergone breast augmentation like me can still breastfeed. Our bodies are powerful, ganun ka-magical yung katawan,” the comedy princess turned breastfeeding queen told me.

Perhaps what makes Kitkat’s story particularly interesting is that she refuses to fit into just one box. She is a celebrity. A comedian. A mother. A breastfeeding advocate. A beauty queen ambassador. And, yes, a woman who is perfectly comfortable talking about cosmetic enhancements. This is Kitkat being Kitkat: no filters, except perhaps the ones on Instagram.

blocks.caption: Kitkat Favia

blocks.text: Kitkat Favia
Her daughter, meanwhile, apparently has a say in when the breastfeeding journey ends.
“When she says, ‘Mom, I don’t like this anymore because my classmates are teasing me,’ that's when probably,” Kitkat said.
I couldn’t help but ask her if she ever feels awkward breastfeeding a four-year-old. “No,” she answered simply.

And that confidence perhaps explains why Kitkat is a fitting ambassador for maternal empowerment. She isn’t presenting motherhood as a perfectly polished Instagram photograph. She talks about the realities, the choices, the questions and even the awkward moments.
For now, Kitkat seems happy with the little universe she has created with Uno. From comedy stages to beauty-queen sashes, her biggest role remains the one she clearly treasures most: being a mother.

articles.title: Jury finds Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis guilty in Tupac Shakur murder
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — A jury found Duane “Keffe D” Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, bringing a long-awaited development to a case that has captivated hip-hop fans…

blocks.text: LAS VEGAS (AP) — A jury found Duane “Keffe D” Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, bringing a long-awaited development to a case that has captivated hip-hop fans for nearly three decades.
Davis, 63, was convicted Monday of murder with a deadly weapon. The jury reached its verdict in less than three hours after a weekslong trial in Las Vegas. He faces a possible life sentence.
After the verdict was read, Shakur’s sister, Sekyiwa “Set” Shakur, cried and hugged prosecutors. Davis’ son covered his face with one hand.
Prosecutors argued that Davis obtained a gun and organized the shooting after his nephew was beaten by Shakur and Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight earlier that night.
Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors during closing arguments that Davis “went hunting” for Shakur and Knight and urged them to find him guilty.

Prosecutors said Davis had repeatedly placed himself inside the white Cadillac from which the shots were fired. Although Davis was not accused of pulling the trigger, prosecutors argued that he supplied the gun and directed the younger men in the vehicle.
Davis had acknowledged in interviews and in his 2019 memoir that he was inside the Cadillac and had provided the weapon. However, he never identified himself as the gunman.
Defense attorney Michael Sanft argued that Davis’ public statements were exaggerated stories designed to make money and that there was no physical evidence connecting his client to the shooting.
“They have nothing in this case that says that man was here in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996,” Sanft said during closing arguments.
The case dates back to Sept. 7, 1996, when Shakur was riding in a BMW with Knight near the Las Vegas Strip. A white Cadillac pulled alongside them at a red light and gunfire erupted.
Shakur was struck multiple times and died six days later at age 25. Knight was wounded but survived.
For years, no one was charged in Shakur’s killing. The case gained new momentum after Davis began publicly discussing his involvement and authorities arrested him in 2023.
Prosecutors relied heavily on Davis’ own interviews, statements and memoir, arguing that his accounts consistently placed him in the vehicle and established his role in organizing the attack.
The defense challenged those statements, pointing to disclaimers in Davis’ memoir and arguing that he had changed or embellished his story over the years.

The trial also revisited the gang rivalries surrounding Shakur’s death, including the conflict between the Mob Piru and South Side Compton Crips and their connections to rival record labels Death Row Records and Bad Boy Records.
Shakur’s death came months before the September 1996 murder of fellow rap icon The Notorious B.I.G., a case that remains unsolved.
Davis is the first person convicted in connection with Shakur’s killing.

articles.title: Global lenders unite to strengthen fertilizer supply chains, shield food security
articles.summary: The world’s largest multilateral development banks (MDBs) and international financial institutions (IFIs) are seeking increased investments in fertilizer production, storage, transportation, and…

blocks.text: The world’s largest multilateral development banks (MDBs) and international financial institutions (IFIs) are seeking increased investments in fertilizer production, storage, transportation, and other infrastructure to shield global food security from future supply shocks.

In a joint statement last Monday, Aug. 31, the African Development Bank Group (AfDB), the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the Inter-American Development Bank Group (IDB Group), the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), and the World Bank Group (WBG) committed to developing a coordinated roadmap covering financing, policy dialogue, technical assistance (TA), and private-sector engagement.
The institutions said repeated shocks have exposed structural vulnerabilities in global fertilizer supply chains, disproportionately affecting smallholder farmers and low-income households.
“We, the MDBs, recognize that food security remains one of the world’s most pressing development challenges,” they said.

Beyond ensuring fertilizer availability, they said long-term food security requires improving fertilizer-use efficiency, diversifying nutrient sources, restoring healthy soils and natural capital, and investing in resilient food systems.

The initiative builds on measures undertaken following the 2022 global food crisis, when MDBs and other IFIs implemented the IFI Action Plan to Address Food Insecurity and expanded support for agriculture, food trade, social protection, and resilient food systems.

More recently, discussions among the Group of 20 (G20) economies have emphasized resilient food and fertilizer value chains, while the proposed Group of Seven Plus (G7+) Action Plan on Fertilizer Shocks and Food Systems Resilience has highlighted stronger monitoring, early warning, coordination, and timely financing to address fertilizer-related food security risks.

Against this backdrop, the AfDB, the ADB, the EBRD, the IDB Group, the IFAD, and the WBG expressed readiness to work with G20 members, development partners, and the private sector on a coordinated MDB Roadmap on Strengthening Fertilizer Supply Chains.

“We affirm our readiness to work with G20 members, development partners and the private sector to develop a coordinated MDB Roadmap on Strengthening Fertilizer Supply Chains in line with MDB financing, analytical work, policy dialogue, and technical assistance around a shared agenda to strengthen fertilizer value chains, including through economic corridors that are less vulnerable to future shocks, complementing G20 and G7 efforts,” they said.

Under the proposed roadmap, the institutions aim to increase financing for fertilizer production, upstream production, processing, blending, storage, transportation, and other critical infrastructure while improving market monitoring and ensuring timely access to fertilizers.

They also intend to promote more efficient fertilizer use through soil diagnostics, fertilizer recommendations, precision nutrient management, digital agriculture, farmer advisory services, research, and innovation.
The initiative would also support improved soil and water management, nature-based solutions, resilient value chains, innovative technologies, and private-sector investment.

The institutions committed to continuing support for vulnerable households while improving smallholder farmers’ and agrifood enterprises’ access to financing, inputs, logistics, and markets, particularly for fertilizers.

They also plan to deepen collaboration with governments, international organizations, research institutions, civil society, and the private sector through data and knowledge sharing, evidence-based policy dialogue, and coordinated operational support.

articles.title: UP study: Resort visitors willing to pay P75 to conserve Mt. Makiling
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Visitors to resorts in Calamba City and Los Baños, Laguna, said they were willing to pay about P75 per visit for improved conservation of Mt. Makiling’s groundwater, a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Visitors to resorts in Calamba City and Los Baños, Laguna, said they were willing to pay about P75 per visit for improved conservation of Mt. Makiling’s groundwater, a University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) study found.

If captured through a proposed water user fee, the amount could generate an estimated P159.52 million a year for groundwater conservation, resort water conservation measures and the management of Mt. Makiling, according to the study.

The estimate was based on an online survey of 492 resort visitors, who were asked how much they would be willing to pay under a hypothetical program that required resorts to recycle and treat pool water and support groundwater conservation. The researchers used a contingent valuation method and interval regression to estimate the visitors’ willingness to pay.

The study, “Potential Contribution of Tourism for Groundwater Conservation in Mt. Makiling, the Philippines,” was written by Margaret M. Calderon, Analyn L. Codilan, Jan Joseph V. Dida, Vanessa M. Palma-Torres, Angela Marie S. Alducente and Canesio D. Predo of the UPLB Institute of Renewable Natural Resources, College of Forestry and Natural Resources. It was published in the Philippine Journal of Science, Volume 154, No. 2, in April 2025.
The researchers stressed that P75 is an estimated willingness to pay under a hypothetical scenario, not an existing fee or money currently being collected from resort visitors.
Resort boom puts pressure on groundwater

Mt. Makiling is a dormant volcano and a vital watershed that supplies water for domestic, agricultural and industrial uses. Its hot springs and groundwater have also supported the growth of the resort industry in Calamba and Los Baños.

The study cited an earlier inventory that counted 1,043 resorts in the two areas as of 2020 — 871 in Calamba and 172 in Los Baños. The number of resorts in Calamba alone increased from 193 in 1998 to 466 in 2014, according to earlier research cited in the paper.

blocks.caption: mt. makiling

blocks.text: Graphics by Ed Lustan/Inquirer.net
“The growing number of resorts has naturally led to a surge in tourism,” the researchers wrote.

The expansion of the resort industry has also meant greater use of groundwater. The researchers said many resorts had shifted from naturally flowing hot springs to pumping groundwater for their pools and other uses.
They noted that resorts predominantly use pumped groundwater because it is cheaper than metered water from local water districts, which charge based on the volume consumed.

The paper also cited an earlier survey that found resort pools had an average size of 80 cubic meters, with water temperatures ranging from above 30 C to 50 C. The researchers said drained pool water eventually reaches Laguna de Bay and pointed to the need to regulate and monitor its disposal.
Many visitors did not know where the water came from
Despite using resort pools supplied by groundwater or hot springs, many respondents were unsure about the source of the water.

Of the 492 respondents, 52.6% said they knew the source of the resort’s water. Among those who identified a source, 26.2% said hot springs, 14.8% identified Mt. Makiling and only 7.3% identified groundwater.
The researchers also found that 40.7% correctly identified pumping as the way pools were filled, while 34.1% believed the water flowed naturally.
“A notable finding was that while 40.7% of respondents correctly identified pumping as the method for filling the pools, 34.1% mistakenly believed the water flowed naturally,” they wrote.
The paper said this was significant because resorts in the area have increasingly relied on pumped groundwater rather than naturally flowing hot springs.

blocks.caption: mt. makiling

blocks.text: Awareness was stronger when it came to the role of forests in maintaining groundwater. Some 98.4% of respondents agreed that good forest cover was important to securing groundwater supply, while 66.7% knew that groundwater was not unlimited.
Still, 33% believed groundwater was unlimited regardless of how much water was used, the researchers found.
The researchers described this as “disturbing,” noting that the findings “may imply a need to improve citizens’ understanding of water scarcity.”
Relaxation draws visitors to resorts

For most respondents, resort visits were primarily for recreation. The most common reason was relaxation or enjoyment, followed by the accessibility of resorts for family and friends and their affordability.

“The main reasons of the respondents for visiting the resorts in Los Baños or Calamba are for relaxation (53%), to be with family and friends (39.6%), and because of the resorts’ accessibility (40%) and affordability (37.2%),” the researchers said.

“About a fourth of the respondents went because they heard positive reviews either of a specific resort (28.3%) or the resorts in Los Baños and Calamba in general (27.4%) and for therapeutic or health reasons because of the perceived therapeutic properties of the hot water common in the pools (25%),” they added.

blocks.caption: mt. makiling

blocks.text: PROTECTING MT. MAKILING’S GROUNDWATER Mt. Makiling’s forests and groundwater help sustain the resort industry in Calamba and Los Baños, Laguna. A University of the Philippines Los Baños study found that resort visitors were willing to pay an estimated P75 per visit for improved groundwater conservation, potentially generating P159.52 million a year if captured through a proposed water user fee. —PHOTO COURTESY OF MAKILING CENTER FOR MOUNTAIN ECOSYSTEMS

The study also found that 81.7% of respondents were repeat visitors, having visited resorts in the area at least twice. Social media and recommendations from family and friends were among the main ways they learned about resorts.

The researchers said the findings showed that the resort industry was not simply providing recreational services but was also drawing visitors who depended on the natural water resources associated with Mt. Makiling.
Willingness to pay P75 fee

The researchers used contingent valuation, a survey method that estimates how much people are willing to pay for an environmental resource or improvement that does not have a conventional market price.

In the hypothetical scenario presented to respondents, local governments would require resorts to reuse and treat pool water rather than routinely replace it. An additional water user fee would be added to existing resort entrance fees.
Under the proposed arrangement, half of the fee would be used to maintain pool water quality, while the other half would go toward the conservation of Mt. Makiling.
Respondents were presented with payment amounts ranging from zero to more than P200 per visit.

blocks.caption: mt. makiling

blocks.text: Of the 492 respondents, 488 selected an amount greater than zero. The most common choices were P50, selected by 25%, and P100, selected by 25.81%. Another 11.2% chose P20, while 8.1% selected P200.
Only four respondents, or 0.81%, indicated zero willingness to pay.
“The mean [willingness to pay] estimated using the payment card format was P75 [per] visit,” the researchers wrote.

The P75 figure was calculated using interval regression based on the payment amounts selected by respondents. The researchers cautioned that the result represents stated preference rather than actual behavior or a guaranteed amount of revenue.

“Stated preference techniques may be used when it is not possible to infer or observe people’s [willingness to pay] from markets or when markets are absent, as in the case of the groundwater resource of Mt. Makiling,” the study noted.
Conservation was the main reason to pay
The researchers found that the strongest motivation for willingness to pay was concern about Mt. Makiling’s groundwater.
Among respondents who were willing to pay, 82.2% said they wanted to contribute to groundwater conservation on Mt. Makiling, while 52.3% cited the belief that groundwater is a finite resource.
The researchers said only 28.2% cited the perception that current resort water use was wasteful as a reason for their willingness to pay.

“Most respondents were willing to pay, primarily because they wanted to support the conservation of Mt. Makiling’s groundwater resources and recognized its limited availability,” the researchers wrote.
The survey also found broad support for the conservation measures presented in the hypothetical scenario.

blocks.caption: mt. makiling

blocks.text: About 84% agreed or completely agreed that conserving Mt. Makiling would enhance groundwater supply, while 78% agreed or completely agreed that recycling pool water would help conserve groundwater.
About 75% agreed or completely agreed that the proposed groundwater conservation program was plausible.
“For all three questions, there were more respondents who completely agreed than only agreed,” the researchers observed.

The four respondents who indicated zero willingness to pay gave different reasons. Two did not believe groundwater was limited, one cited affordability, and another said visitors “should not be responsible for paying for pool water recycling.”
The researchers said these responses showed that willingness to pay was influenced not only by environmental concerns but also by how visitors viewed the proposed fee and its affordability.
Potential P159.5 million a year
To estimate how much could potentially be raised, the researchers multiplied the P75 mean willingness to pay by average annual resort visitor numbers in the two cities.

For Calamba, they used an average of 2,015,124 resort visitors a year, based on visitor figures from 2013, 2014 and 2018. For Los Baños, they used an average of 111,821 visitors annually, based on available figures from 2013, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2019.
This produced an estimated P151.13 million in annual potential revenue for Calamba and P8.39 million for Los Baños, or P159.52 million combined.

blocks.caption: mt. makiling

blocks.text: The researchers estimated that, assuming the annual benefits remained constant, the amount would have a present value of P1.358 billion over 20 years at a 10% discount rate.
“This present value can be used to decide policy options that will contribute to the conservation of Mt. Makiling’s groundwater resource,” the researchers said.

Under the hypothetical fee arrangement used in the survey, half of the estimated annual revenue — or P79.76 million — could be allocated to improved management of Mt. Makiling, while the same amount could support water conservation practices among resorts.

“These funds could support the enhanced management of Mt. Makiling and help resorts implement water conservation measures while maintaining pool water quality at international standards, reducing unnecessary and excessive water disposal,” the researchers stressed.
Visitors favored frequent water replacement
The survey also asked respondents how often they believed resort pools should be emptied and refilled.

Among visitors to public resorts, 45.5% believed pool water was changed daily, while 38.4% thought it was changed weekly. Among private-resort visitors, 42.5% believed water was changed daily and 19.3% thought it was changed every 12 hours.

When asked how frequently water should ideally be replaced, 27% of public-resort visitors preferred replacement before every group’s use, while 39% preferred daily replacement. Among private-resort visitors, 46.5% preferred changing water before each group and 23% preferred daily replacement.

blocks.caption: mt. makiling

blocks.text: The study also found a gap in visitors’ knowledge about pool water treatment.
Only 23.4% knew that properly maintained and monitored pool water could remain in use for years without annual replacement, while 76.6% did not know this.
At the same time, 67.9% said they would be less satisfied if they learned that pool water had not been changed for two years, even if it had been properly treated and maintained.
“This points to the need for information dissemination about safe pool water standards,” the study noted.
Age, water-saving habits also mattered
The study also examined factors associated with respondents’ willingness to pay.
Its model found that age and water-conserving behavior were significant predictors. The researchers estimated that willingness to pay decreased by P0.802 for every additional year of age.

blocks.caption: mt. makiling

blocks.text: Meanwhile, respondents who consistently practiced water conservation also had an estimated P27.23 lower willingness to pay than those who did not consistently practice water conservation.

“Interestingly, respondents who do not consistently practice water conservation demonstrated a higher WTP. Conversely, those who already engage in water-conserving behaviors showed a lower WTP, possibly reflecting costs they have already absorbed for their current practices,” the researchers stated.
Researchers urge policy, public education

The researchers recommended that local governments consider policies that would capture visitors’ stated willingness to pay and use the resulting funds for Mt. Makiling management and resort water conservation measures.

The researchers also called for stronger information and education efforts among resort owners, visitors, the public, and local and national government officials to raise awareness of growing groundwater scarcity in Mt. Makiling and other parts of the country.
“Additionally, resort owners should be informed about the importance of proper pool maintenance to minimize frequent and unnecessary water replacement,” the study noted.
“In contrast, resort visitors should be educated on how pool water can meet international quality standards without excessive water use,” it added.

articles.title: Sandiganbayan defers Tarlac solon’s arraignment until Oct. 7
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division on Tuesday moved the arraignment of Tarlac Rep. Noel Rivera to October 7 in light of his motion to consolidate the cases against him. Rivera,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division on Tuesday moved the arraignment of Tarlac Rep. Noel Rivera to October 7 in light of his motion to consolidate the cases against him.

Rivera, who represents the third district of Tarlac province, faces nine counts of violating Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act before the Sandiganbayan, two of which were raffled to the court’s Fifth Division.

At the hearing on Tuesday, Sandiganbayan Fifth Division Chairperson Associate Justice Zaldy Trespeses noted the motions for consolidation and to quash the information filed by Rivera through his legal counsel on August 11 and 24, respectively.
“The arraignment is deferred, considering [the] pendency of the motion for consolidation and the motion to quash filed by the accused in both cases,” Trespeses said.
He also acknowledged the omnibus consolidated comment-opposition filed by state prosecutors on August 28 in response to Rivera’s motions.
“The same are now submitted for resolution,” Trespeses noted.

The charges against Rivera stem from his and his wife’s alleged shareholdings in Tarlac 3-G Construction and Development Corporation, which obtained nine government infrastructure contracts during his term in office from 2022 to 2025.

State prosecutors indicted Rivera for violating Section 3(h) of RA No. 3019, which prohibits “directly or indirectly having financing or pecuniary interest in any business, contract or transaction in connection with which he intervenes or takes part in his official capacity, or in which he is prohibited by the Constitution or by any law from having any interest.”
Last Thursday, the Sandiganbayan Sixth Division, which also handles two of Rivera’s cases, denied his move to consolidate the nine counts of graft to a single court division.
The Sixth Division agreed with the prosecution’s argument that consolidating the cases “will only result in the muddling of facts and issues, which may cause confusion and delay.” /jpv

articles.title: Indonesia fire-linked haze affects Metro Manila air quality
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Some cities in Metro Manila reached “very unhealthy” to “acutely unhealthy” levels of air quality on Tuesday morning due to haze possibly linked to ongoing fires in Kalimantan,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Some cities in Metro Manila reached “very unhealthy” to “acutely unhealthy” levels of air quality on Tuesday morning due to haze possibly linked to ongoing fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, according to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB).

In its data as of 6 a.m., the DENR-EMB in the National Capital Region (NCR) said several areas recorded high PM2.5 levels. PM2.5 refers to fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometers or less in diameter.

The DENR-EMB in the NCR said that the following areas logged acutely unhealthy air quality index (AQI). Under this level, the bureau said that the AQI ranges from 201 to 300 where everyone may be noticeably affected and outdoor activities must be restricted:

items: Parañaque (296 AQI)
Quezon City (Ateneo) (241 AQI)
Las Piñas (237 AQI)
Manila (231 AQI)
Malabon City (229 AQI)
Taguig (224 AQI)
Valenzuela (224 AQI)
Marikina (Parang) (217 AQI)
Muntinlupa (Filinvest) (216 AQI)
San Juan City (213 AQI)
Mandaluyong (207 AQI)

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Navotas and Pateros reached very unhealthy air quality, where their AQI stood at 153 and 172, respectively. Under this level, AQI ranges from 151 to 200 with the bureau warning that those with heart and lung conditions may worsen.

Makati reported an AQI of 111, which is equivalent to unhealthy air quality for sensitive groups. The bureau advised of limiting outdoor activities as there is a risk of difficulty in breathing for everyone, especially for sensitive groups.
Only Quezon City (SMPH Commonwealth) logged fair AQI (98), where sensitive individuals should still avoid outdoor exposure.

The bureau advised the public to wear masks, particularly N95 masks, especially if you need to go outside. It then encouraged the public to limit outdoor activities, especially those who are sensitive to air pollution. /jpv

articles.title: 3 minors held over bookkeeper’s death in QC hotel
articles.summary: Three minors were taken into custody after a 57‑year‑old freelance bookkeeper was found strangled inside the bathroom of his Quezon City hotel room on Aug. 26. The victim was discovered around 11:20…

blocks.text: The 57-year-old victim was found lifeless inside the bathroom of his hotel room in Quezon City. (Photo courtesy of the QCPD CIDU)
Three minors were taken into custody after a 57‑year‑old freelance bookkeeper was found strangled inside the bathroom of his Quezon City hotel room on Aug. 26.
The victim was discovered around 11:20 a.m. at a hotel on Timog Avenue in Barangay Sacred Heart after an employee, who had gone to clean the room, received no response despite repeated knocks.
The staff sought help from the front desk, prompting personnel to open the room where the victim was found dead, his belongings in disarray and blood scattered inside.
A Scene of the Crime Operatives (SOCO) examination showed he died of asphyxia due to strangulation.
QCPD‑CIDU acting chief P/Maj. Errol Frejas said the victim appeared to have been struck on the head with a bottle before a pillow was pressed over his face.
The victim, who was from Mindanao, had traveled to Metro Manila to process work-related documents and booked the hotel room for eight days starting Aug. 18.
Police reviewing CCTV footage found that he was last seen alive on Aug. 23 with three male children.
Two of the minors were seen with the victim during the morning and afternoon, while the third was later fetched by one of the minors.
At about 9:15 p.m., the three were seen leaving the hotel together while carrying backpacks and the victim’s personal belongings.
Frejas said the victim met the minors through a social media app and arranged to meet them for drinks while he was in Manila.
Police said robbery was the primary motive behind the killing.
The minors allegedly took three cellphones, a wristwatch, identification cards, debit and credit cards, and two passbooks belonging to the victim.
They allegedly withdrew about P150,000 using his ATM card and made purchases worth nearly P40,000 using his credit card.
A cellphone recovered from the crime scene helped investigators track the minors.
With the consent of the victim’s wife, investigators accessed the device and found that it was synchronized with other phones allegedly being used by the suspects.
Photos taken by the minors and other information from the device helped police trace the stolen phones and establish their whereabouts.
Police also traced a transport network vehicle service (TNVS) driver allegedly hired by the minors. The driver cooperated with authorities and helped investigators locate them.

CIDU and Kamuning Police Station 10 personnel conducted a hot-pursuit operation that led to the protective custody of two suspects, aged 16 and 17, at about 6:50 p.m. on Aug. 29 in Barangay Segunda Pulo, Lumban, Laguna.
Through coordination with the Tanauan City Police Station, a third suspect, 16, was placed under protective custody at about 11:55 p.m. the same day in Trapiche 3, Tanauan City, Batangas.
Police recovered several items believed to belong to the victim, including cellphones, a wristwatch, a black pouch, and bank and credit cards issued in his name.
The three CICLs were informed of their constitutional rights and placed under protective custody in accordance with laws governing children in conflict with the law.
They were later turned over to the Quezon City Social Services Development Department for discernment assessment and appropriate intervention.
Frejas said the three minors obtained above-average results in their discernment assessment, indicating that they could distinguish right from wrong.
The three face complaints for robbery with homicide, which will be referred to the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office for appropriate proceedings.
Police have informed the victim’s children of his death, while relatives are expected to bring his remains back to Mindanao.

articles.title: Jessy Mendiola, Luis Manzano on parenthood, ‘bikini boundaries’
articles.summary: Parenthood has apparently changed the way Jessy Mendiola and Luis Manzano look at bikini photos on social media. Jessy revealed that she has toned down her own bikini and swimsuit posts since…

blocks.text: Parenthood has apparently changed the way Jessy Mendiola and Luis Manzano look at bikini photos on social media.
Jessy revealed that she has toned down her own bikini and swimsuit posts since becoming Luis’ wife and the mother of their daughter.
The actress talked about the change during Luis’ latest vlog, saying she now wants to set a good example for their child.
“I don’t know if people have noticed, dati kasi, ‘di ba, ako rin naman, nagpo-post ng mga bikini, ng mga swimsuit, ganyan-ganyan, or ng mga sexy posts.
“But ever since I became a wife and a mother, I kind of toned it down a bit,” Jessy said.
She stressed that she has nothing against women who post sexy photos. For her, however, becoming a mother made her want to establish certain boundaries for herself.
“I mean, I still appreciate others na ginagawa ‘yon. I have nothing against it. But personally, as a mom, I want to be a good role model for my daughter,” she said.
Jessy also noticed that Luis had made a similar adjustment.
She recalled how, when they were still dating, she would wonder why her then-boyfriend followed so many women who posted bikini photos.
“Dati talaga, nagugulat ako, ‘Bakit ang daming pina-follow nito na naka-bikini?’” Jessy recalled.
Apparently, Luis eventually came to the same conclusion after they got married.
“Na-realize niya na hindi na rin siya appropriate ngayon, kasi nga mag-asawa na kami,” she said.
Jessy made clear, many of the women Luis followed were his actual friends.
His solution? Mute the accounts of those who frequently post sexy content.
“Sinasabi niya sa ‘kin, ‘Imu-mute ko na lang ‘yung mga ka-close ko na mahilig mag-post ng sexy,’” she shared.
Jessy said the arrangement works for them because it gives them boundaries they both feel are appropriate for their marriage.
“Nandu’n na rin ‘yung boundaries kumbaga,” she said.
It is quite the change for the couple.
Jessy used to post the bikini photos. Luis used to follow them. Then they got married, became parents and suddenly, bikini content came with rules.
For Jessy, the shift is about being a role model for their daughter.
For Luis, apparently, there is always the mute button.

articles.title: Thirty years of waiting, a memoir and a trial: conviction in Tupac Shakur killing brings closure
articles.summary: A Las Vegas jury on Monday found Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis guilty in the 1996 murder of the hip-hop icon

blocks.text: Thirty years after the killing of Tupac Shakur, conspiracy theories and rumors about the perpetrator’s identity, one man has now been held criminally responsible for the rap icon’s death.

A Las Vegas jury convicted Duane “Keffe D” Davis, a 63-year-old former South Side Compton Crips gang leader, of murder for his role in the drive-by shooting. During the two-week long trial, prosecutors argued Davis was the “on-the-ground, on-site commander of the effort to kill Tupac” and had sought revenge after the musician was involved in a fight with his nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson.
The conviction brings long-awaited resolution to the case, which has captured public attention and dominated headlines for decades.
“We’ve been waiting 30 years to grieve properly,” Zayd Akinyela, Shakur’s cousin, told reporters outside the courtroom when the trial was under way.

Shakur, the son of members of the Black Panther party was at the height of his career in 1996. The rapper had released the hit album All Eyez on Me, which sold millions of copies, and had become a global superstar.

In September 1996, he was in Las Vegas attending a Mike Tyson fight at the MGM Grand hotel. While heading to an afterparty that evening, he was attacked just off the Las Vegas strip alongside Marion “Suge” Knight, the founder of Death Row Records. As they waited at a red light, a Cadillac pulled up next to Shakur’s vehicle and shot him multiple times. Shakur died days later, at age 25.

Shakur’s death, at a young age and an ascendant point in his cultural power, turned him into an almost saint-like figure within hip-hop. A flood of posthumous songs, music videos and albums were released after the murder, eulogizing his legacy as one of the most prolific and talented artists of his generation.
Diss tracks, gang rivalries and a shooting

There were no arrests made in his killing and Las Vegas police faced criticism that the department had bungled the investigation and failed to pursue crucial leads. Questions and conspiracy theories persisted for decades, but few official answers.

The killing was for years viewed as connected to the east coast-west coast rivalry between different hip-hop groups and record labels. Shakur had a longstanding feud with Christopher Wallace, a Brooklyn rapper, better known as Biggie Smalls or The Notorious B.I.G., that had involved numerous diss tracks and threats between their camps. Wallace was murdered in Los Angeles less than six months after Shakur’s killing, adding to the lore around the feud.

Both Shakur and Biggie quickly became pop culture icons representing a golden era of 90s hip-hop. The unsolved nature of their deaths also created a cottage industry of books and documentaries claiming to uncover the real story of their deaths, many of which involved conspiracy theories and allegations of cover-ups.
Authorities say a clearer picture of what unfolded that September evening emerged in recent years thanks to Davis himself.

blocks.caption: Biggie and Tupac. Photograph: Film Four/Lafayette/Kobal/REX/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Davis, a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips gang, had long been known to investigators. He was the only living witness from the car that fired shots at Shakur. Detectives had also Davis to talk about the fatal shooting of the Notorious B.I.G. Though Davis was briefly a suspect, he was later ruled out by investigators.

During the weeks-long trial, jurors heard a 2008 interview where Davis told detectives that Anderson, who died in an unrelated 1998 shooting, fired the shots that killed Shakur. But prosecutors never gathered enough evidence to press charges.
The case took a turn when Davis published his memoir in 2019. In it, he described his involvement in the hit.

blocks.caption: Duane Davis and his attorney Michael Sanft in the courtroom in Las Vegas. Photograph: Bizuayehu Tesfaye/Pool Las Vegas Review-Journal/AP

blocks.text: According to Davis’s account, he was angry about the attack on his nephew and obtained a gun with the intent to “hunt down” Shakur and confront Knight. He and others, including his nephew Anderson, went searching for the group, and once they found them the incident unfolded quickly.

“No words were exchanged, the time for talking had passed, the shit was on! Tupac made an erratic move and began to reach down beneath his seat. It was the first and only time in my life that I could relate to the police command to, ‘Keep your hands where I can see them.’ Instead, Pac pulled out a strap, and that’s when the fireworks started. One of my guys from the back seat grabbed the Glock and started bustin’ back,” he wrote.
It was Davis decision to write the book that ultimately led to the trial, prosecutors said.
“Had he decided to never write the book, he would not, probably, have ever been prosecuted for the crime,” prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo said.
Davis’ defense unsuccessfully sought to have the memoir excluded from the trial, and said that it had been exaggerated to “falsely place [Davis] at the center of it all for personal gain”.

Over the course of the trial, defense attorney Michael Sanft argued that investigators had very little evidence to prove their case. He said that authorities, including the FBI, did not follow up with Davis because they did not believe what he said was credible.
“What they are telling you, they are representing as fact, when it’s really fiction,” said Sanft.
On Monday, a Las Vegas jury disagreed. The judge has set sentencing for 13 October.

articles.title: Remote Grand Canyon lodge hit by deadly flash flood boasts fabled history
articles.summary: Phantom Ranch, set up by Teddy Roosevelt, has welcomed exhausted hikers to its famed cabins for over a century

blocks.text: Phantom Ranch has been a solitary refuge visited by some of the most famous names of history. More typically, it’s been a beacon for the half-collapsed, exhausted and overheated hikers trudging down the Grand Canyon for more than a century.

The sole lodge at the very bottom of the Grand Canyon, the cabins long had a near mythical reputation. Located along the Bright Angel Creek, which tumbles into the mighty Colorado River at the base of the canyon, they served as a reminder of the long history of one of America’s most spectacular but savage environments.
It’s unclear yet how much damage the lodge has sustained after Saturday’s lethal flash flood.

On Saturday afternoon, more than 60 people had to be evacuated by air from the ranch and the bottom of the adjacent North Kaibab Trail, which winds 14 miles down from the lesser-trodden North Rim of the canyon. Two people were confirmed dead, nearly 80 people were rescued and one person remained unaccounted for.

Native Americans have made their home in various parts of the canyon for thousands of years and were driven out of much – though not all – of it before US president Theodore Roosevelt declared the canyon a national monument in 1908. It was Roosevelt who set up a camp on the site where the little visitor lodge now stands, while he was on a hunting trip in 1913. The area became a national park in 1919 and the ranch, named after one of the many side canyons within the Grand Canyon, opened in 1922.
Boaters floating and paddling down the Colorado River stay there, as do people riding mules. The future King Gustaf VI Adolf of Sweden was a prominent early guest, arriving via mule, in 1926.

In 1967, then senator Robert F Kennedy stayed at Phantom Ranch beneath the towering canyon walls after rafting down the Colorado with family and friends, bouncing and gliding 90 miles on the east-west flow of the river from Lake Powell.

Today, more than a vertical mile above, the hundreds of thousands of visitors who just peep over the South Rim, where lodges, tourist information spots, shops and restaurants buzz, cannot see the river, let alone the tiny ranch so far below.

But hikers who trek down the seven or eight zig-zag miles of the nearby dusty South Kaibab or Bright Angel trails to the bottom and cross footbridges over the Colorado to reach the ranch descend steadily from tourist hullabaloo into an ever more rugged and tranquil wilderness. Here, heat, thirst or flood are the biggest dangers, not the resident mountain lions, rattlesnakes or scorpions.

Having pounded the hard rock paths and rough steps all the way down, the few who get to stay at the ranch or snag a campsite along the creek are mostly thinking of the relief of not having to climb back up to the rim yet and the magic of cooling their throbbing feet in a stream before a simple canteen meal at communal tables and a rudimentary bed for a night or two.

But that sense of safety can be as elusively spectral as the name of the refuge. A fast and fierce deluge, such as occurred at the weekend, can quickly form a roaring flash flood when the rain swells creeks that drop steeply into the canyon as tributaries to the Colorado, which is what just happened in the Bright Angel Creek.

The National Park Service describes flash flooding as an inherent risk in the canyon but had additionally warned in February of “the elevated potential for flash flooding and debris flows in the Bright Angel Creek watershed” following the Dragon Bravo wildfire that decimated parts of the North Rim last year and forced the closure of the North Kaibab trail from July to March of this year.

articles.title: How intense rains in the Grand Canyon turned into a deadly disaster
articles.summary: Flash flooding in Arizona tourist destination was likely triggered by compounding climate factors, such as drought and warming in Pacific Ocean

blocks.text: A deadly flash flood in the Grand Canyon over the weekend was likely driven by a confluence of climate factors, including drought, wildfire scarring and warming temperatures in the Pacific Ocean that can supercharge storms.

At least two people have died, nearly 80 people were rescued and one remained unaccounted for after a surge of water and debris swept through the immensely popular tourist destination on Saturday, fueled by torrents of rain that hit the national park’s Bright Angel Creek area.

Flash floods are not uncommon in the region, especially during the monsoon season from June to September, when strong rains pummel the arid landscapes and can quickly fill narrow rock formations. Visiting the Grand Canyon – a crown jewel of the US national park system – can be particularly dangerous in the summer because of the risk of flash flooding, when clear days can give way quickly to thunderstorms and downpours.
The steep, rocky nature of the canyon itself funnels water rapidly, transforming downpours into a charging wall of water.

blocks.caption: This handout image released by the National Park Service shows a storm system moving across the North Rim of Grand Canyon national park on 29 August. Photograph: J Baird/National Park Service/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: But Saturday’s strong storm also hit part of the burn scar of the Dragon Bravo wildfire, a destructive and fast-moving blaze that swept across nearly 150,000 acres (60,700 hectares) and consumed the historic Grand Canyon Lodge in July 2025.
Runoff tends to flow more quickly in the aftermath of a fire, especially in hotter burns where slopes are left barren of vegetation.

While it’s still unclear how directly long-term damage to the landscape from that fire played a role in last weekend’s disaster, federal models indicated a rise in the risks of debris flows in Bright Angel Creek.

blocks.caption: Floods sweeping through Grand Canyon national park

blocks.text: Teams with the Department of Interior charged to assess post-fire threats to “life, property, and critical natural and cultural resources”, found runoff risks would be between two and eight times greater upstream of Phantom Creek. “Hikers on the trails within or downslope from the burned area will experience frequent stabilization issues, especially hazardous rockfall for at least the first year,” the team wrote in a report on conditions.

Park officials were reportedly concerned at the start of this summer that stronger storms could create dangerous conditions near the burned areas. Hikers that had to be evacuated by helicopter after the rushing waters swallowed bridges and other infrastructure told the Arizona Republic that the creek turned black as it filled with runoff.

blocks.caption: This handout image released by the Grand Canyon National Park Service shows remnants of stone bridge pylons along Bright Angel Creek following a flash flood. Photograph: J Thompson, handout/National Park Service/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Scientists have long warned that the climate crisis will create stronger extremes and destructive shifts between wet and dry conditions. As temperatures continue to climb, extreme events will not just increase – they are more likely to overlap, causing more calamity and testing the limits of the nation’s resilience and recovery.
So-called “compound extremes”, where a combination of contributing factors come together, are on the rise, according to researchers.

blocks.caption: The sudden, heavy rainstorm that fueled this catastrophic flood may have been been supercharged by the historic El Niño. Photograph: J Thompson, handout/National Park Service/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Along with the potential impact from a previous fire, a severe drought that continues to affect the Grand Canyon region – and the Colorado River basin that runs through it – could have contributed to the disaster. The deluge unleashed torrents of rain on hardened and sparsely vegetated steep terrain that is less able to absorb and contain abrupt increases in moisture.
The sudden and strong rainstorm that fueled this catastrophic flood may have been been supercharged by the historic El Niño that has sharply increased sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean.

blocks.caption: The Grand Canyon national park in northern Arizona on Sunday, a day after it was hit by heavy flooding. Photograph: Craig Sanderson via AP

blocks.text: The climate phenomenon has the ability to affect weather systems around the world. But in the south-west, the higher amount of water vapor in the atmosphere due to El Niño is wrung out in the form of rainfall, Park Williams, a hydroclimatologist at the University of California, Los Angeles, told the Associated Press.

El Niño is part of a natural cycle, but models show there is a strong likelihood this will become one of the strongest on record. It layers on top of spikes in temperature fueled by the climate crisis. Together, the possibility of severe and extreme weather is expected to dramatically increase.

blocks.caption: Bright Angel Canyon, the scene of flash floods, runs into the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon on Monday. Photograph: John Locher/AP

blocks.text: The link to human-caused climate change and the heavy Arizona rain is moderately strong, said Daniel Swain, a climate scientist at the California Institute for Water Resources.

Swain and colleagues recently published a study in the journal Weather and Climate Extremes finding that during the summer, short-term intense downpours in the US west – akin to the one that hit the Grand Canyon – have become 10% stronger since 2000.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: AFP: Chinese vessels spotted in West Philippine Sea increased to 56 in August 2026
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said a total of 56 Chinese vessels have been monitored in some West Philippine Sea (WPS) features in August 2026.

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 9:52am
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said a total of 56 Chinese vessels have been monitored in some West Philippine Sea (WPS) features in August 2026.
This was higher compared to the 48 Chinese ships seen in the disputed area in July 2026.

In an update, AFP spokesperson for the WPS Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) and China Coast Guard (CCG) vessels were seen in WPS features from August 1 to 31:
• Ayungin Shoal – 18 Chinese vessels (17 CCGs, one PLAN)
• Bajo de Masinloc – 23 (14 CCGs, nine PLANs)
• Escoda Shoal – nine (five CCGs, four PLANs)
• Pag-asa Islands – six (five CCGs, one PLAN)

Tensions continue as Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea, a conduit for more than $3 trillion of annual shipborne commerce, including parts claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
Parts of the South China Sea that fall within Philippine territory have been renamed by the government as West Philippine Sea to reinforce the country’s claim.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago, including the Luzon Sea and the waters around, within, and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
China has refused to recognize the decision. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: LizDon, anyone? Donny Pangilinan-Liza Soberano sightings spark fan frenzy
articles.summary: Two sightings. Two days. And, naturally, enough material for fans to start making theories. Liza Soberano and Donny Pangilinan have been getting attention online after being spotted together on…

blocks.text: Two sightings. Two days. And, naturally, enough material for fans to start making theories.

Liza Soberano and Donny Pangilinan have been getting attention online after being spotted together on consecutive days, prompting fans to wonder if there is more to their increasingly interesting proximity.
Donny was among the celebrities who attended the advance screening of Liza’s DreamWorks animated film “Forgotten Island” at SM Mall of Asia on Tuesday.
The following day, Liza was spotted at Analog MNL, Donny’s soon-to-open restobar.
Liza was with Anne Curtis, Isabelle Daza, Solenn Heussaff, Liz Uy and Georgina Wilson, who were also invited to check out the new restaurant.
Still, try telling that to the internet.
Some fans were quick to ship Liza and Donny, while others were already sulking on behalf of Belle Mariano, Donny’s popular on-screen partner.
There were also those reminding everyone that Liza is reportedly in a relationship and that her visit to Donny’s restaurant was simply part of a celebrity gathering.
So for now, two sightings remain just that: two sightings.
But apparently, that was more than enough for fans to start asking if LizDon could be the next big screen pairing.

articles.title: 'Sa korte na mag-usap': HPG files case vs 2 Customs personnel over Bulacan raid
articles.summary: Just when everyone thought it’s over, the police’s Highway Patrol Group fought back and brought the entire issue of the smuggled cigarette raid in Bulacan to the legal forum. On Aug. 28, the HPG…

blocks.text: Just when everyone thought it’s over, the police’s Highway Patrol Group fought back and brought the entire issue of the smuggled cigarette raid in Bulacan to the legal forum.

On Aug. 28, the HPG filed a criminal case against two personnel of the Bureau of Customs (BOC) for their alleged involvement in selling smuggled cigarettes that were supposed to be destroyed in Bulacan.

In the charge sheet filed before a Bulacan prosecutor’s office, a police corporal who acted as the complainant said the two BOC personnel were involved based on the testimony of a middleman who was first arrested in a buy-bust in Sta. Maria, Bulacan.

The two BOC personnel were initially identified as a certain Joy and a certain Alex and their identity was established when the arrested middleman started revealing information as to the source of the smuggled cigarettes he was selling.
The revelation of the middleman was contained in an affidavit which was used by the HPG in filing a complaint against the two BOC personnel.
In the affidavit, the arrested middleman said it was a certain Joy, allegedly a special agent of the BOC, who asked for their assistance in selling around 225 boxes of cigarettes.
The same Joy allegedly instructed them to meet a buyer and where the cigarettes would be found, with the alleged assurance that there would be BOC personnel in the area where they would go.
According to the middleman, it was the certain Alex, allegedly a technical support staff of the BOC, who opened the warehouse for them on August 19 to get the cigarettes.
A few moments after they arrived, HPG personnel announced the raid.
The raid became controversial after the HPG operatives were accused of wrongdoing during the raid in the area where the alleged destruction of smuggled cigarettes was ongoing.
This resulted in the relief of 13 HPG personnel involved in the planning and the operation.
The Philippine National Police is yet to release its findings on the investigation into the matter.

articles.title: Lionel Richie hospitalized after St. Louis concert - reports
articles.summary: Lionel Richie has been admitted into an intensive care unit of a hospital after performing in St. Louis, Missouri, Saturday. According to Page Six , he checked himself into a local hospital to get…

blocks.text: Lionel Richie (Facebook)
Lionel Richie has been admitted into an intensive care unit of a hospital after performing in St. Louis, Missouri, Saturday.
According to Page Six, he checked himself into a local hospital to get testing done.
Doctors are reportedly looking into slight dehydration as cause of his illness.
According to those who attended his concert, the singer was having difficulty moving.
Lionel also asked his bandmates for a chair to sit on before singing "All Night Long."
Doctors attribute the singer's weakness to possible dehydration.
However, the fans are worried because he has been admitted to the hospital's ICU.
This isn’t the first time the singer has struggled to perform this year.
Back in June, Richie was rushed to the hospital after he fell ill onstage and abruptly ended his concert early.
During the first night of Richie’s 26-city North American tour at the Grand Casino Arena in St. Paul, Minnesota, the four-time Grammy winner appeared visibly distressed.
“When you’re feeling dizzy, sit your ass down,” Richie told the crowd.
After a 15-minute intermission, Richie’s band performed for the crowd.
Nearly an hour later, saxophonist Dino Soldo announced the show was canceled because Richie was “not feeling well.”

articles.title: Arci Muñoz’s ‘sana sa next flight may katabi na ako’ prayer has fans lining up
articles.summary: Arci Muñoz is perfectly capable of traveling solo. Then again, she is already tired of doing so. If there is one thing she would like to upgrade on her next flight, it is the seat beside her. The…

blocks.text: Arci Muñoz is perfectly capable of traveling solo.
Then again, she is already tired of doing so.
If there is one thing she would like to upgrade on her next flight, it is the seat beside her.
The actress and singer recently took to social media with a prayer that had less to do with turbulence and more to do with the lack of a willing shoulder.
“Lord Sana sa next flight may katabi na ako na puwedeng sandalan. Hindi naman puro bintana lang,” Arci wrote.
And just like that, her followers saw an opening.
The comment section quickly turned into what looked like an unofficial audition for the vacant seat.
“Pramis magli-leave pa ako sa opis,” one follower offered.
Another went straight to the terms and conditions: “Basta sagot mo pamasahe...”
Then there was the confident “Anytime idol, kalabitin mo lang ako.”
And perhaps the most efficient of them all: “Binata o Bintana?”
Arci’s post was clearly meant as a playful take on being single, but her followers were apparently more than willing to turn the joke into a travel arrangement.
At this rate, Arci may no longer have to worry about finding someone to lean on.
She might just have to worry about choosing who gets the seat.

articles.title: What if Michael Poa invokes lawyer-client privilege?
articles.summary: Impeachment endorser La Union 1st district Rep. Paolo Ortega V says the House prosecution panel will known what to do in the event witness Michael Poa invokes his lawyer-client privilege with…

blocks.text: Impeachment endorser La Union 1st district Rep. Paolo Ortega V says the House prosecution panel will known what to do in the event witness Michael Poa invokes his lawyer-client privilege with impeachment trial respondent, Vice President Sara Duterte.

In an virtual interview over the weekend, Ortega expressed belief that prosecutors have already anticipated this defense strategy, which had been one of the talking points leading to trial given Poa's former role under Duterte over at the Department of Education (DepEd).
“Well, isa po ’yan sa pinaghahandaan ng prosecution (That's one of the things the prosecution is preparing for),” Ortega said.

“Kung hiningi ng prosecutors o ng prosecution team na maging parte po siya sa roster of witnesses, kahit na hostile witness po siya, ibig sabihin nakahanda po ’yung team para po sa kahit anong bagay na kanyang maaaring sabihin or i-invoke, or ultimately kung strategy man nila ’yon,” added the House deputy speaker.

(If the prosecutors or the prosecution team asked him to be part of the roster of witnesses, even as a hostile witness, it means the team is prepared for anything he may say or invoke, or ultimately, if that is indeed their strategy.)
Poa served as DepEd undersecretary, chief-of-staff and spokesperson during Duterte’s tenure as education secretary from 2022 to 2024.
Poa has said he is willing to testify on matters involving his time at DepEd but may invoke lawyer-client privilege when necessary on matters related to his role as Duterte’s counsel.

In 2024, the House Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability held an inquiry into Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds. Poa, one of the invited resource persons, pointed to the Vice President as being the one responsible for the funds.
“Central figure po kasi siya, eh (He is a central figure)," Ortega said of Poa.

The prosecution is set to present Poa as third hostile witness in the trial after former Office of the Vice President (OVP) special disbursing officer Gina Acosta and Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio.

articles.title: Manileños urged to mask up amid toxic haze
articles.summary: Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno" Domagoso on Tuesday, Sept. 1, urged Manileños to wear masks and stay indoors as air quality in the city deteriorated amid haze reportedly linked to forest and…

blocks.text: Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno" Domagoso on Tuesday, Sept. 1, urged Manileños to wear masks and stay indoors as air quality in the city deteriorated amid haze reportedly linked to forest and land fires in Indonesia.

In his “Talk to the People” broadcast via Facebook, Domagoso said three of the city government’s five air quality monitoring stations recorded “Very Unhealthy” Air Quality Index (AQI) levels as of 6 a.m.
These were the stations at Puregold Tayuman, Anda Circle, and San Sebastian Residences.
The two other stations, located at Sta. Ana Hospital and Rajah Sulayman Park, recorded AQI levels classified as “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.”
Domagoso urged Manileños, particularly those with pre-existing health conditions, senior citizens, pregnant women, and students, to wear masks whenever they go outdoors.
He strongly recommended doubling up on masks because of the severity of the air pollution.

“Importanteng-importante na gumamit tayo ng mask, at hangga't maaari, ito ay doblehin ninyo dahil hindi po maganda ang hangin na ating malalanghap sa mga darating na oras (It is very important to use a mask, and as much as possible, double it because the air we will breathe in the coming hours is not good),” he said.
The mayor also advised residents without urgent outdoor activities to stay indoors and keep their windows closed to limit their exposure to polluted air.
He said those with pre-existing health conditions should take extra precautions as poor air quality could affect their respiratory systems.
The city government said the air quality readings were consistent with data from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB).
The DENR-EMB’s real-time monitoring station at Mehan Garden in Manila recorded an AQI of 231, classified as “Acutely Unhealthy.”
Domagoso said the haze was linked to forest and land fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra, Indonesia, with prevailing winds carrying smoke toward the Philippines.
He also assured residents that the Manila Health Department (MHD) and the city’s seven district hospitals were on alert for a possible increase in patients affected by the poor air quality.

“Rest assured that the Manila Health Department and our hospitals are on alert. Inaabangan na namin, baka magkaroon ng bulusok o biglang pagdami ng mga pasyenteng maaaring naapektuhan nitong masamang hangin (Rest assured that the Manila Health Department and our hospitals are on alert. We are anticipating that there could be a sudden increase in patients who may be affected by this poor air quality),” he said.
Domagoso noted that the deteriorating air quality adds to the city’s existing public health concerns, including a surge in leptospirosis cases following monsoon rains.

He directed the Manila City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Department (MCDRRMD) and the Department of Environment and Public Services (DEPS) to continue monitoring air quality and wind conditions and provide updates to the public.
He urged Manileños and those visiting the city to take additional precautions against the deteriorating air quality.

“Daig ng maagap ang masipag. Hinihikayat ko po ang lahat ng mamamayan sa Lungsod ng Maynila, at ang mga taong dumadako dito, na magbigay ng additional protection sa inyong sarili (It is better to be prepared than simply work hard. I urge all residents of Manila, as well as those who come here, to provide additional protection for yourselves),” he said.

blocks.text: The air quality in several areas of Manila reached unhealthy to very unhealthy levels on Tuesday, Sept. 1, prompting the city government to advise residents, particularly those belonging to sensitive groups, to limit prolonged outdoor activities.

The Department of Environment and Public Services (DEPS) said two of the city’s five air quality monitoring stations under the Asia Blue Skies Project recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) level classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups” as of 6 a.m.
These were the monitoring stations at Sta. Ana Hospital and Rajah Sulayman Park.
The three other stations—Puregold Tayuman, Anda Circle, and San Sebastian Residences—recorded “very unhealthy” AQI levels.
The city government said the elevated air pollution levels could be attributed to forest and land fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia.

DEPS advised individuals considered sensitive to air pollution, particularly those with respiratory conditions such as asthma, senior citizens, children, and pregnant women, to limit prolonged outdoor activities, especially in affected areas.
The advisory is part of the Manila City Government’s continuing efforts to monitor air quality and protect public health amid conditions that may affect the city’s urban environment.

articles.title: NLEX-San Simon Interchange traffic remains heavy as flooding prompts diversions
articles.summary: Traffic remained heavy along parts of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) on Tuesday morning amid the flooding in San Simon, Pampanga.

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 9:29am Updated September 1, 2026 9:53am
Traffic remained heavy along parts of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) on Tuesday morning amid the flooding in San Simon, Pampanga.
According to a report of GMA News' James Agustin on Unang Balita, NLEX management began diverting northbound vehicles at the Santa Rita Exit at 10:40 p.m. on Monday.
This was to prevent them from proceeding toward San Simon due to flooding caused by the overflowing Pampanga River.
Motorists were advised to take the Maharlika Highway and proceed toward the Central Luzon Link Expressway.

In a 9 a.m. advisory, NLEX Corporation said that Class 1 vehicles traveling northbound are being diverted to Balagtas exit and advised to proceed to Maharlika Road toward the Central Luzon Link Expressway due to the rising water level of the Pampanga River.
It added that the Balagtas northbound entry is temporarily closed for class 1 vehicles while Class 2 and 3 vehicles may continue.
NLEX Corporation added that Sta. Rita and Pulilan northbound entries are temporarily closed to all types of vehicles.
The diversion caused long lines of vehicles, including delivery and cargo trucks bound for provinces in northern Luzon.
Some truck drivers said they had been stuck in traffic for hours, while other motorists opted to park their vehicles and wait for the traffic situation to improve.
Bus passengers traveling to destinations such as Cagayan are also expected to face longer travel times.
The Santa Rita northbound entry and the Pulilan northbound entry were also temporarily closed.
Meanwhile, Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation (MPTC) said it would implement flood control measures to help ease the heavy traffic caused by the flooding.
The tollway operator said it would install 300-meter flood control barriers on both sides of the NLEX.
Trucks and pumping equipment would be deployed to remove accumulated floodwater in San Simon, it added.
MPTC also said a counterflow lane would be opened for emergency and response equipment.
The firm apologized to affected motorists and asked for their patience and understanding as efforts continue to address the flooding and restore normal traffic flow.—Joviland Rita/AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Alex Eala battles untested American qualifier to begin US Open
articles.summary: Eyeing a deep run in the last major of the year, Alex Eala launches her US Open campaign against American qualifier Mary Stoiana, who sees action in a Grand Slam main draw for the first time ever.

blocks.text: RETURN. The Philippines' Alex Eala in action during the Stars of the Open exhibition event in the 2026 US Open.
Eyeing a deep run in the last major of the year, Alex Eala launches her US Open campaign against American qualifier Mary Stoiana, who sees action in a Grand Slam main draw for the first time ever.

items: Alex Eala, seeded 17th and ranked 18th, faces American qualifier Mary Stoiana in the first round of the US Open, marking a shift from her previous struggles in qualifying rounds.
Eala has achieved significant milestones in her career, including historic wins against top players like Iga Swiatek and Clara Tauson, showcasing her growth and experience in high-stakes matches.
Stoiana, competing in her first Grand Slam main draw, faces Eala as her first top-20 opponent, highlighting the unpredictability of matches and the importance of consistency in performance.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala used to fight her way through the qualifying rounds just to earn a spot in a Grand Slam main draw. Now, the tables have turned as she faces a qualifier to open her US Open campaign.
Eala battles American world No. 122 Mary Stoiana in the first round at the Louis Armstrong Stadium in Flushing Meadows, New York, on Tuesday, September 1 (Wednesday, September 2, Manila time).
Seeded 17th and ranked 18th in the world, Eala enters the matchup as the heavy favorite to advance, having already proven she can win on a Grand Slam stage.
Last year in the US Open, she stunned Denmark’s Clara Tauson to become the first Filipino to win a major main draw match in the Open Era.
Eala then took another historic step in the Wimbledon Championships in July, dethroning Poland’s Iga Swiatek to reach the fourth round and once again becoming the first Filipino to achieve the feat.

“I think I’ve experienced so much growth in the past year and so many milestones in my career. I think there’s so many lessons in particular in terms of, you know, I’ve gotten to work closely with so many, so many amazing tennis players,” said Eala.
“I’ve gotten to experience more of their work ethic, obviously being in this environment a lot more. And I’ve gotten to compete against the best of the best a lot more frequently.”

Eala has proven to be a giant killer as she owns a 7-3 record against top-10 opponents this year, with her victims including Swiatek, Kazakhstan’s Elena Rybakina, USA’s Jessica Pegula, Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina, USA’s Coco Gauff, and Italy’s Jasmine Paolini.

While Eala has been in his position before, Stoiana treads into uncharted territory as she competes in a Grand Slam main draw for the first time in her career after overcoming France’s Harmony Tan, Great Britain’s Katie Swan, and China’s Yue Yuan in the qualifying.
In fact, the match against Eala marks Stoiana’s first-ever meeting with a top-20 opponent.
But Eala knows better than most not to underestimate an opponent, having once navigated the lower ranks herself.

“When you’re winning, you’re not that good. And when you’re losing, you’re not that bad. Even though now, maybe I’m top 20, even when I was 70 or something like that, the level, the difference is [marginal]. I think the huge difference comes in the consistency of how often you’re able to execute that level,” Eala told Andy Roddick’s Served.
“In individual matches, or even in trainings, anything can happen.”
A victory over Stoiana will propel Eala to a second-round clash against the winner between Ukraine’s Oleksandra Oliynykova and USA’s Reese Brantmeier.
Eala’s bracket includes world No. 4 Gauff and another American in Iva Jovic, who is ranked No. 14. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Ha Young withdraws from ‘The Trauma Code’ Season 2
articles.summary: Korean actress Ha Young will no longer appear in the second season of Netflix’s hit medical drama “The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call.” Netflix announced her withdrawal on Sept. 1. “Respecting the…

blocks.text: Korean actress Ha Young will no longer appear in the second season of Netflix’s hit medical drama “The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call.”
Netflix announced her withdrawal on Sept. 1.
“Respecting the actress's position, Ha Young has decided not to appear in the sequel to ‘The Trauma Code,’” the streaming platform said.
Ha Young’s decision comes amid the controversy surrounding her family background, which drew public attention in South Korea in August.

The actress had discussed her great-grandfather, Ahn Sang-ho, during an appearance on the TV program “Problem Child in House.” She said he was the first doctor to open a practice in Hanyang after returning from Japan, where he had studied Western medicine, and that he had treated Emperor Gojong.
Korean netizens subsequently raised allegations that Ahn had been a pro-Japanese collaborator during Japan’s colonial rule of Korea from 1910 to 1945.
Ha Young later apologized for her comments.
“Shamefully, in that state of ignorance, I spoke of my great-grandfather at various gatherings as if he were a source of family pride,” she said.
Ha Young had been announced as part of the cast of “The Trauma Code” Season 2 after appearing in the first season as nurse Cheon Jang-mi.
Her performance in the series earned her the Best New Actress award at the 2025 APAN Star Awards.
With her withdrawal, Ha Young will not reprise her role in the upcoming season.
The actress currently stars opposite Jung Hae-in in the Netflix series “Our Sticky Love.”
Her remaining announced project is the 2027 SBS drama “The Long Shot Trial,” in which she stars with Lee Je-hoon. Filming was reportedly nearing completion as of last month.
