articles.title: Alan Peter Cayetano defends Taguig Lakeshore, tells Lacson to show evidence of 'wasted' funds
articles.summary: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Monday defended the Lakeshore project in Taguig City after Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson said billions of public funds were wasted on flood control and…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 9:04am

Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Monday defended the Lakeshore project in Taguig City after Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson said billions of public funds were wasted on flood control and infrastructure projects.
He said Lakeshore had not been neglected or wasted.

“Sa kamay ng Taguig bilang tagapamahala, hindi po sinayang at hindi sinasayang ang Lakeshore... Let’s not let politics rob this generation and future generations of the opportunity to reap its benefits,” Cayetano said in a post on Facebook.
(Under Taguig's management, Lakeshore was not wasted or is being wasted.)

"Lakeshore is an area full of potential that we continually want to transform! We turned this into a home for events and other different functions—for health, education, leisure, businesses, and more. Many many people po rely on the Laguna Lake," Cayetano added.

"May this be a model for other lakes and developments in different LGUs—that with proper stewardship, purpose, and vision, we can transform these blessings into opportunities that benefit our people," he said.
"PS - ANG GANDA TALAGA KAPAG ANG GOVERNMENT PROJECT AY NAPAPAKINABANGAN NG MGA PILIPINO. SENATOR PING, ITO BA ANG TINATAWAG MO NA WASTED?" Cayetano wrote.
(PS - It is really good if a government project benefits Filipinos. Senator Ping, is this what you call wasted?)

The feud between Lacson and Cayetano over allegedly illegal reclamation projects on the Taguig side of Laguna Lake has continued, with Lacson claiming that at least P3.713 billion in public funds has been wasted on related projects.
In a post on X, Lacson said his team would submit its latest findings on the alleged anomalous projects to the Office of the Ombudsman’s fact-finding team for appropriate action.

“Based on official records and our investigation, the total cost of identified completed, ongoing (and suspended) DPWH flood control and multi-purpose projects along the ‘illegal’ Laguna Lakeshore reclamation areas in Taguig City has so far reached P3.713 billion,” he said.

“These do not include other anomalous slope protection and flood mitigation projects along Taguig River involving double appropriations and ‘ghost’ projects using recycled photographs in different ‘completed’ projects, for billing purposes,” he added.
Cayetano however challenged Lacson to present evidence to back his claims.

“If there is evidence against DPWH, Taguig, or against me, then present it. Stop the theatrics and let the evidence do the talking set in the proper judicial venue where fairness is assured,” he said.

“Every hour the government spends on political warfare instead of solving problems is wasted. Every peso spent on projects that do not serve the people is wasted. Every opportunity to reform a broken system sacrificed for personal or partisan advantage is wasted,” Cayetano said.
GMA News Online asked Lacson's camp for comment but has yet to receive their reply as of posting time. —with a report from Giselle Ombay/KG, GMA News

articles.title: Dr. Mike Varshavski reveals he dated Pia Wurtzbach at height of her Miss Universe reign
articles.summary: American doctor and content creator Dr. Mike Varshavski has revealed that he dated Pia Wurtzbach during the height of her Miss Universe reign, shedding new light on the romance that sparked…

blocks.text: American doctor and content creator Dr. Mike Varshavski has revealed that he dated Pia Wurtzbach during the height of her Miss Universe reign, shedding new light on the romance that sparked speculation in 2016.

Varshavski, popularly known as Doc Mike, brought up his past with Wurtzbach while talking to Filipino-Canadian nurse and content creator John dela Cruz, better known as Nurse John, in a recent episode of his YouTube channel.
The two were discussing the intense scrutiny Filipino celebrities and pageant queens face when Varshavski suddenly shared his own connection to the Philippines.
“You probably don’t know but I should share some of my history. I dated Pia Wurtzbach at the peak of her career,” Varshavski said.
His admission came nearly 10 years after he and Wurtzbach were first linked.
The two met at a small gathering in New York in February 2016, while Wurtzbach was still serving as Miss Universe.
Photos and clips of them together soon circulated online, prompting speculation that they were romantically involved.
At the time, Wurtzbach did not publicly acknowledge a relationship with Varshavski.
In March 2016, she addressed the rumors during a Facebook Live session, saying she was not dating anyone, emphasizing her focus was on her duties as Miss Universe.
She later confirmed in a television interview that she was, in fact, dating Varshavski.
The relationship was brief, however, and the two eventually went their separate ways.
Neither became particularly open about the details of their romance or what led to their breakup.
Varshavski’s recent comments offer a rare glimpse into that chapter of Wurtzbach’s life, which unfolded while she was under intense public scrutiny as Miss Universe.
Wurtzbach has since married Scottish-Colombian businessman and content creator Jeremy Jauncey. The couple currently live in Dubai.
Varshavski, meanwhile, has built a massive following as Doc Mike, combining his work as a family medicine physician with health and lifestyle content.

articles.title: Fuel prices roll back after 2 weeks of hikes
articles.summary: It's welcome news after motorists suffered through a rough August with pump prices swinging sharply due to the continuing conflict in the Middle East

blocks.text: ADJUSTMENTS. A gas station in Paco, Manila, on January 12, 2026.
Rappler
It's welcome news after motorists suffered through a rough August with pump prices swinging sharply due to the continuing conflict in the Middle East

items: Starting September 1, fuel prices in the Philippines were rolled back after two weeks of increases, with gasoline down by 0.32 per liter, diesel by P3.83, and kerosene by P3.84.
Prior to the rollback, retail prices in Metro Manila were P76.90 for gasoline RON95, P75.90 for gasoline RON91, P89.40 for diesel, and P118.10 for kerosene.
The rollback follows significant price hikes in August due to global market volatility, but local prices remain higher than before the Middle East crisis that began in February.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Fuel prices rolled back starting Tuesday, September 1, giving motorists some relief after two straight weeks of fuel price increases.
The Department of Energy (DOE) announced the following fuel price adjustments:

items: Gasoline – rollback of 0.32 per liter
Diesel – rollback of P3.83 per liter
Kerosene – rollback of P3.84 per liter

blocks.text: Before the latest adjustment, the Department of Energy’s price monitoring showed common retail prices in Metro Manila at P76.90 per liter for gasoline RON95, P75.90 per liter for gasoline RON91, P89.40 per liter for diesel, and P118.10 per liter for kerosene for the week of August 25 to 31.
The rollback follows last week’s fuel price hike, when gasoline rose by P1.08 per liter, diesel by P2.31 per liter, and kerosene by P0.95 per liter.
A week earlier, on August 18, gasoline prices also increased by P2.49 per liter, diesel by P3.84 per liter, and kerosene by P5.01 per liter.

The latest rollback provides some breathing room after a volatile August dominated by sharp swings in domestic pump prices due to movements in global crude and refined fuel markets, foreign exchange pressures, and continuing geopolitical risks in the Middle East.

The DOE’s August 25 oil monitor, which covered August 17 to 21 trading, showed the market pressures behind the previous week’s fuel price hike, including higher Dubai crude, gasoline, and diesel prices, as well as a weaker peso. But the same monitor also pointed to factors that could limit further increases, including rising US inventories, improving refinery output in Asia, and improved shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

Local pump prices remain above levels seen before the Middle East crisis erupted on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, DOE data showed common retail prices in Metro Manila at P56 per liter for gasoline RON95, P54.70 per liter for gasoline RON91, P55 per liter for diesel, and P83.47 per liter for kerosene.

The Philippines is a net importer of petroleum products, making local pump prices vulnerable to global oil price swings, foreign exchange movements, regional refined fuel prices, and disruptions in international supply routes. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis found guilty of orchestrating 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur
articles.summary: A jury has found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, marking the first conviction in a case that has gripped hip-hop fans for decades.

image.caption: Duane Davis is the first person convicted in the 30-year-old murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur. (Steve Marcus/Pool/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
A jury has found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, marking the first conviction in a case that has gripped hip-hop fans for decades.
Jury delivered its verdict after 3 hours of deliberations

The 63-year-old Davis was convicted Monday of murder with the use of a deadly weapon and could be sentenced to life in prison. The jury deliberated for three hours after a weeks-long trial in Las Vegas.
After the verdict was read, Shakur's sister, Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur, cried and reached back to a person behind her. Also in the courtroom was Davis's son, who covered his face with one hand.

Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors in closing arguments that Davis acquired a gun and "went hunting" for Shakur and Death Row Records co-founder Marion "Suge" Knight after they beat up Davis's nephew earlier that night.

Palal acknowledged that Davis's accounts of the killing evolved over the years but argued those differences reflected Davis's changing motivations and efforts to protect himself. One critical detail, he said, remained consistent: Davis repeatedly placed himself inside a white Cadillac from which the shots were fired.
"The core facts remain. The material facts remain," Palal said.

Davis's defence attorney, Michael Sanft, challenged jurors to identify evidence outside Davis's own statements that placed him in Las Vegas or inside the Cadillac on the night Shakur was shot. He pointed to the absence of surveillance footage, phone records and other evidence putting Davis there.
"They have nothing in this case that says that man was here in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996," Sanft said, pointing toward Davis.
Justice in murder of Tupac 'foregone years ago': cousin
The decades-old case has drawn the attention of hip-hop fans and crime experts alike.

Shakur, who was considered one of the most influential rappers of all time, was in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996, and stopped at a red light when a white Cadillac pulled up beside him, and shots were fired. He died six days later from his wounds. Knight was also wounded but survived.

For years, nobody had been charged in the rapper's death until Davis began making public statements, saying he was in the Cadillac and gave the gun to others in the backseat. Davis described the shooting as an act of retaliation after Knight and Shakur's entourage beat up Davis's nephew hours before the shooting.

items: Accused in Tupac Shakur murder trial says nephew fired the fatal shots in 1996 drive-by shooting
Former gang leader directed Tupac's drive-by killing, prosecutor tells jury
Man charged with arranging Tupac Shakur's murder heads to trial 30 years after hip-hop legend's death

blocks.text: Under Nevada law, someone who helps another person commit murder can be convicted of the crime. Davis is the only person still alive among the four men prosecutors say were in the Cadillac. The man prosecutors say originally gave the gun to Davis is also dead.
Palal told jurors that if they believe Davis's statements, they do not have to be independently corroborated with additional evidence.
"Who fired is not the question," Palal said. Prosecutors didn't argue that Davis pulled the trigger, but instead that he was criminally responsible because he provided the gun and ordered the attack.
Palal also argued the shooting was premeditated, pointing to testimony and Davis's accounts that the group searched for Shakur before spotting him on the road and making a U-turn.
"It's a plan, not an impulse," Palal said.
Davis's own words

Palal held up Davis's 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend, and played an interview in which Davis encouraged people to buy it to get the "real truth." Although the book contains a disclaimer saying some facts were changed, Palal argued that names, hotels and other details changed while the central account did not.

Palal also rejected the defence's contention that Davis fabricated his accounts to make money. "It is an entirely different proposition to be profiting from a murder," Palal said. "And that is what Mr. Davis is doing."

Sanft also turned to his client's memoir during his closing argument. While reading an excerpt, he said the N-word aloud, prompting people watching in an overflow courtroom to recoil and shake their heads.
In multiple interviews, Davis said he handed the gun to the back seat, but in others as well as in his book, Davis wouldn't say who pulled the trigger.
In a rebuttal argument, prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo pointed to a scrapbook Davis kept containing articles about Shakur.
"This guy's scrapbooking his murder, for God's sake," DiGiacomo told jurors.

articles.title: US army secretary resigns after months of tension
articles.summary: Dan Driscoll, the youngest-ever army secretary, was about 18 months into his post.

blocks.text: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has submitted his resignation after about 18 months in the role.
His departure was confirmed by CBS, the BBC's US media partner, which reported it came after months of conflict between him and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The youngest-ever army secretary has often been referred to as President Donald Trump's "drone guy".

Driscoll, 41, has been "highly effective" in advancing Trump's agenda "to Make America Strong Again" and provided "outstanding leadership" during military operations, the White House said in a statement given to CBS.
The BBC has contacted the White House, Pentagon and Army for comment.
Driscoll is the latest in a string of recent high-profile military leaders to depart, including Navy Secretary John Phelan who abruptly quit in April.
Other notable departures include Army Chief of Staff Randy George, Army Gen David Hodne and Maj Gen William Green.
Since entering the Pentagon, Hegseth has fired more than a dozen senior military officers, including the chief of naval operations and the Air Force's vice-chief of staff.

The details of the behind-the-scenes friction between Driscoll and Hegseth are unclear but CBS notes that the army secretary is good friends with George, who was reportedly asked by Hegseth to resign.
The post of army secretary is the top civilian leader of the US Army, directing active duty troops, along with the National Guard and reserve soldiers.
Driscoll previously served in the Army and was an officer in 2007 before leading a cavalry platoon and deploying to Iraq for several months in 2009.
As army secretary, Driscoll became known as Trump's "drone guy" due to his embrace of emerging battlefield technologies.
He took on a leading role last year in talks aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war, taking on foreign trips and meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
He's also a close ally and friend of Vice-President JD Vance, whom he met at Yale Law School.
During his tenure as head of the US Army, he was a key figure in Trump's deployment of the National Guard to US cities.
He also took over the role of acting director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.

articles.title: ‘Difference-maker’ Sotto played like an import for Gilas, says Cone
articles.summary: Much has already been said about the impact of Kai Sotto to the national team but head coach Tim Cone once again showered his 7-foot-3 big man with praises following Gilas Pilipinas’ sweep of the…

blocks.text: Much has already been said about the impact of Kai Sotto to the national team but head coach Tim Cone once again showered his 7-foot-3 big man with praises following Gilas Pilipinas’ sweep of the fourth window of the qualifiers.
Cone stressed that the decision of Sotto to suit up for the Gilas in this window was pivotal in pumping life to the Nationals’ hopes of making it back to the World Cup.
According to the veteran mentor, the 24-year-old big man was simply the difference maker who elevates Gilas’ level to a notch higher.

“He is the difference maker. Without him joining us I don't think we can get these two games. I don't think we can get close,” Cone said of Sotto, who averaged 15.5 points, 15.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.0 blocks through the two games in the window.
“He’s the one who takes us to the top. He’s the one who makes everybody better on the floor —offensively and defensively.

It was Sotto’s first pair of games for Gilas since recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury which sidelined him from national team duty. He last played for the Nationals in the FIBA Asia Cup qualifiers when Gilas took down New Zealand for the first time.
Sotto rejoining the team couldn’t be more timely as well, especially with Justin Brownlee sitting out the fourth window of the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian qualifiers.

“We’re just tickled pink that he’s chosen to join us this time, especially without Justin. We had our import in this guy. He certainly played like an import so thank you Kai for coming and doing the work that you did,” he added.
In a hot mic moment before the start of the press conference, Cone even stated that he believed Sotto actually deserves to be in the NBA.

The veteran mentor even opened up the possibility of him reaching out to the Miami Heat organization — having close ties – with current head coach Erik Spoelstra to try and help Sotto make it to the big league.
“I still think you need to get into the league (NBA). Find a way. I’ll talk to Miami and see what I can do,” said Cone.

articles.title: Putin, Xi hold talks in Kyrgyzstan as regional summit begins
articles.summary: BISHKEK — Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping began talks Monday in Kyrgyzstan, where a dozen other heads of state also gathered for a two-day summit of the Shanghai…

blocks.text: BISHKEK — Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping began talks Monday in Kyrgyzstan, where a dozen other heads of state also gathered for a two-day summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), which seeks to be a counterbalance to the West.

Iran’s leader Masoud Pezeshkian, Turkey’s Recep Tayyip Erdogan, India’s Narendra Modi and Pakistan’s Shehbaz Sharif were also among those in Bishkek to attend the summit of the regional SCO bloc, which celebrates its 25-year anniversary.
The summit takes place four-and-a-half years into Moscow’s Ukraine invasion and six months into the war between Washington and Tehran.
Putin and Xi have previously used SCO summits to promote their vision of a multipolar world and present a united front against the West.
Xi told Putin he was “happy” to see him, saying Russia-Chinese ties have become “more solid” and that their “prospects will be even brighter”.
“The amount of uncertainty and unpredictability in the international order has obviously increased,” the Chinese leader said.
Putin told Xi: “Cooperation is successfully developing on all fronts.” The pair last met in May.
Russia’s economy has become increasingly dependent on China during its invasion of Ukraine. Western countries have called on Beijing to pressure Moscow to end its offensive.
The Kremlin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian media the pair only discussed the Ukraine war “in passing”.
Putin also met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with both leaders arriving in the same car for the talks.
The Russian leader said Moscow was “following the path” towards resolution of the conflict in Ukraine, without elaborating.
The peace talks, brokered by the United States, remain stalled.
Putin is also expected to hold separate talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.
Russia and Iran — among the most sanctioned states in the world — have massively deepened their military and economic ties since Moscow invaded Ukraine.
War not ‘in our interest’
US President Donald Trump has warned Moscow and Beijing against arming Iran.

Putin’s meeting with Pezeshkian will come days after the CIA’s director John Ratcliffe made a rare trip to Moscow, with US media speculating he could have discussed Ukraine and Iran with his Russian counterparts.
Speaking in Bishkek after the first exchange of fire between the United States and Iran in a month, Iran’s Pezeshkian said continuing the war was not in Tehran’s interests.
“We continue to strive for a path of agreement and understanding, and we believe that continuing the war is neither in our interest, nor in the interest of the region,” he told India’s Modi.
Putin, Xi, Pezeshkian, Modi and Sharif are due to take part in a plenary session chaired by Kyrgyz leader Sadyr Japarov.
The SCO has historically focused on economic issues but has gained momentum in recent years under Moscow’s and Beijing’s leadership.
On top of its 10 members, it now has 15 “dialogue partners”, including Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
It also has two observer countries: Afghanistan and Mongolia.
Real and trade wars

The Bishkek summit takes place at a time when some SCO members are in the midst of real wars — the Ukraine and Iran conflicts — or trade wars, with the imposition of US tariffs on Chinese and Indian goods.
This month, the US slapped secondary sanctions on Iran’s trading partners in the sectors of gold, technology, digital assets, aviation and maritime transport, aiming to cripple Tehran’s economy.
Washington has also threatened Iran’s allies with sanctions.
China, a major importer of Iranian oil, responded by saying it would “firmly defend” its interests.
Iran, living under sanctions since its 1979 revolution ended with Islamic authorities taking charge, has regularly said it will not cave to economic pressure.
But Pezeshkian has acknowledged his country faces “economic difficulties”.
Iran only joined the bloc in 2023.

Mohammad Hassan Najmi, an international relations expert, told AFP that Tehran “believes its membership and active participation in these alliances can enable it to circumvent US and European sanctions”.
But concrete benefits of the group are uncertain, he said, as “in times of crisis, these alliances have rarely allowed Iran to resolve its difficulties”.
While the bloc claims to represent some 40 percent of the world’s population and 25 percent of global GDP, it remains diverse, with disagreements among members. /dl

articles.title: Marcos orders DPWH to restore connectivity in flood-hit Central Luzon -- Dizon
articles.summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. ordered the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to immediately restore connectivity in areas in Central Luzon severely affected by flooding and…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. ordered the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to immediately restore connectivity in areas in Central Luzon severely affected by flooding and infrastructure damage, Secretary Vince Dizon said Tuesday.

Interviewed on GMA Network’s Unang Hirit, Dizon said Marcos’ directive particularly covers Pampanga, Tarlac, and Zambales, where heavy rains damaged roads and bridges that led to disrupted transportation.
“Unang kabilin-bilinan po ng Pangulo is kailangan mabilis nating maresolba itong mga nananatili nating mga problema lalo na sa Central Luzon,” Dizon said.
(The President's first order is to resolve immediately the problems, particularly in Central Luzon.)
“Lalo na sa mga probinsya ng Tarlac, Pampanga, at Zambales. Dahil nga napakadami pang mga problema ang iniwan nitong napakabigat na pag-ulan nitong nakaraang mga araw,” he added.
(Especially in the provinces of Tarlac, Pampanga, and Zambales. The heavy rains in the past days really caused a lot of problems.)
Dizon made the statement following a meeting with the President on Monday evening.
In Pampanga, traffic remained heavily affected along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) in San Simon, where floodwaters have disrupted the movement of vehicles and goods.

Dizon said DPWH, NLEX Corp., the Department of Transportation and the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) have been coordinating efforts to address the flooding. Temporary flood barriers have been installed and pumps deployed to remove water from the expressway.
As of early Tuesday morning, Dizon said the first two inner lanes of NLEX in San Simon had become passable to vehicles.

He said authorities are also looking at a permanent solution to the recurring flooding, noting that simply raising the expressway further may not be feasible because of an existing bridge that needs to accommodate buses and trucks.
In Tarlac, two bridges connecting Tarlac City were damaged.

Dizon said the DPWH is prioritizing the repair of Agana Bridge. Workers have been deployed on a 24/7 basis to reconnect the bridge as soon as possible. However, repairs remain difficult because the river beneath the bridges continues to have a strong current.

The Agana Bridge, which was built in the 1960s, needs structural reinforcement, according to Dizon. The Aquino Bridge will also be repaired once weather conditions improve and the river's flow subsides.
“Hindi po 'yan inayos nang mabuti. Hindi po 'yan ni-retrofit nang mabuti. Hindi po na-maintain nang mabuti,” Dizon said.
(It was not repaired properly. It was not retrofitted properly. It was not maintained well.)

Authorities are investigating a sinkhole near the Aquino Bridge. Dizon said simply filling it with soil would not be enough because engineers first need to determine the source of the water that caused the ground to collapse.
Authorities have closed the affected pedestrian area as a precaution.
Dizon pointed out that man-made factors contributed to the flooding, including years of inadequate maintenance and repair of infrastructure.

He acknowledged concerns over the billions of pesos spent on flood-control projects in previous decades. He said the government now needs to prioritize the repair of damaged dikes and bridges and ensure proper maintenance of flood-control infrastructure.
Retarding basins

For Pampanga's long-term flooding problem, Dizon said the government is looking at the construction of retarding basins or water-storage areas that can temporarily hold excess water from mountains and rivers before it reaches populated areas.
He said the DPWH, Pampanga provincial government, and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) are nearing completion of a master plan for the Pampanga River Basin.
“Ang solusyon lang talaga is umpisahan na nating i-implement immediately itong plano ng Asian Development Bank, kasama na rin ang mga partners natin sa Japan,” Dizon said.
(The only solution is to start implementing the ADB plan, together with our partners from Japan.)

“At marami dito ang tinatawag ay 'yung mga retarding basin, 'yung mga imbakan ng tubig na kailangan itayo natin mula sa kabundukan ng Nueva Ecija hanggang sa lahat ng mga munisipyo ng Pampanga at Bulacan,” he added.
(Many of these are retarding basins; these are water storage we need to build from the mountains of Nueva Ecija up to the municipalities of Pampanga and Bulacan.) —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Police presence ordered in flood-hit roads after NLEX traffic ordeal
articles.summary: Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), ordered chiefs of police and unit commanders to strengthen monitoring on flooded roads and expressways amid heavy…

blocks.text: Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), ordered chiefs of police and unit commanders to strengthen monitoring on flooded roads and expressways amid heavy rains that rendered even major expressways and thoroughfares not passable to vehicles.

Nartatez said the move is to maximize assistance to the affected motorists and it starts with repositioning and strategic deployment of police vehicles are also necessary in cases of emergencies and any untoward incident that could happen.

He issued the statement after the incident at the San Simon portion of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) where travel disruption and monstrous traffic jams were experienced by thousands of motorists and passengers.

“Motorists are usually left on their own in dealing with flooded roads. We do not want that to happen. There should be police presence in areas where they are needed, and that includes this kind of situation in cases of emergencies and other forms of assistance that the PNP is capable of,” said Nartatez.
Some motorists said they had been stuck for hours before getting past the flooded section of the expressway as flooding struck since Friday and worsened over the weekend.
The northbound traffic tail-end had reached Candaba and stretched for more than seven kilometers while the southbound queue reached around five to six kilometers.
Traffic measures were implemented in the affected section as Class 1 vehicles were directed to the innermost lane while trucks and buses were allowed to use the second lane.

While dealing with flooded roads is a serious challenge, Nartatez said these areas should be part of the ground monitoring and should be factored in deployment of PNP personnel and resources for the safety and peace of mind of the affected residents.

He said territorial police forces and concerned police units should maintain visibility, assist stranded motorists, facilitate the movement of emergency vehicles, and coordinate closely with local government units and even expressway managements for a unified response system.
Nartatez directed concerned police units to closely monitor flood conditions, traffic queues, and motorists who may require assistance.

“We urge motorists to avoid unnecessary travel through the affected area. Those who need to travel should exercise caution, follow traffic advisories, and cooperate with police and highway authorities on the ground,” Nartatez said.

articles.title: 'Pilandok' keeps strength as habagat brings heavy rain over Luzon, Visayas
articles.summary: Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength Tuesday as the southwest monsoon or habagat is expected to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon and the western section of the Visayas, PAGASA…

blocks.text: September 1, 2026 | 8:52am
Satellite rendering shows Typhoon Depression Pilandok taken on Sept. 1, 2026.
PAGASA via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength Tuesday as the southwest monsoon or habagat is expected to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon and the western section of the Visayas, PAGASA said.
In its 5 a.m. bulletin on Tuesday, September 1, the state weather bureau said Pilandok was located 1,050 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon.
Pilandok was carrying maximum sustained winds of 55 kilometers per hour near the center, with gustiness of up to 70 kph.
It was moving west-northwestward at 10 kph.
Pilandok is not directly affecting the country's land areas, while the southwest monsoon continues to bring rains over Luzon and the western section of the Visayas.
No tropical cyclone wind signal is currently raised over any part of the country.
Strong winds

PAGASA said the southwest monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over most of Luzon and Visayas, as well as Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental until Thursday, September 3.
PAGASA said strong to gale-force gusts are particularly possible in coastal and upland areas exposed to the winds.
Heavy rainfall
The state weather bureau said the southwest monsoon or habagat will continue to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon through Thursday, September 3.
Tuesday, September 1

items: 50-100 mm: Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Batanes, Abra, Benguet, Zambales and Bataan

blocks.text: Wednesday, September 2

items: 50-100 mm: Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Batanes, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro

blocks.text: Thursday, September 3

items: 100-200 mm: Benguet, Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro
50-100 mm: Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Abra, La Union, Pangasinan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Cavite and Batangas

blocks.text: PAGASA said forecast rainfall may be higher in mountainous and elevated areas. The impacts in some areas may also be worsened by significant antecedent rainfall.
Sea conditions
A gale warning is in effect over the northern and western seaboards of Northern Luzon.
Very rough seas with waves reaching up to 5 meters are expected over the western seaboard of the Babuyan Islands and the seaboards of Ilocos Norte.
Waves of up to 4.5 meters are also forecast over the western seaboards of Batanes and Pangasinan, as well as the seaboards of Ilocos Sur and northern La Union.
PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for all types and tonnage of vessels under these conditions.
Small seacraft operators, including those using motorbancas, are also advised not to venture out to sea in affected waters.
Track, intensity
PAGASA said Pilandok is forecast to slowly turn east-northeastward then northward over the next 24 hours.
It will then move generally north-northwestward for the remainder of the forecast period.
Pilandok is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility by Wednesday evening, September 2, or Thursday morning, September 3.
The tropical depression is less likely to make landfall over the Philippines and is expected to remain far from the country's landmass.
Pilandok is forecast to intensify into a tropical storm within the next 12 hours and may remain a tropical storm as it moves toward southern Japan.
PAGASA said that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still be experienced in areas outside Pilandok's forecast track and confidence cone.

Chuck Thompson, the head of public affairs at CBC, says the public broadcaster is reviewing the Republican National Committee's "disappointing" decision to revoke CBC/Radio-Canada press accreditation for next month's event in Dallas, Texas.
CBC official says public broadcaster hopes 'disappointing' decision will be resconsidered
The Republican Party has revoked CBC/Radio-Canada's media accreditation for the party's upcoming midterm convention.

Chuck Thompson, the head of public affairs at CBC, confirmed on Monday that the Republican National Committee (RNC) would no longer provide accreditation for CBC/Radio-Canada journalists to cover the convention in Dallas, Texas, on Sept. 9 and 10.
Thompson said in a written statement that CBC was reviewing the RNC's decision.
"It is a disappointing development; we hope it will be reconsidered."

items: America 'not at war' with Canada, insists U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent
IN PHOTOS | In the crosshairs of a trade war

blocks.text: Convention organizers did not immediately respond to CBC News' emailed requests for comment on Monday evening.
The White House referred CBC's questions to the RNC. CBC News was not able to reach the committee by phone Monday evening.
The revocation comes as tensions between Canada and the United States have soared amid a new wave of tit-for-tat sanctions and heated rhetoric from politicians on both sides of the border.

Republican lawmakers and Trump administration officials also recently criticized CBC after a leaked internal memo from the public broadcaster regarding the use of the words "terrorism" and "terrorist" in relation to the 9/11 attacks drew international attention.
How is the Canada-U.S. trade war affecting Carney's approval ratings?

The memo referred to a longstanding policy that had instructed CBC journalists to "generally avoid labelling any specific bombing or other assault as a 'terrorist act' unless this term is attributed."
It drew widespread condemnation ahead of the 25-year anniversary of 9/11 next month.

items: How and why CBC News will adjust its 9/11 language guidance

blocks.text: "What possible motive could there be for sanitizing the worst terrorist attack on American soil? Care to explain, @Canada?" a group of Republican members of the U.S. House of Representatives wrote on social media on Thursday.

On Friday, Basem Boshra, CBC's senior director of journalistic standards and public trust, said that after reviewing the public broadcaster's current language guidance, "we have decided to adjust it to clarify that direct attribution is not required for describing the historic events of 9/11 as terrorism."
"We are doing so to remove what has unfortunately (and unintentionally) become an impediment to clarity and public understanding," Boshra said.

articles.title: Taal Volcano logs 6 quakes, lone tremor in past 24 hours
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — Taal Volcano in Batangas recorded six volcanic earthquakes and a single prolonged tremor in the past 24 hours, indicating a decline in seismic activity, the Philippine Institute of…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — Taal Volcano in Batangas recorded six volcanic earthquakes and a single prolonged tremor in the past 24 hours, indicating a decline in seismic activity, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) reported Tuesday, Sept. 1.

In its latest bulletin, Phivolcs said the volcanic tremor lasted 420 minutes. Despite its duration, the agency said there was no immediate cause for alarm, noting that volcanic tremors are a normal occurrence at Taal.

The latest seismic activity marked a notable decline from the previous nine days, from Aug. 20 to 28, when Taal recorded double-digit numbers of volcanic earthquakes daily, for a total of 229 earthquakes and 12 tremor episodes.
On Aug. 29, Taal recorded eight volcanic earthquakes, another eight the following day, and 13 on Aug. 31.
Phivolcs defines volcanic earthquakes as those “generated by magmatic processes or magma-related processes beneath or near an active volcano.”

“Unlike tectonic earthquakes that are produced by faulting, volcanic earthquakes are directly produced by many processes and are, therefore, much more varied in characteristics,” the agency explained.
Volcanic tremors, meanwhile, are continuous seismic signals with regular or irregular oscillations and low frequencies, typically ranging from 0.5 to 5 hertz, that can last for more than a minute.
Despite the decline in seismic activity, Taal continued to emit sulfur dioxide. Phivolcs recorded 381 metric tons of SO₂, although the emission level remained classified as “weak.”
The agency also reported no observed upwelling of hot volcanic fluids in the Main Crater Lake and no volcanic smog, or “vog,” during the monitoring period.
On Saturday (August 29), Phivolcs warned of possible lahar flows and volcanic debris around Taal and Mount Pinatubo amid prolonged heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or “habagat.”
Heavy rainfall may trigger muddy streamflows and volcanic debris flows around Taal Volcano, particularly along the western and northern slopes of Taal Lake.
These hazards could affect parts of Batangas, particularly the municipalities of Agoncillo, Laurel, and Talisay.
Phivolcs advised communities in potentially affected areas to closely monitor weather conditions and take necessary precautionary measures.
Taal Volcano remains under Alert Level 1, indicating a low level of volcanic unrest. /dp

articles.title: Heavy rain at Grand Canyon after flood kills 2, dozen missing
articles.summary: GRAND CANYON VILLAGE, United States — Heavy rainstorms swept through the Grand Canyon on Monday, threatening efforts to find more than a dozen people missing after flash floods over the…

blocks.text: GRAND CANYON VILLAGE, United States — Heavy rainstorms swept through the Grand Canyon on Monday, threatening efforts to find more than a dozen people missing after flash floods over the weekend, the National Park Service (NPS) said, with two bodies already recovered.
The floods hit the iconic US park’s Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area on Saturday afternoon, forcing dozens of people to evacuate and damaging the sole water pipeline serving the area.
The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered on Sunday evening, the park service said.
The NPS said on Monday that a second body had been recovered, while warning that “forecasted weather may affect the timing and pace” of further search operations.
On Monday afternoon, low cloud shrouded the deep ravine, and the National Weather Service warned of more flooding with rain and thunderstorms in the forecast.

“Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded,” it said in a bulletin.

On Monday, a handful of visitors, many of them foreign tourists, huddled under umbrellas or wore rain ponchos as they stood on the South Rim snapping selfies and straining to make out the Colorado River far below.

Video footage taken over the weekend by hikers showed a torrent of muddy water rushing by trails and under footbridges as well as logs and other debris floating down swollen rivers, accompanied by a rumbling roar.
The park service said it was working with Arizona authorities to evacuate people and account for missing individuals.
As of Sunday morning, 62 people had been evacuated, with others scheduled for later, it said.
It said around 15 people were thought to be missing.
A press conference was expected later Monday, when first responders would be joined by local and park officials to give reporters an update on the search for those left unaccounted for.
Water pipeline damaged
The flooding damaged or destroyed 40 percent of the Transcanyon Waterline, a key water pipeline into Grand Canyon National Park, the park service said Monday.
It announced water restrictions in its most visited area and a ban on wood and charcoal fires.

The twelve-and-a-half-mile (20 kilometers) pipeline runs from the Roaring Springs source on the North Rim to the South Rim, providing drinking water and fire suppression, according to the park’s website.
The flooding also resulted in “significant impacts to infrastructure,” destroying footbridges and blocking hikers from crossing Bright Angel Creek, the park service said.

Trails down into the Canyon from the South Rim remained open on Monday, but staff were warning visitors of the potential dangers, with sudden squalls possible at any time during the Southwest monsoon season.
The hike down into the wild belly of the Canyon from one popular starting point takes many visitors around four hours, one staff member said, while the return journey would likely add another six.

Flash floods are common in Northern Arizona because the arid, sparsely vegetated environments there have little capacity to absorb rain, the park’s website said, urging visitors to be especially cautious from July to mid-September.

The Grand Canyon — considered one of the greatest wonders of the natural world — is the result of the Colorado River eating away at layers of red sandstone and other rock for millions of years, leaving a chasm up to 18 miles wide and more than a mile deep.
Last year almost five million people visited the site. /dl

articles.title: 11 NCR stations record ‘acutely unhealthy’ air amid haze possibly linked to Indonesia fires
articles.summary: Eleven of 15 monitoring stations in the National Capital Region (NCR) recorded “acutely unhealthy” air quality based on fine particulate matter (PM2.5) readings on Tuesday morning, Sept. 1, amid haze…

blocks.text: Philippines | National
Public advised to wear masks amid haze
(MB FILE PHOTO)

Eleven of 15 monitoring stations in the National Capital Region (NCR) recorded “acutely unhealthy” air quality based on fine particulate matter (PM2.5) readings on Tuesday morning, Sept. 1, amid haze that the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) said was “possibly associated with smoke and transboundary haze from ongoing fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia.”
PM2.5 refers to fine pollutants small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs.
In an advisory, the bureau said prevailing winds may have transported the haze toward the Philippines.
The DENR-EMB said it is closely monitoring the air quality situation, particularly in the National Capital Region, Calabarzon, and Mimaropa.
Data from DENR as of 7 a.m. showed that the Don Bosco monitoring station in Parañaque registered an air quality index (AQI) of 300, the highest among the 15 stations listed on the bureau’s dashboard.
The reading was one point below the “emergency” range of 301 to 500. Under the EMB-NCR scale, AQI readings from 201 to 300 are classified as “acutely unhealthy.”

blocks.caption: (MB FILE PHOTO)

blocks.text: Other stations with acutely unhealthy air quality were Quezon City (Ateneo), 242; Las Piñas, 240; Manila, 233; Malabon, 230; Taguig (TUP), 226; Valenzuela, 224; Marikina (Parang) and Muntinlupa (Filinvest City), both 219; San Juan, 214; and Mandaluyong, 209.
Meanwhile, Pateros recorded an AQI of 177, followed by Navotas at 155 and Makati at 151. All three readings were classified as “very unhealthy.”
The SMPH Commonwealth station in Quezon City posted the lowest reading at 140, which was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups.”
Amid the haze, the DENR-EMB advised the public to reduce their time outdoors.
“Minimize prolonged outdoor activities, particularly in areas visibly affected by haze,” it said.

“Persons who are sensitive to air pollution, including children, older persons, and individuals with respiratory or cardiovascular conditions, are advised to limit outdoor exposure and take necessary precautions,” it added.
As such, DENR-EMB advised people going outdoors in areas with noticeable haze to wear a well-fitting mask, preferably an N95 or its equivalent.
“The DENR-EMB is continuously monitoring air quality levels through its network of air quality monitoring stations to assess the extent and potential impacts of the haze,” it said.

articles.title: Krystal Mejes reveals fear ahead of 10th anniversary concert
articles.summary: Krystal Mejes may have gained a bigger following after her “Pinoy Big Brother Celebrity Collab Edition 2.0” stint, but the actress and singer admitted she still had doubts about whether people would…

blocks.text: Krystal Mejes may have gained a bigger following after her “Pinoy Big Brother Celebrity Collab Edition 2.0” stint, but the actress and singer admitted she still had doubts about whether people would actually show up for her 10th-anniversary celebration.
Mejes, who finished as second big placer of the reality show, said she became nervous when ticket-selling for her anniversary celebration began.
“Honestly po, kinakabahan talaga ako… I don’t think people are gonna come. But when I saw so many people, I was super grateful and happy,” she said.
Seeing fans come out to support her eased those fears and made the milestone more meaningful for Mejes, who has spent a decade working in showbiz.
She started in the industry at age six and has grown up in front of the public, taking on different acting roles before gaining a new wave of attention through “PBB Celebrity Collab Edition 2.0.”
Now, as she marks 10 years in the business, Mejes said she wants to make sure the people who have supported her feel that their presence matters.
“I’ll make sure it’s worth their time,” she said.
Her anniversary celebration, “Becoming,” will be held on September 26 at the New Frontier Theater. The fan meet and advocacy concert will also benefit her outreach initiative, Tala Gives.

Asked what "Becoming" means for her, she said, “'Becoming' is not about having figured out everything, but figuring myself out with people watching me… Growth is a continuous journey and self-discovery is lifelong.”
She also sees the event as a chance for fans to see a more personal side of her.
“They’re used to seeing me portray different characters. But this night is just going to be really me,” Mejes said.
Her work through Tala Gives has also shaped how she views her journey in showbiz.
“Tala Gives has taught me compassion and service. More than having projects and accomplishments, I realized it’s important to create stories and leave a lasting impact on people’s lives,” she said.

articles.title: Tupac Shakur murder trial: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis guilty
articles.summary: The jury reached a verdict in less than three hours in a case that had been unsolved for nearly 30 years.

image.caption: Davis is 63 years oldImage: Steve Marcus/REUTERS

blocks.text: A Las Vegas jury on Monday found former gang leader, Duane "Keffe D" Davis, guilty of orchestrating the killing of hip hop artist Tupac Shakur, following nine days of testimony.
It took jurors less than three hours to reach a guilty verdict in a case that has up until now been unsolved for almost three decades.
Sixty three-year-old Davis was convicted of murder with the use of a deadly weapon and could be sentenced to life in prison.
Shakur was wounded in a drive-by shooting on September 7, 1996, and died in a hospital six days later at the age of 25.
He was an award-winning rap artist, activist and actor who sold over 75 million records worldwide, many posthumously.
Davis, a one-time leader of the South Side Compton Crips gang, is the only person ever to have been charged in Shakur’s murder.
He is the only person still alive among the four men prosecutors say were in the Cadillac from which shots were fired. The man who prosecutors say originally gave the gun to Davis is also dead.
In closing arguments, Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors that Davis acquired a gun and “went hunting” for Shakur and Knight after they beat up Davis’ nephew earlier that night.
Palal said that Davis’ accounts of the killing evolved over the years but maintained that those differences showed Davis’ changing motivations and efforts to protect himself.
Palal argued that a key detail remained consistent throughout and that was that Davis repeatedly placed himself inside the white Cadillac from which the shots were fired.
More to follow…

articles.title: Two dead and at least 15 missing after flash flood in Grand Canyon
articles.summary:
National Park Service confirms second death from weekend flash flood as area braces for more storms

A second death was…

blocks.text: A second death was confirmed by National Park Service officials on Monday after a flash flood sent a surge of water and debris through an area of the Grand Canyon over the weekend.

Dozens of visitors had to be evacuated by helicopter during the deluge, which consumed trails and infrastructure. Fifteen people are still missing or unaccounted for, as more heavy rain and thunderstorms in the forecasts threaten additional debris flows, flash floods or rock falls, the NPS said in a statement.
“With deep monsoonal moisture in place and already saturated soils in some locations, an elevated risk of flash flooding will be in place through Monday,” the National Weather Service (NWS) said.

Park officials are calling on the public to provide any information on those who may have been hiking or backpacking in the inner canyon near Bright Angel Creek, or campers with a reservation in the area.

Flash floods are not uncommon in the region, especially during the monsoon season from June to September when strong rains pummel the arid landscapes and can quickly fill narrow rock formations. Visiting the Grand Canyon – a crown jewel of the US national park system – can be particularly dangerous in the summer because of the risk of flash flooding that accompanies the monsoon, when clear days can give way quickly to thunderstorms and downpours.

The deluge that unleashed torrents of rain on hardened and sparsely vegetated steep terrain came as the Grand Canyon region – and the Colorado River basin that runs through it – continue to be mired in a severe drought that has fueled a widespread water crisis.

Scientists have long warned that the climate crisis will create stronger extremes and destructive shifts between wet and dry conditions. The sudden and strong rainstorm that fueled this catastrophic flood may have been been supercharged by the historic El Niño that has sharply increased sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, which has the ability to affect weather systems around the world.

The NWS has issued flood watches across a large part of the south-west, including in northern Arizona. Officials cautioned against visiting creeks, slot canyons, burn scars and low water crossings in the area, where flash floods can quickly develop.

Videos taken by hikers before they were airlifted to safety showed churning brown waters carrying large metal objects and other debris. Some crossed the bridges just shortly before they were consumed by the waterway.

blocks.caption: Bright Angel Canyon, the scene of flash floods, runs into the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon. Photograph: John Locher/AP

blocks.text: “It must have been, like, 10 minutes afterwards – we crossed the bridges to get to the evacuation zone,” hiker Gabriel Burgeman told a local news station. “We were just barely in time to cross them before they got wiped out.”

The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered on Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River, the NPS said, without providing additional details. At least one other body has been recovered, according to a statement posted on Facebook by the Grand Canyon national park without details.

Early assessments also showed roughly 40% of a key pipeline that provides drinking water for tourists and residents had been damaged or destroyed. The 12.5-mile (20km) long Transcanyon Waterline has endured dozens of breaks in recent years. A more than $200m repair and replacement project was well under way when the floods hit.

The pipeline moves water from one side of the canyon, down to its base, across a bridge and back up the other side of the rough landscape. Any effort to fix a break from rock falls or flash floods is time-consuming, precarious and costly, so addressing the latest damage will be complicated.

Emergency water restrictions began on Monday, closing down all overnight stay lodges and hotels within Grand Canyon national park, and spigots at campgrounds on the South Rim were turned off. Year-round residents were asked to conserve water. The park had water conservation measures in place even before the latest bout of flooding and damage.

blocks.caption: People wait near a bridge as a helicopter flies nearby. Photograph: Wieke De Boer/Reuters

blocks.text: The flooding on Saturday in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, led to more than 60 people being airlifted from the canyon’s depths.
Parth Desai was hiking through a narrow passage in Bright Angel Canyon with fellow physicians and a park ranger when heavy rain started falling on Saturday.
“We saw the creek flood, waterfalls coming up out of nowhere, boulders, mud, landslides happening everywhere,” he said.

Torrents of water wiped out footbridges over the creek and altered the landscape, widening the creek bed and extending an existing river rapid or creating a new one. The flood was a blow to an enduring effort to modernize the pipeline that serves 6 million visitors a year and roughly 1,600 residents of Grand Canyon Village.

“Heaven help us if the whole thing down there at the bottom has to be reconstructed,” said Jack Schmidt, director of the Center for Colorado River Studies at Utah State University. “Where are they going to get the money?”

blocks.caption: The campsite at Bright Angel Creek corridor is seen from Grand Canyon Village. Photograph: Ian Maule/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Halting overnight stays at the park because of a lack of water is rare, although the pipeline frequently has failed over the years. While the Grand Canyon has large storage tanks for potable water on the South Rim, they will not be refilled while the pipeline is out of service.

A $208m rehabilitation of the pipeline and upgrades to the associated water delivery system started in 2023, with the park service calling it a crucial investment to ensure the park can meet the needs of residents and visitors. The project was expected to be completed next year.
In unrelated flooding, officials in San Antonio, Texas, on Sunday reported a pair of deaths related to a severe storm there two days earlier.

blocks.caption: Flood debris lines Bright Angel Creek. Photograph: John Locher/AP

blocks.text: Police said a 46-year-old woman died after being caught in rushing water in San Pedro Creek north of downtown, Texas Public Radio reported. A person with that woman made it out the situation safely, police said.
Separately, police said a man in his 50s was found at Woodlawn Park on Sunday morning.
The woman’s death is being investigated as a drowning while the man’s death is considered a possible drowning, police said.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: Man to face raps for throwing dead dog into Marikina River
articles.summary: Marikina City Mayor Maan Teodoro on Monday, Aug. 31, assured the public that appropriate charges will be filed against a man who was seen in a viral video throwing a sack containing a dead dog into…

blocks.text: Marikina City Mayor Maan Teodoro on Monday, Aug. 31, assured the public that appropriate charges will be filed against a man who was seen in a viral video throwing a sack containing a dead dog into the Marikina River.
A man is seen in a viral video allegedly throwing a sack containing a dead dog into the Marikina River. (Screengrab from Angelica Nvrr Casas/Facebook)

In a video uploaded on Sunday, Aug. 30, by Facebook user Angelica Nvrr Casas, the man was seen holding a sack allegedly containing the dog's body. The uploader pleaded with him not to throw it into the river, but he did so anyway.
The uploader was also heard saying, “Tuwang-tuwa ka pa, kuya, oh (And you’re still happy),” after the man appeared to smile after throwing the sack.
Teodoro commented on the post, saying that the man had already been located and would be facing the appropriate charges after she asked authorities to look for him upon seeing the video.

“Located na ang lalaki sa video at sasampahan ng kaukulang reklamo, ipinapaubaya na natin sa mga rightful authorities ang proseso ng hustisya (The man in the video has been located and will face the appropriate charges. We will leave the process of justice to the proper authorities),” she said.
The mayor added that such acts are unacceptable in Marikina.

“Bastos at nakakapanggigil ang ginawa niya. Walang kalaban-laban ang aso, itinapon pa sa ilog. Hindi ‘yan katanggap-tanggap at hindi natin palalampasin ‘yan sa Marikina. Hahanapin natin at papanagutin sa batas (What he did was disrespectful and infuriating. The dog was defenseless, yet he still threw it into the river. That is unacceptable, and we will not let it slide in Marikina. We will find him and hold him accountable under the law),” she added.
The uploader, who is also a fur mom, expressed anger and disappointment, saying that the man treated the dog like garbage when he casually threw it into the river.

“Patay na nga yung aso, itatapon mo pa sa ilog na parang walang halaga ang buhay niya?! Sana man lang inilibing na lang nang maayos (The dog was already dead, and you still threw it into the river as if its life meant nothing?! You should have at least buried it properly),” Casas said.

“Kahit patay na sila, they still deserve respect and a proper burial. Kung hindi kayo marunong magmahal ng hayop, at least matuto kayong rumespeto (If you don't know how to love animals, at least learn to respect them),” the uploader added.
She also urged the public to be more responsible and compassionate, not only toward people but also toward animals and the environment.
“Hindi sila basura (They are not garbage). They deserve dignity and respect, even in death.”

articles.title: Man shot and killed in Sydney home invasion was ‘targeted attack’, police believe
articles.summary: Alleged offenders at large after man in his early 20s fatally shot in early hours of Tuesday

blocks.text: A man in his early 20s has been fatally shot in an alleged home invasion in Sydney’s south-west that police believe was a “targeted attack”. A homicide investigation is under way, with the alleged offenders still at large.

Acting supt Gretchin Atkins said the man, who was yet to be formally identified, was at his Glen Alpine home with his family in the early hours of Tuesday morning when multiple individuals allegedly broke in.
Emergency services were called to the property at about 3.40am, Atkins said, where officers found the man with a gunshot wound. He died at the scene.
Officers were told the unknown offenders fled the scene shortly before police arrived.
“We believe at this point in time it is a targeted attack – that is all the information that we’ve been able to gather at this time,” Atkins said. “Everything is certainly subject to our inquiries.”
A crime scene has been established and an investigation is under way, with the assistance of the New South Wales crime command’s homicide squad.
Atkins said police had confirmed there were “multiple” alleged perpetrators behind the attack but there was “a lot we don’t know”.
“We are appealing to any person who was in the area, who saw, whether cars or people, who can assist us with our our current investigation, our inquiries,” she said.
The victim was only known to police for a traffic offence, Atkins said, and otherwise had no known criminal involvement. She said his family were assisting with inquiries.
Atkins also confirmed police were “aware” of reports of a social media post shared by an alleged Sydney gangland figure on Tuesday, claiming a shooting had been a case of mistaken identity.
“A young man has lost his life today and that’s obviously just tragic,” she said. “There were family who were home and, as I said, they’re assisting us and being very, very helpful.
“It’s an active crime scene and we’re obviously waiting for a lot of that information from our forensics who are on the scene.”

The incident comes three days after a separate home invasion in Guilford where a 28-year-old man was fatally shot, also in the early hours of the morning. NSW police made no suggestion the cases were linked.
It also follows the separate kidnapping murder of 85-year-old Chris Baghsarian earlier this year, who was abducted from his home in Sydney’s north in a case of mistaken identity.

articles.title: [Rear View] Is stupid the new Dutertismo?
articles.summary: Stupidity, in the context of the Duterte impeachment trial, is a conscious act. Arrogance can do that.

blocks.text: Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo called a witness, Gina Acosta, the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) special disbursing officer, stupid, “in the name of blind loyalty,” for handing over millions in confidential funds to the security chief of Vice President Sara Duterte on Duterte’s orders, and for taking the security chief’s word that all was good with the stack of receipts on faith.

Another senator-judge in the Duterte impeachment trial, Ping Lacson, used the same word for the cut-and-paste contents of the OVP’s confidential and intelligence fund (CIF) plans. The “plan” was drawn up, it turns out, only after the amount had already been decided by the Vice President apparently out of thin air. The prosecution’s spokesperson put it starkly: “pera muna, bago plano.” Money first, plan later.
Earlier, Lacson used “bopol,” slang for stupid, to refer to a senator-judge he did not name. He was just being fair and precise in calling out a colleague’s breathtaking displays of stupidity.
What the recent impeachment hearing reveals is that stupidity, in this context, is a conscious act.

Arrogance can do that. Being arrogant and stupid enough to think you won’t get caught. Arrogance, incompetence, or impunity, take your pick. Either way it unmasks a sense of entitlement to taxpayers’ money, molded by decades of treating a city like a kingdom, and the public purse like a private ATM for whatever strikes one’s fancy. Let’s see.

Thus far, the prosecution has presented evidence of payouts to informants with dodgy aliases, million-peso safehouses, Christmas parties, tree-planting activities. Receipts for liquidation? Liquidation can mean another thing in Dutertespeak. The confidential fund spending was so confidential that the disbursing officer herself didn’t know how it was spent, only the Vice President and her security chief apparently did.

Deposed Senate president Alan Peter Cayetano, a shameless Duterte enabler, cautioned the prosecution against language that could undermine the impartiality of the impeachment court, the offense in question being private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia’s use of the word “scam” to describe the confidential fund affair, and “mastermind” to describe the Vice President. The court struck both words from the record.

For his part, Senator-judge Francis Escudero, the presiding officer, reminded senator-judges that political neutrality cuts both ways. The sub judice rule the impeachment court has adopted applies not only to the senator-judges and the lawyers on both sides, but to the accused herself, the Vice President. Escudero made this clear in a ruling he read in full, one he ordered conveyed to Duterte through her lawyers.
Escudero also warned everyone, senator-judges included, against “trial by publicity.”

Arguing the case in media rather than the chamber would “threaten the court’s integrity, degrade its dignity, and weaponize the media to substitute public outrage for actual evidence.” And senator-judges, he added, are bound by their oath to “do impartial justice.” They are free to question witnesses for clarification, but not to turn those questions into partisan theater. Everyone: pakibaba ang kilay.

Ironically, that same hearing day, one such violation was ignored: Senator-judge Robin Padilla invoking the selfless sacrifice of Filipino heroes who, he’ll have you know, used aliases as a way of justifying the unjustifiable. He was clearly lawyering for the accused, but not de campanilla, as old lawyers would say. Just a hollow bell, ringing annoyingly.

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte trial: Whose soundbites did Escudero flag?

blocks.text: Perhaps the presiding officer should also include a rule against displays of stupidity, though it will predictably be ignored, since stupid people wearing robes tend to think they’re geniuses.

But unlike most netizens, Padilla’s interjections don’t make me laugh. They’re an invitation to anger, despair, or serious reflection on the decline of erudition in that chamber. That bar has been set that low.

And yet his remarks draw approving nods from those who revel in the open display of smart-shaming, where “bopol” has become a signifier of authenticity. Macho posturing, crude and divisive rhetoric, bloodlust, and now the celebration of the vacuous. Is stupid the new Dutertismo? – Rappler.com
Joey Salgado is a former journalist, and a government and political communications practitioner. He served as spokesperson for former vice president Jejomar Binay.

articles.title: How is Gilas’ World Cup bid after the fourth-window sweep?
articles.summary: Gilas Pilipinas’ World Cup hopes were hanging in the balance before the start of the fourth window of the 2027 FIBA Asian Qualifiers. According to Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone, closing the…

blocks.text: Gilas Pilipinas’ World Cup hopes were hanging in the balance before the start of the fourth window of the 2027 FIBA Asian Qualifiers.

According to Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone, closing the first round of the qualifiers with a 2-4 record left the Nationals with little room for error. Based on their computations, Gilas needed to win at least five games to have a favorable shot at making it back to the world stage.
Gilas needs to finish in the Top 3 of the Group E standings for an assured World Cup spot or become the best fourth-placed team in its group should Qatar finish outside the Top 4 in Group F.
The Qataris are currently tied with South Korea for fourth and fifth spots with similar 4-4 records.
But with the Nationals getting the job done in the two crucial games against Jordan and Iran, where does Gilas’ bid to make it to a fourth straight World Cup appearance currently stand?

The Nationals improved to a 4-4 slate following a pulsating 82-81 victory over Jordan and a 68-56 win over Iran, and they are now a game behind their victims, who both have 5-3 records for the third and fourth spots in the standings.
Australia and New Zealand hold the top two spots with 8-0 and 6-2 records, respectively.
“I think we do. I don’t know if we actually do, but I think we have some control (of our fate),” said Cone.

The wins against Jordan and Iran gave Gilas a lifeline, to say the least, but the November window, where it will figure in a rematch against Iran and a game against Syria, remains just as crucial for the Nationals.
A sweep of those two matches would put Gilas in position to move into the Top 3. Of course, the Nationals also need New Zealand and Australia to keep both Iran and Jordan from winning their games.
A loss would hurt but not totally take Gilas’ chances away, while another winless window would become problematic for the Nationals.
“At this point, we were hanging on Australia and New Zealand to continue winning their games so that we can elevate ourselves into the standings,” said Cone.

“We just got to the locker room saying that this was really a special moment, but this isn’t our goal. Our goal is to make it to the World Cup, and all this did was to give us a big step forward,” he added.
