articles.title: Nearly half of Tacloban barangays log dengue cases
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY, LEYTE, Philippines — Dengue cases in the city have risen to 323 as of Aug. 26, with nearly half of the city’s 138 barangays reporting confirmed cases, prompting health authorities to…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY, LEYTE, Philippines — Dengue cases in the city have risen to 323 as of Aug. 26, with nearly half of the city’s 138 barangays reporting confirmed cases, prompting health authorities to intensify mosquito-control measures and urge communities to eliminate breeding sites.

The City Health Office (CHO) warned that the number of cases could continue to increase in the coming months as more frequent rains create conditions favorable for the breeding of Aedes mosquitoes, which transmit the dengue virus.
Dr. Jaime Opinion, a city health official, said barangay officials and residents play a crucial role in preventing further transmission of the disease.

“Our barangay officials and residents are really the main players on this. We at the City Health Office and the Tacloban City Hospital can only help in terms of interventions,” Opinion said in an interview.
Opinion said communities should conduct regular cleanup activities in their neighborhoods and homes, particularly in areas where mosquitoes can breed.

The Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes that transmit dengue commonly lay their eggs in containers and other places where stagnant water collects, including discarded tires, cans, bottles, buckets, and uncovered water-storage containers.
Densely populated
Opinion also noted that many of the barangays reporting dengue cases are densely populated, which could facilitate the spread of the disease.
Dr. Gloria Fabrigas, chief of the Tacloban City Hospital, said the facility had treated 180 dengue patients from the start of the year through the previous week.
Of the total, only six patients came from outside Tacloban, she said.
Fabregas said 34 percent of the dengue patients treated at the hospital were between 6 and 20 years old, with males accounting for most of the cases in this age group. /cb

articles.title: 11 mining protesters in Nueva Vizcaya appeal for bail aid
articles.summary: BAYOMBONG, NUEVA VIZCAYA, Philippines — Eleven antimining villagers arrested during a police dispersal of a human barricade in Kasibu in this province appealed for financial assistance to post bail…

blocks.text: BAYOMBONG, NUEVA VIZCAYA, Philippines — Eleven antimining villagers arrested during a police dispersal of a human barricade in Kasibu in this province appealed for financial assistance to post bail after they were detained on Aug. 28.
Antimining leader Florentino Daynos made the appeal on behalf of the 11 villagers, one of whom was hospitalized after sustaining injuries during the dispersal in Barangay Paquet.
The protesters had set up a human barricade to oppose the entry of mining company vehicles carrying crude oil for exploration activities.
Daynos said residents were opposing the mining exploration because of what they claimed was a lack of adequate consultation and necessary permits.

“The residents are opposing mining exploration due to the alleged lack of adequate consultation and the necessary permit process, but they were violently dispersed and arrested,” he said in a statement.
Daynos himself and six others were arrested on Jan. 23 for defying a court order and forming a human barricade to block access to the mining exploration site of Woggle Corporation in Nueva Vizcaya.
He thanked residents who gathered at the site and showed solidarity and moral support for those opposing mining activities in defense of the environment and their livelihoods.

Kasibu police said the protesters came from the villages of Paquet, Dine and Catarawan. Police said those at the frontline of the blockade put up the strongest resistance as vehicles carrying oil products attempted to enter the mining site.
The protesters were facing charges of grave coercion; resistance and disobedience to a person in authority and their agents.
Brutality?
The arrests and dispersal drew condemnation from residents and other groups online, with some describing the police action as brutality.
Loreta Ramel-Galima, a former government official, said the protesters were peacefully exercising their rights.
For Atos Margie Kidsolan, police should uphold their mandate to enforce the law, prevent and control crimes, maintain peace and order and ensure public safety.
Nueva Vizcaya police director Col. Paul Bometivo acknowledged the criticism and said police understood the frustration in the community following their response to a 911 emergency call in Kasibu.
“We understand that emotions are high and that public trust feels fragile,” Bometivo said, adding that police remained committed to protecting the community despite the backlash.
He said police were required to respond to the 911 call, regardless of who made it, because the road had been obstructed.
Bometivo said the road was a municipal road certified by the municipal government and was therefore open to the public.
He said barricades preventing passage were not allowed and that police had the authority to regulate access when necessary to maintain public safety and order.
“Rights must coexist,” Bometivo said, adding that the right to protest should coexist with the right of others to pass through and use a public road.
Bometivo said police officers involved in the dispersal were only performing their duty to uphold the law, maintain peace and prevent further harm.
Kasibu police chief Capt. Lloyd Guillermo also denied that officers had escorted the mining company’s vehicles through the barricade.
Guillermo said police responded solely to the emergency call because the vehicles had the right to use the municipal road.
The protesters’ lawyer, Fidel Santos, said the dispersal occurred before he could speak with them.

Antimining protests and community-led barricades have been held in Barangay Paquet, Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya, since May 2026 to block exploration and drilling activities of North Luzon Mineral Resources Corp. (NLMRC).

Local farmers, Indigenous communities and environmental groups have raised concerns over possible environmental damage, threats to livelihoods and water security and alleged lack of genuine consultation and Free, Prior and Informed Consent.

Three Indigenous leaders were arrested on Aug. 19 over alleged grave coercion and disobedience but later posted bail. On Aug. 28, tensions escalated when police moved to clear a blockade against fuel trucks, resulting in the arrest of 11 to 13 protesters.

Provincial and municipal officials, including Gov. Jose Gambito and Kasibu Vice Mayor Alberto Bumolo Jr., have since negotiated with protesters for a temporary agreement to keep NLMRC personnel and equipment out of the site while talks continue. Religious leaders have also called for dialogue.
NLMRC holds an exploration permit covering a 4,456-hectare gold and copper exploration area in Barangay Paquet, Kasibu, approved in 2025. /cb

articles.title: Cat stationmaster draws visitors to Japan railway
articles.summary: JAPAN — A cat stationmaster at a local Japanese train station is drawing fans and boosting merchandise sales as the struggling railway operator banks on the feline’s popularity to attract more…

blocks.text: JAPAN — A cat stationmaster at a local Japanese train station is drawing fans and boosting merchandise sales as the struggling railway operator banks on the feline’s popularity to attract more tourists.

The female cat, tentatively named Nakano-san, found a home at Nakanocho Station in the port town of Choshi, Chiba prefecture, near Tokyo, after being rescued by a staff member last October. Thin and suffering from a cold that kept her eyes closed, she gradually recovered and grew accustomed to people under the care of station personnel.

The cat debuted as an apprentice employee in January before becoming a full-fledged stationmaster in May. She now works about once a week due to the summer heat and appears on social media as part of Choshi Electric Railway Co.’s public relations activities.
‘Special skills’

When Nakano-san—whose name includes the honorific suffix “san” in Japanese—reported for duty in mid-July, fans with cameras crowded the station premises. The feline used to roam the area, but the sweltering weather has led her to spend most of her time atop a bookshelf inside the station.
Remi Magami, the cat stationmaster’s secretary, said, “I hope Nakano-san will give people a reason to visit Choshi.”

Mayumi Ito, who is from Tokyo, said she has visited the station once a month since Nakano-san became stationmaster. The 47-year-old said she sees the cat as “like a relative’s child,” having known her since she was a kitten.

According to the cat’s online profile, she is curious, affectionate, playful and sleeps a lot. Her “special skills” include dropping the computer mouse on the floor and sleeping on top of documents. /cb

articles.title: US Supreme Court clears way for Trump to keep building White House ballroom
articles.summary: The National Trust for Historic Preservation argued the president did not have authority to proceed with construction.

blocks.text: The US Supreme Court has ruled that construction of a $400m (£297m) ballroom at the White House can go ahead, handing a win to President Donald Trump.
In a 5-4 ruling, the justices granted the Trump administration's emergency request, blocking lower court rulings that would have halted construction of an above-ground portion of the project.
The National Trust for Historic Preservation filed the legal challenge, arguing that the president did not have unilateral authority to proceed with construction.
Trump demolished the historic East Wing of the executive residence last autumn to begin building the ballroom.
On Friday, the high court had temporarily allowed construction of the White House ballroom to move forward.
Chief Justice John Roberts issued a stay, allowing the ballroom project, which includes a military complex, to continue while the high court considered the lawsuit aiming to halt it entirely.
On Monday, it was Roberts, a conservative, who sided with the three dissenting liberal justices to write that "construction is likely unlawful".
The dissenting justices said that Congress "has explicitly prohibited" the construction of any building or structure on federal grounds in the capital "without express authority of Congress".
They added that the legislative branch had "not passed any law resembling 'express authority' for the Executive's construction of it".

In the unsigned order, the five judges who cleared the way for construction said the Trump administration had established that it was likely to succeed in arguing that it would "suffer irreparable harm without a stay, and that the balance of equities tips in its favor".
"Beginning with the merits, the government is likely to prevail in showing that the Trust lacks standing to challenge the East Wing project," they wrote.
Trump has long argued that the White House needs a larger events space, and more recently, that it was important for his security.
The National Trust for Historic Preservation argued that construction was causing irreversible damage to a historical landmark.

articles.title: US Supreme Court allows Trump ballroom project to proceed
articles.summary: The ruling allows the Trump administration to continue the $400 million White House ballroom construction project for now.

image.caption: The ballroom project, hailed by Trump, has sparked controversy after the White House East Wing was torn downImage: Joyce N. Boghosian/White House/Planet Pix/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: The US Supreme Court on Monday allowed US President Donald Trump's administration to continue with the $400 million (€345 million) White House ballroom construction project for now.
The nonprofit National Trust for Historic Preservation first brought the case after the East Wing was torn down and work began on a 90,000-square-foot (8,360-square-meter) ballroom.
The Trump administration had asked the nation's highest court to intervene after federal courts determined that the project needed to be halted on the grounds of it not having congressional approval.
More to follow…

articles.title: First Nation leaders call parole for man guilty in Thunder Bay, Ont., trailer-hitch death 'miscarriage of justice'
articles.summary: First Nation leaders are seeking accountability following the full parole of Brayden Bushby, who was found guilty in the manslaughter of Barbara Kentner of Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation. Members of…

image.caption: Connie Kentner, sister of Barbara Kentner, and others marched on Parliament Hill in Ottawa on Monday to protest the full parole of Brayden Bushby, who was convicted of Barbara's manslaughter. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Thunder Bay·New

First Nation leaders are seeking accountability following the full parole of Brayden Bushby, who was found guilty in the manslaughter of Barbara Kentner of Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation. Members of Kentner's family were among those marching in Ottawa on Monday. The 34-year-old faced medical complications in the months after she was struck by a trailer hitch thrown at her from a moving vehicle in Thunder Bay in 2017.
Brayden Bushby sentenced in 2021, trailer hitch was thrown at 34-year-old in 2017 in Thunder Bay, Ont.
'We will continue seeking justice,' says Barbara Kentner's sister
WARNING: This story contains details of violence against Indigenous women, as well as references to racist beliefs and behaviours. Resources can be found at the bottom of this story.

Family and friends of Barbara Kentner, and First Nation leaders marched on Parliament Hill in Ottawa on Monday to raise concerns about the full parole of the man found guilty in the manslaughter of the 34-year-old from Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation.
In 2017, Kentner died from medical complications months after she was struck by a trailer hitch that Brayden Bushby threw from a moving vehicle.

items: Man convicted in woman's 2017 trailer hitch death in Thunder Bay, Ont., granted full parole

blocks.text: Bushby, now 27, was released on full parole with conditions on Aug. 13, according to documents from the PBC that were obtained by CBC News.

“There is a family on the other side of that decision, which is us. There is a community on the other side of that decision,” Connie Kentner, Barbara's sister, told media ahead of the march in Ottawa by about 30 people.

“There are Indigenous women and girls watching. There are families who are asking themselves whether the justice system will protect them and whether their voices will matter if something happens to them.”

The PBC’s decision documents say releasing Bushby on full parole won't pose “undue risk” and “will contribute to the protection of society” by facilitating his reintegration “back into society as a law-abiding citizen.”
Connie said the family “is left feeling that we have once again been failed by a system that is supposed to recognize and respect victims of crime.”
She also said the family wasn't made aware beforehand by the PBC that Bushby would be getting full parole.
CBC News previously reported that the family wasn't informed when Bushby was granted day parole in August 2023.

That day parole was revoked in July 2024 after the PBC said he violated various conditions. He was granted day parole again in December 2025 for six months and denied full parole. In June 2026, his day parole was extended.
Parole board says members do thorough assessments
During Monday's march, CBC News observed a representative of the PBC accepting a letter from Barbara's family.
No decision can undo what happened, but we will continue to speak for my sister, Barbara.- Connie Kentner, sister of Barbara Kentner
A spokesperson for the PBC later sent an emailed statement to CBC News that said the board "would like to express its sincere sympathy for the harm and loss that the Kentner family have experienced."
It also said the PBC can't comment directly on Bushby's release in accordance with the Privacy Act.

However, it added, registered victims "may receive information about the offender who harmed them, attend a PBC hearing, submit and present a victim statement at the hearing, and request PBC written decisions and to listen to the audio recording of PBC parole hearings."

items: Man convicted in 2017 trailer hitch death in Thunder Bay gets day parole extension

blocks.text: As for the family's lack of knowledge about his release, the PBC said “we understand that in this instance, some members of the victim’s family may not have been aware of the need to register with the PBC or Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) in order to receive and submit information.
“We have reached out to a representative of the family members to offer to assist them with registering and to answer any questions they may have."
Parole board board members receive extensive training to conduct thorough risk-based assessments, which include anti-racism and trauma-informed approaches, the statement added.
Chiefs call for 'culturally safe support service'

A news release issued Monday by Chiefs of Ontario said First Nation leaders are calling for “a dedicated, proactive, culturally safe support service for First Nations [victims] and families navigating the federal corrections and parole system.”

“Families should be informed directly of hearings and decisions, supported in exercising their rights, and provided with a clear point of contact throughout the process. No grieving family should be left to navigate a complex federal system on their own,” the release said.

items: Man convicted in 2017 trailer hitch death in Thunder Bay gets day parole extension

blocks.text: First Nation leaders at the march included those from Nishnawbe Aski Nation (NAN), Kitigan Zibi Anishinabeg, the Assembly of First Nations’ 2SLGBTQQIA+ Council and Grand Council Treaty #3.
Ogichidaa (Grand Chief) Francis Kavanaugh of Grand Council Treaty #3 spoke of the disproportionate number of Indigenous women, girls and two-spirit people who experience violence.
Decision on Bushby conditional parole 'unacceptable': Grand Chief Kavanaugh
“Today I am more ashamed of this country than I have been in a long time, and I stand with you all today in solidarity to call out this national shame,” Kavanaugh said.

“As I have said over and over again, this decision [to release Bushby] is a miscarriage of justice. It sends a horrible message to our people that our lives are only worth a small jail sentence and a few lines in the media.”
Kavanaugh told a story about his daughter, who attended college in Thunder Bay. He said a group of non-Indigenous boys threw full cans of Coke at her and her friend.
“This is not an isolated incident. It's systemic racism and hatred,” he said.

items: Brayden Bushby gets day parole in Barbara Kentner trailer hitch death in Thunder Bay after 1st one was revoked
Day parole revoked for Brayden Bushby, man convicted of trailer hitch death of Barbara Kentner in Thunder Bay

blocks.text: Connie has vowed to continue to tell her sister’s story.
“My sister was a real person. She was not just a victim. She had a laugh, she had dreams. She deserved to see her children grow and she deserved to be a grandmother,” she said.
“We will not let Barbara be forgotten. We will continue to seek justice and accountability.”

Support is available for anyone affected by the issue of missing and murdered Indigenous people. Immediate emotional assistance and crisis support is available 24/7 through a national hotline at 1-844-413-6649.
Mental health counselling and crisis support is also available 24 hours a day, seven days a week through the Hope for Wellness hotline at 1-855-242-3310 or by online chat at www.hopeforwellness.ca.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Sarah Law is a CBC News reporter based in Thunder Bay, Ont., and has also worked for newspapers and online publications elsewhere in the province. Have a story tip? You can reach her at sarah.law@cbc.ca.
With files from Brett Forester

articles.title: Group seeks dismissal of cops in Cagayan de Oro intern ‘abuse’
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY, Philippines — A group of criminologists has called for the dismissal of two police officers accused of acts of lasciviousness against two female criminology student-interns…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY, Philippines — A group of criminologists has called for the dismissal of two police officers accused of acts of lasciviousness against two female criminology student-interns inside a police station here.
Gerry Caño, president of the Professional Criminologists Association of the Philippines (PCAP), said the group would provide legal assistance to the interns and help file administrative complaints.
“We will lead and take charge of filing the administrative cases,” Caño said in an online interview.
He said officers found guilty of misconduct and violations of the Safe Spaces Act should face administrative and criminal charges, including possible revocation of their professional licenses.

“Touching or caressing the body parts of female interns must not be taken lightly or treated as a joke,” Caño said, urging the Commission on Higher Education and other concerned agencies to strengthen safeguards against sexual harassment during student internships.

PCAP is prepared to assist the victims in filing complaints before the Professional Regulation Commission, National Police Commission, People’s Law Enforcement Board and Office of the Ombudsman, Caño said.
Confirmation

The call followed confirmation by the Police Regional Office (PRO)-10 that a police captain and a corporal allegedly committed acts of lasciviousness against two female interns inside Police Station 7 of the Cagayan de Oro City Police Office (COCPO) on Aug. 8.
PRO-10 Director Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay Jr. said the two officers had been placed under restrictive custody at the Regional Personnel Holding and Accounting Unit.
“Misconduct will not be tolerated,” Babagay said, stressing that police personnel must uphold professionalism, integrity and respect for the dignity and welfare of others.

He directed the Regional Investigation and Detection Management Division to conduct a pre-charge evaluation, while COCPO director Col. Dexter Paje was instructed to assist the alleged victims through the Women and Children Protection Desk in filing criminal complaints.
The COCPO earlier formed an investigation team after a local higher education institution requested the withdrawal of its student-trainees following complaints of sexual harassment. /cb

articles.title: QC public schools suspend classes over unhealthy air
articles.summary: The Quezon City government suspended face-to-face classes in all public schools on Tuesday, Sept. 1, due to unhealthy air quality readings in several parts of the city. The city government said its…

blocks.text: The Quezon City government suspended face-to-face classes in all public schools on Tuesday, Sept. 1, due to unhealthy air quality readings in several parts of the city.
The city government said its latest Air Quality Index (AQI) readings showed “Very Unhealthy” to “Acutely Unhealthy” air quality levels.
The suspension covers Child Development Centers, Kindergarten, Grades 1 to 12, and the Alternative Learning System (ALS), pursuant to Local Government Memorandum Circular No. 3, s. 2025.

The increase in air pollution in some parts of the country, including the National Capital Region, may be linked to smoke or haze from ongoing fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, based on the current assessment.
Quezon City has 68 air quality sensors deployed in various parts of the city to monitor air pollution.
At these levels, exposure to polluted air may cause coughing, airway irritation, and difficulty breathing, particularly among people with asthma and other respiratory conditions.

Private schools and higher education institutions may decide whether to suspend face-to-face classes based on the decision of their respective administrators. However, they were encouraged to follow national or localized class suspension measures to protect teachers and students.
The public was advised to wear face masks, limit outdoor exposure and physical activities, and monitor succeeding announcements for further information.
Residents who need immediate assistance during an emergency may call Helpline 122.

articles.title: Poland launches sabotage probe in drone factory fire
articles.summary: According to the prosecution, the fire that occurred at a drone factory 150 kilometers south of Warsaw was deliberately set.

image.caption: WB Electronics is a producer of combat drones [FILE: April 2022] Image: Rafal Guz/PAP/picture alliance

blocks.text: Poland launched on Monday an investigation into a fire at a drone production factory south of Warsaw, suspecting terrorism and the involvement of a foreign intelligence service.

According to the prosecution statement, the probe had started "for participation in the activities of a foreign intelligence service directed against the Republic of Poland and for a terrorist offence, consisting of deliberately causing a fire on the premises of the WB Electronics factory using a device containing flammable materials."
The WB Electronics factory in Skarzysko-Kamienna, located 150 kilometers south of Warsaw, was reported on fire shortly after midnight Monday. The facility manufactures key components for drones.
Firefighters spent two hours containing the fire. There were no injuries in the incident.
The country's Internal Security Agency (ABW) is assisting the police with the investigation, officials said.
Poland supports Ukraine in its war with Russia
Earlier, Polish government accused Russia and Belarus of sending several agents into the country to carry out acts of sabotage.

Poland, who has been a vocal supporter of Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion into the country, has been increasing its security expenditure and military capabilities due to fears of Russian attacks.
WB Electronics, Poland's largest private defense company, is a supplier to the Polish military.

The company specializes in developing and manufacturing advanced defense technologies, including digital command and control systems, automated fire control systems, communications equipment, and modern unmanned strike systems.
Can Poland hold NATO’s line against Russia without the US?

articles.title: Canada's last captive whales set to leave Niagara Falls, Ont., Marineland for U.S. aquariums
articles.summary: Canada's last captive whales are set to leave the country today as the six belugas from Marineland are headed to two aquariums in the United States.

image.caption: A beluga whale swims in a tank at Marineland before being moved to an aquarium in the U.S., in what will be the last transfer of whales out of the closed park, ending whale captivity in Canada, in Niagara Falls, Ont., on Monday, Aug. 31, 2026. (Carlos Osorio/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Hamilton·Breaking
Canada's last captive whales are set to leave the country today as the six belugas from Marineland are headed to two aquariums in the United States.
The six remaining belugas are the captive whales in Canada
The closed Niagara Falls, Ont., tourist attraction is up for sale and the park has said it is running out of money and can no longer care for its animals.

items: More belugas from Marineland in Niagara Falls, Ont., head to new home in U.S.
Everyone loved Marineland — then the tide turned. A look inside the park's final days

blocks.text: Once today's journey is complete, Marineland will have shipped 30 belugas and four dolphins over six moves to five different aquariums in the largest collective relocation of captive whales the world has ever seen.
The whales and dolphins have moved to Shedd Aquarium in Chicago, SeaWorld locations in San Diego and San Antonio, Georgia Aquarium in Atlanta and Oceanografic Valencia in Spain.
Canada banned whale and dolphin captivity in 2019, but grandfathered in the animals at Marineland.
The federal government blocked a previous plan to move the whales to an aquarium in China, which prompted Marineland to threaten to euthanize the animals if it did not get an emergency cash infusion.

articles.title: Festival honouring Dolly Parton set for Nashville and London
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's estate says DollyFest will take the place of a traditional public memorial for the artist, just as she wanted.

blocks.text: Dolly Parton's estate has announced a festival honouring the life and legacy of the late singer, set for London and Nashville.

The "star-studded" two-day DollyFest will happen across two consecutive weekends in both cities in 2027, her estate said in a Monday press release, adding that the specific dates will be announced later.

Parton herself dreamed up an earlier version of the event, where she would host and perform alongside other artists, but the original January 2026 event was called off before it was announced publicly, due to Parton's health struggles, her estate said.
"DOLLYFEST will be the party of a lifetime she wanted to share with the world," her estate said.
DollyFest will take the place of a traditional public memorial for the artist, who died at the age of 80 on 25 August after a brief battle with cancer.

She was laid to rest at a private family funeral in Nashville on Friday, and placed next to her late husband, Carl Dean, at Woodlawn Memorial Park and Mausoleum in the Tennessee city, her great-niece said.

DollyFest organiser Danny Nozell, the founder and CEO of CTK Enterprises, said the estate is not discouraging people from celebrating Dolly in whatever ways they choose, but Parton did not want a traditional memorial.

"It feels more appropriate for us to take a beat, let all the tributes that immediately make sense occur naturally, and then, see through this festival-style concept that was truly dreamed up by Dolly," Nozell said.

"This is something that is authentic to her, something that feels right to me, and something that artists and fans around the world can participate in, while also giving everyone time to grieve, and giving everyone time to plan."

Originally from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee, Parton was a country music icon, philanthropist and businesswoman whose most famous songs included Coat of Many Colors, Jolene and I Will Always Love You.
In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote thousands of songs.
Parton took her writing seriously, and considered herself a songwriter over everything else. "It's my way of expressing myself," she said. "It's my therapy."
Since her death, emotional tributes from celebrities, politicians, and countless fans have flooded social media.
"A lot of people always say, WWDD (What Would Dolly Do?), and, well, at this moment, DOLLYFEST is WDWD (What Dolly Would Do!)," Nozell said.

articles.title: Conservative reshuffle: who’s who in Kemi Badenoch’s top team?
articles.summary: From a darling of the Tory right to a moderate former army officer, we profile the key players

blocks.text: Kemi Badenoch has kicked off the return to parliament with a reshuffle of her top team in order to take on Andy Burnham and Reform UK. She has made sweeping changes to the shadow cabinet and ruthlessly axed her shadow chancellor. Here is a run-down of the new characters sitting across from Labour on the opposition frontbench.
Andrew Griffith

Griffith, the MP for Arundel and South Downs, replaces Mel Stride as shadow chancellor, a role he has reportedly long coveted. He is loyal to Badenoch and was one of her first backers for leader in 2024.

Previously the chief financial officer and chief operating officer of Sky and the chair of Just Eat, he entered parliament as an ally of Boris Johnson after allowing the former prime minister to use his £9.5m townhouse as his leadership campaign HQ in 2019. He later became Johnson’s business adviser in government before running for election later that year.

Griffith was a backer of Liz Truss for leader and as her treasury minister was partially responsible for the disastrous mini-budget which caused economic chaos. He continued to defend the budget and said the market turmoil was linked to global events.

He was spotted last year at the launch of a climate denial group with Truss and Nigel Farage. Of his attendance, he said: “In any year, I attend hundreds of external events with business organisations and thinktanks, none of which automatically imply my endorsement.” He also recently spoke at a hard-right Cpac event organised by Truss.
Claire Coutinho

Widely tipped as one of the party’s rising stars, Coutinho made a fierce opponent to Ed Miliband when he was energy secretary and she shadowed his brief. A cabinet minister in Rishi Sunak’s government, she has been shifted to Badenoch’s economic unit and made shadow business secretary. Before parliament she was an investment banker at Merrill Lynch and KPMG, and has recently been holding the Labour government’s feet to the fire over rising energy bills.

blocks.caption: Claire Coutinho. Photograph: Justin Tallis/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Colleagues describe her as forensic, she delights in doing her own research about what she terms “the hidden cost of net zero” and has spoken up in parliament for whistleblowers at the national energy systems operator.

She became the first person to represent a political party at PMQs while pregnant earlier this year. Julia Lopez, the MP for Hornchurch and Upminster, will cover for her until the new year while she is on maternity leave. Coutinho is a keen cook in her spare time and once appeared on Nigella Lawson’s cooking gameshow The Taste.
Tom Tugendhat

Badenoch has made a show of purging the more “woke” MPs from the party, banning those who believe in pursuing net zero from standing at the next election for example, so the choice of the moderate Tugendhat as shadow foreign secretary surprised some.

blocks.caption: Tom Tugendhat. Photograph: House of Commons/PA

blocks.text: He replaces Priti Patel, who was sacked from the shadow cabinet. Tugendhat has experience in foreign affairs and previously served in the cabinet as security minister from September 2022 to July 2024. A former British army officer, he served in Afghanistan and Iraq.
A remainer, he has also said he does not support leaving the European convention on human rights, which puts him at loggerheads with Badenoch.
Tugendhat stood as the moderate option in the Tory party leadership contest in 2022, but was beaten by a long way by Truss. He tried and lost again against Badenoch when Sunak stood down in 2024.
He was banned from driving for six months in 2022 for using his mobile phone at the wheel.
after newsletter promotion
Katie Lam

A darling of the Tory right, Lam was only elected in 2024. She has been given the role of shadow housing and communities minister, and is likely to relish being Angela Rayner’s opposite number. She is a former special adviser to Johnson, and she worked on Sunak’s first leadership bid. Outside politics she worked at the PR company Portland Communications and the AI company Faculty.

blocks.caption: Katie Lam. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

blocks.text: She has sometimes been tipped as a potential defector to Reform after saying many immigrants should “go home” and supporting the policy of revoking indefinite leave to remain. Her comments on immigration have gone further than official Conservative policy at some points.
Lam has written five musicals, including an adaptation of The Railway Children.
Other changes and those staying on
Chris Philp remains shadow home secretary. He supported Badenoch’s successful leadership campaign and has held the role since she became party leader.
James Cartlidge stays on as shadow defence secretary, a position he has held since Sunak appointed him to the role in 2024.
Andrew Bowie takes up Coutinho’s previous role as energy secretary.
The shadow health secretary, Stuart Andrew, quit the frontbench to “focus on constituency work”, and Damian Hinds assumes his brief.

articles.title: Seabirds, silting and salt: Photos show some of the early effects of El Niño
articles.summary: The El Niño weather pattern won't peak for several months, but some effects are noticeable right now — both in terms of weather and human preparation. Here's a photographic look at some of the ways…

image.caption: Emmanuel Velasquez, head of forecasting and monitoring at the Panama Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology, shows a U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration map in Panama City on Aug. 5 of sea surface temperatures indicating unusually warm waters along the Peruvian coast as El Niño warm

blocks.text: World·Photos

The El Niño weather pattern won't peak for several months, but some effects are noticeable right now — both in terms of weather and human preparation. Here's a photographic look at some of the ways El Niño is already making its mark.
El Niño weather pattern won't peak for several months, but some effects already visible
El Niño — the natural climatic chaos agent that pops up periodically and spikes global temperatures — won't peak for several months and should last through next spring, experts say.
But there are noticeable effects right now, both in terms of weather and human preparation.
Here's a photographic look at some of the ways El Niño is already making its mark.
Low water levels in Panama Canal
A ship transits the Panama Canal near a hydrometeorological monitoring station on Aug. 27 as a lack of rainfall linked to El Niño affects the water levels in Gamboa, Panama.
(Enea Lebrun/Reuters)

Panama Canal Authority hydrologist Ricardo Guete shows the low water level on a gauge at the monitoring station in Gatun Lake. The authority will cap daily transits in early September as it gears up for a longer-than-usual El Niño season.
Displaced seabirds

Blue-footed boobies rest on rocks near the entrance to the Panama Canal on Aug. 5. Seabirds are appearing in unusual numbers near Panama City as El Niño warms the eastern Pacific and disrupts marine food supplies.
Preparations across Latin America

Governments across Latin America are mobilizing firefighters, activating contingency plans and preparing water, energy and transportation systems as El Niño strengthens across the Pacific, raising concerns about drought, extreme heat, flooding and other climate-related disruptions in the months ahead.

In Honduras, the Secretariat of Risk Management and National Contingencies declared a red alert in 75 municipalities in the central and southern parts of the country and a yellow alert in another 71 municipalities due to climate conditions affecting crops and livestock. Here, police officers on a motorcycle drive past a cornfield affected by drought on Aug. 26.
(Orlando Sierra/AFP/Getty Images)

Unlike hurricanes or earthquakes, this climate phenomenon develops gradually over months, which gives governments time to prepare before its most severe impacts arrive. In Peru, recently elected President Keiko Fujimori, left, has made preparing for El Niño a top priority.
(Ernesto Benavides/AFP/Getty Images)

Here, she speaks with Lima Mayor Renzo Reggiardo on July 9 during a cleaning and desilting operation on the Rímac River as a preventive measure against El Niño, which can cause heavy rainfall. Stones and gravel are removed to keep the channel clear and protect the city's drinking water.
Indonesia bakes
Across the Pacific, in Indonesia, salt farmers in West Java province are reaping the benefits of an El Niño-driven drought even as crop farmers brace for a prolonged challenge from the baking heat.
(Willy Kurniawan/Reuters)
Here, a farmer packs sacks of salt on a dyke during harvest at a salt pond in Pengarengan, Indonesia, on July 30.

For most of Indonesia, however, the weather pattern is not a positive. Here, villagers collect spring water with bottles at Gunung Batur village in Cilegon, Indonesia, on July 17, after struggling to access groundwater at their homes. Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) has warned that the country's dry season will be more intense and prolonged than average — in part due to El
Niño
(Bay Ismoyo/AFP/Getty Images)

A strengthening El Niño has already broken records for intensity in its early stages, and it will likely spark even more wild weather worldwide as it grows, “adding fuel to a planet already on fire,” United Nations officials have warned.

While El Niño is not a direct cause of Indonesia's catastrophic wildfire season, it serves as a catalyst, Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency chief told Reuters, with the additional heat and dryness enabling the fires to spread more quickly. Here, firefighters take a moment to commemorate Indonesia's 81st Independence Day by hoisting the national flag in an area affected by forest and land fires in Palangkaraya on Aug. 17.
(Reina/AFP/Getty Images)

Meanwhile in Canada, models suggest much of the country can expect a warmer winter than usual due to this El Niño, with British Columbia's normally wet south coast potentially seeing far less precipitation and a much lower snowpack. El Niño also typically means fewer tropical storms in the Atlantic.
For how El Niño will affect Canada, watch this video.
What exactly is a ‘super’ El Niño? And what does it mean for you?
With files from John Mazerolle, Nick Logan and The Associated Press

articles.title: Turkish deep-sea search vessel joins efforts to retrieve 20 still missing after Cyprus ferry disaster
articles.summary:
TCG Isin expected to play vital role in locating Filo Jet’s voyage data recorder 514 metres below surface

A deep-sea search and rescue vessel is on its way to Cyprus as Turkey joins efforts…

blocks.text: A deep-sea search and rescue vessel is on its way to Cyprus as Turkey joins efforts to retrieve the 20 people still missing after a passenger ferry capsized off the island’s northern coast.
The TCG Isin will join the vast operation to find survivors after the high-speed ferry sank on Sunday barely four nautical miles outside the port town of Kyrenia.

Authorities confirmed late on Monday – the first of three days of national mourning in Turkish-held northern Cyprus – that the tragedy had claimed eight lives, increasing the number of passengers still unaccounted for from 17 to 20.

A total of 241 of the 267 people aboard the Filo Jet, bound for Taşucu on the Turkish mainland when it began to take on water, had been rescued, they said. Almost all were either Turkish or Turkish Cypriot.

blocks.caption: Survivors arrive on shore. Of the 267 people on board the ferry, 241 have been rescued, authorities have said.  Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: International sympathy for the victims was highlighted as the Anglo-Cypriot founder of easyJet, Stelios Haji-Ioannou, offered €260,000 (£223,000) in support for the families of the deceased and missing, in a move hailed by Turkish Cypriot officials.

Visiting Kyrenia’s new port, where relatives gathered for news of loved ones on Monday, Tufan Erhürman, the self-styled state’s president, vowed search efforts would “continue with the same intensity, with no interruption, through the day and night”.
The Isin, capable of searching up to 3,000 metres below the sea surface, was due to arrive on Tuesday, he said, as he comforted the families of those still missing.

The ship is expected to play a vital role in recovering the ferry’s voyage data recorder, or black box, now viewed as key in deciphering the cause of a maritime disaster not seen since the breakaway territory declared independence in 1983.
Turkish Cypriot officials told the Guardian it was likely “all those responsible” would be charged with gross negligence as the seaworthiness of the 26-year-old ferry was also questioned.
The owners and shareholders of the privately owned company operating the passenger vessel have also been ordered to appear in court.

blocks.caption: The Turkish Cypriot leader, Tufan Erhürman, talks with relatives waiting for news outside the port of Kyrenia.  Photograph: Yiannis Kourtoglou/Reuters

blocks.text: It remained unclear whether those still missing had been trapped on board.

“Nobody is saying it publicly, but the hope of any survivors being found at this point is very slim,” one official confided. “Those who weren’t rescued very likely didn’t find a lifejacket. We believe many were elderly people and mothers with babies and young kids.”

In testimony – and video footage – that emerged on Monday, panic-stricken passengers could be seen desperately looking for lifejackets and screaming before the double-hulled ferry flipped over. One mother, Ayten Bicer, described feeling her 12-year-old daughter slip from her hands and disappear as the ferry capsized and sank in a matter of minutes. “She was saying, ‘Don’t let go.’ And I didn’t let go of my daughter. I swear, I didn’t let her go,” she sobbed. Two of Bice’s other children are among the 20 still missing.

blocks.caption: Ayten and Hayri Bicer wait for news of their two missing children outside the port of Kyrenia. Photograph: Yiannis Kourtoglou/Reuters

blocks.text: The captain of the ferry and seven crew members were detained on Monday as judicial authorities launched an inquiry into the tragedy amid claims they had been among the first to abandon ship.

Appearing before a local magistrate, the crew attributed the disaster to the bow of the catamaran-style ferry breaking apart in turbulent seas. But eyewitness accounts contradicted that version of events, with passengers telling officials that appeals to turn back to port had fallen on deaf ears as the ferry began to take on water.

Ünal Üstel, the northern Cyprus prime minister, told reporters the Filo Jet was lying on the seabed at a depth of 514 metres and that he foresaw the Turkish salvage ship “reaching [it] tomorrow afternoon”. Boats, helicopters, aircraft and other search and rescue teams had joined the operation, he said, adding that search efforts were continuing “on a 24-hour basis”.

Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when a coup aimed at union with Greece – engineered by the military junta then in power in Athens – prompted Turkey to invade and seize the island’s northern third. Ever since, as many as 45,000 mainland Turkish troops have been stationed in the north.
In 1983, the territory unilaterally declared independence, but in the absence of a settlement, decades of international isolation have ensued.

articles.title: Ex-congressman George Santos banned from betting platform for life
articles.summary: The prediction market operator Kalshi says Santos made barred trades and misleading comments that influenced prices.

blocks.text: Prediction-market operator Kalshi has permanently barred former US congressman George Santos from trading on its platform.

The company alleged that Santos, who was expelled from Congress following a series of fraud and identity-theft charges, placed bets in February related to his own attendance at US President Donald Trump's State of the Union address, according to a notice of disciplinary action.

Kalshi said its compliance team concluded his activity showed signs of insider dealing, prompting the lifetime ban. It said it was acting independently without waiting for external enforcement action.
Santos on X thanked Kalshi for the ban and said "Let's see how much longer you guys are around for".
The BBC has contacted Santos for comment.
In 2025, Trump ordered the release of Santos, who had been sentenced to a seven-year prison term for wire fraud and identity theft. He had served three months.
In July, Santos agreed to pay $35,000 to settle a federal investigation by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission into his State of the Union trades.
Kalshi, alleging Santos used non-public information to place bets, issued a penalty of $71,356 (£38,000).
The disciplinary moves come at a moment when prediction markets – which allow users to wager on outcomes ranging from elections to economic indicators – are facing heightened scrutiny.
Both Kalshi and rival Polymarket have reported an uptick in unusual trading patterns, forcing platforms to strengthen monitoring systems and respond more aggressively to potential misconduct.
Kalshi said Santos's case was referred to federal authorities earlier this summer after internal systems flagged suspicious behaviour linked to his account.
The company said the case centered on his trades in a market tied to whether he would attend Trump's address – an event he could directly influence.
Its compliance team found he placed a series of sizeable bets between 2 and 25 February, some of which were based on false or misleading public statements about his plans, according to the company.
His comments moved contract prices, and he ultimately earned $17,839.57 from the trades.

Santos has denied wrongdoing in various matters but has admitted to stealing identities of nearly a dozen people, including next of kin. He pleaded guilty to wire fraud and aggravated identity theft and served three months in prison before Trump commuted his sentence last year.
He embellished much about his biography in the run-up to his election to Congress in 2022. The former lawmaker was only the sixth in US history to be expelled from Congress.

The Kalshi episode underscores the growing compliance burden facing prediction markets as they attract more users and move closer to mainstream products. Regulators have signalled that platforms will be expected to meet higher standards as the industry matures, particularly when political or economic events are involved.
Santos, who was expelled from Congress following a series of fraud and identity-theft charges, has remained a polarising figure in US politics.

His criminal conviction led to a prison sentence of more than seven years, which Trump later commuted. Santos has denied wrongdoing in various matters, but has admitted to stealing identities of nearly a dozen people, including next of kin.

articles.title: Burnham to tell Commons more public ownership is only way to grow UK economy
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Prime minister wants to ‘bring back hope’ by tackling cost of living as MPs call for electoral reform

Andy Burnham will drive home his pledge to bring more essential services back…

blocks.text: Andy Burnham will drive home his pledge to bring more essential services back into public control, telling MPs in the Commons on Tuesday that it will be the only way to improve growth across the country.

Burnham will address the house for the first time in 16 years from the frontbench, and six weeks since he became prime minister, after spending the summer recess announcing a slew of policies that will now be put before MPs.

He will use the statement to put public control of services at the heart of his priorities for the coming months, sources told the Guardian, saying he would make the case that it would unlock investment, jobs and growth.
Burnham will say that the cost of everyday services to family budgets is holding back the economy and promise a plan to regain control of the costs.
A No 10 source said: “Andy is optimistic about our country’s future. He has a clear plan for how we turn things round. He is determined we make this the moment we bring back hope.”

The prime minister will face an early test of his commitment to public control as he mulls legislation to make it easier to bring struggling utilities such as Thames Water under government ownership. The Guardian reported last week Burnham was considering laws to make it easier to put companies into insolvency proceedings and then take control of them afterwards.

blocks.caption: The prime minister has said taking water companies such as Thames Water into public control is crucial to his vision for the country. Photograph: Maureen McLean/Shutterstock

blocks.text: He will also face crunch decisions on possible changes to the immigration bill to exempt carers, as well as pressure from MPs to back moves towards electoral reform. A quasi-judicial decision on whether to allow more North Sea drilling is also expected soon: a highly divisive issue within the party.
Burnham will tell MPs that he wants to “bring back hope” in politics and pledge to work constructively with opposition parties.

On Monday, the Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, sacked her shadow chancellor Mel Stride and shadow foreign secretary Priti Patel, promoting Andrew Griffith in Stride’s place in the hope of making further inroads in attacking Burnham’s economic approach. Patel is replaced by Tom Tugendhat.

blocks.caption: Andrew Griffith, right, with Kemi Badenoch and former chancellor Jeremy Hunt, second from right, during a visit to Godalming, Surrey earlier this year. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

blocks.text: Burnham will give a scathing analysis of how privatised services have done little for the public, saying that utilities and transport have not been run in the public interest and are neither reliable nor affordable.

He will point to action already being taken to bring more bus routes under public control, including through a partnership between No 10 North and the West Midlands Combined Authority. The Liverpool City Region will start taking control of bus services from next weekend.

Burnham has promised a 10-year project to take public control of utilities which is expected to be a major focus of his next few months in power. Allies have said the prime minister is “completely committed” to putting utilities such as energy and water companies into public control, and is looking at every option.

As well as setting out key priorities for his first months in office, Burnham will face a two-hour grilling from MPs about policies announced over the summer – including a cut to VAT on energy bills, £2 bus fares, the scrapping of digital ID, a major expansion of devolution and a plan for a national care service.

Opposition MPs are expected to ask tough questions on how the pledges will be funded as well as how Burnham expects to fill a £4.7bn gap in the defence investment plan left by his predecessor, Keir Starmer.
On Tuesday, the justice secretary, Alex Norris, will also present the government’s plans to cut the number of prisoners eligible for early release, including the killers of PC Andrew Harper.
after newsletter promotion

Though the decision will see most of those convicted of manslaughter remain in prison to serve longer sentences, it has also raised alarm that the number of prison places may reach crisis point faster.

Later in the week, Burnham will face Badenoch for his first prime minister’s questions and will also need to navigate the growing number of Labour MPs who are heaping pressure on him to toughen up the representation of the people bill which returns to the Commons this week.

Nearly 100 MPs have called on Burnham to back a commission on electoral reform, given the prime minister has previously been a vociferous supporter of changing the voting system. MPs have also been angered by the decision to drop any cap on party donations, after pressure from trade unions, despite the prime minister having previously backed a cap of £500,000.

The Liberal Democrats said on Monday they would put their full backing behind an amendment from the Labour MP Alex Sobel that calls for a commission on electoral reform to be established within 100 days.

The party’s leader, Ed Davey, said it was a chance for Burnham to prove he was different to Starmer. “Reform stand to benefit from our terrible voting system and could manipulate it all the way to No 10,” he said.

Davey added: “Keir Starmer never would have agreed to a national commission. He failed to grasp that it is our role as progressives to fix the broken system the Conservatives created. The only question now is: what kind of politician is Andy Burnham? Is he willing to do the right thing?”
Reform will host its party conference this week in Birmingham, with Farage speaking on Friday.

In the latest poll from More in Common, Labour hold a four-point lead over Reform, with the Tories a point behind. The latest Opinium poll found that Burnham’s net approval rating had increased over the last fortnight by three points.

articles.title: Nepal rescuers blast hillside in search of hydropower workers as families wait anxiously
articles.summary: Rescuers have resorted to explosives as they struggle to reach trapped workers, as the flooding death toll reaches 939.
articles.byline: Jake Lapham, Kelly Ng, BBC Nepali

blocks.text: The families of more than 600 workers believed to be trapped in a vast network of mud-filled tunnels along Nepal's Trishuli River are clinging to hope their loved ones can be found alive.

Rescuers continued battling to reach them on Monday, using explosives to blast into the hillside before pumping air into the Trishuli-3A site - fearing a critical window to reach survivors is closing.
"I wish we could find him. I wish he would come home," Anushila Bhandari, wife of Aurus Bhandari, a 33-year-old engineer missing on a project site, told BBC Nepali.
It comes as the death toll from the flood disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border reached 939, according to the country's disaster management authority.
The agency also revised its estimate of the number of missing to 3,925, of whom 592 are foreign nationals.
Roughly one in seven missing people are believed to be workers at the hydropower plants. Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah said on Monday that 279 people had been rescued from the sites.
The rescue operation is being spearheaded by an international team made up of Chinese and Nepalese military personnel, while experts from India, Korea and Australia are also involved.
"I still have a 50% hope that he is alive because there is an oxygen system inside," Sita Pandey, whose husband was working in the plant when the floods hit, told Nepalese daily Kantipur.

Nepal relies heavily on hydropower and has spent years developing the projects along its mountainous river systems. At least 11 projects either completed or under construction were damaged in the floods, authorities said.
Rescuers began pumping air into a tunnel over the weekend, but the families of those trapped say that should have been done earlier.
A team was able to get into a tunnel leading to one hydropower plant earlier on Monday, but withdrew after finding no one there.

"The longer it takes, the more our hope dies. This operation must move much faster because every second is meaningful to us," Jiban Khadka, whose relative is also trapped inside the plant, told Kantipur.
"It's a frustratingly slow operation," Khadka added.
Nepalese leader Shah said rescue operations had been "intensified", noting that 11,379 people had been rescued so far.
Another family member anxiously awaiting news is Priya Kharel, whose brother Milan was working as an engineer in the Upper Trishuli-1 plant when the floods hit.
"Those who returned from the hydropower site said there were people inside the tunnel," she told BBC News Nepali. "So there is hope that if the army reaches them quickly, they can be saved."

articles.title: Trump threatens further action as US and Iran exchange fire in new flare-up
articles.summary: Washington says it acted after observing Iran was planning to deploy fresh mines in strait of Hormuz

blocks.text: The US and Iran have exchanged fire for the first time in a month, with missiles and drones fired at Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the strait of Hormuz, and Iran targeting US military bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates in response.

The US president, Donald Trump, on Monday threatened further action. The US is to trying to prise open Tehran’s grip on shipping going through the strait, which before the war accounted for a fifth of the world’s seaborne energy supply. Washington claimed that Iranian control over the waterway had been loosened by repeated US attacks on Iranian missile launchers and radars.

US Central Command said it acted late on Sunday, launching the first strikes on Iran since July, after it detected the Iranians were planning to deploy fresh mines in the strait. Last week Trump claimed the US navy had cleared the strait of mines for the first time since the conflict started on 28 February, a claim the Iranians rejected as lies.

In response to the US attack, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it “targeted technical infrastructure, maintenance facilities and enemy fighter jet positions at the US-operated King Hussein and al-Azraq airbases in Jordan” with ballistic missiles, causing “heavy damage”. The UAE defence ministry said it intercepted a drone over its territorial waters.

Trump responded to the Iranian reprisals by telling Fox News: “We’re going to hit them hard. There will be a response.” The US president called Iran “officially a failed nation without an airforce, a navy or a currency”, adding that inflation was at 300% and its leaders were incapable of representing their country.
The White House last week signalled that Trump was shelving military measures in favour of a campaign to destroy the Iranian economy by enforcing sanctions.

Iranian state TV claimed the military exchanges escalated on Sunday after a tanker caught fire when hitting two Iranian naval mines while attempting to pass through the southern side of the strait close to Oman. Officials later said Iran had targeted three ships trying to navigate the southern route that Tehran says is unauthorised.
The IRGC warned that other ships violating ⁠its rules would face ​the ​same fate and ​said compliance with ​its regulations ‌for ​passage ​through the strait was mandatory.

However, the Iranian president, Masoud Pezeshkian, told Pakistan’s prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, in a bilateral meeting on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan on Monday that continuing the war was not in Iran’s interest, adding he was still ready to implement the memorandum of understanding with the US that Pakistan had mediated in June.
The Iranian currency was under renewed pressure on Monday and the inflationary impact of its rapid depreciation is causing growing concern to MPs.

blocks.caption: People buy bread from a street vendor beneath an anti-US billboard in Tehran. Photograph: Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Iran and Oman last week reached a verbal agreement on a new single temporary route for shipping through the strait in which Oman retains controls on shipping in Omani waters.

One western diplomat familiar with the talks said the message had got through to Washington that this bilateral agreement would not be enough for Iran to open the strait and that to do so would at least require the US to end its blockade of Iranian oil exports, something Trump is not currently prepared to do. “There are many in Iran determined to torment Trump right up to the end of his presidency,” the western diplomat said. “We are stuck.” He said some oil was getting through but not very much.

The latest fighting broke out late on Sunday with the US claiming it attacked Larak Island in the strait. A US official said: “I can confirm that earlier today US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island. Islamic ⁠Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait of Hormuz.”

The IRGC said the US attack had killed three soldiers and wounded two citizens. Iran’s Mehr news agency quoted the IRGC as saying its air defences shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the strait, causing it to crash ‌into Gulf waters.
The US said all missiles fired towards US forces in Jordan had been intercepted with no significant impact.

The White House claim that the US now controls the strait and ships are free to navigate its waters is heavily contested. Tanker Trackers, an independent tracking agency, said on Sunday: “Past seven days daily average of crude oil exports via the strait of Hormuz was 3.8m barrels per day. During the formal ceasefire period (which in effect only lasted for 25 days), it was 9.8m.” The agency said Iranian crude exports had been at zero for some time.

A meeting of G20 finance ministers in the US is likely to lead to a clash over American demands that more countries impose sanctions on Iran or face punitive action by Washington. The German finance minister, Lars Klingbeil, who is facing difficult regional elections, is to urge the US to bring the conflict to a diplomatic end, pointing to the war’s inflationary impact.

The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, echoing Trump, claimed on Monday the resumed exchanges of fire showed Iran was “lashing out” because the fresh sanctions were taking ​a heavy toll on its already battered economy.

blocks.caption: Scott Bessent speaks to reporters as he arrives for the G20 finance ministers meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. Photograph: Allison Joyce/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: “They’re taking it very seriously ... they’re in shock at the state of their ‌economy,” Bessent told reporters at the G20 finance ministers ‌meeting in North Carolina. “I would think that they are lashing out kinetically because they are losing economically.”

China, a key Iranian customer for its oil, has said it opposes the new US sanctions campaign. In Kyrgyzstan, Pezeshkian will be looking for concrete assurances from the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, that he will not allow the US to spread economic chaos through Iran.

articles.title: Head of Viktor Orbán’s favourite thinktank quits over unpaid wages
articles.summary:
Frank Furedi announces resignation from MCC Brussels after organisation’s staff ‘not paid in July or August’

The head of Viktor Orbán’s favourite Brussels thinktank has quit, citing unpaid…

blocks.text: The head of Viktor Orbán’s favourite Brussels thinktank has quit, citing unpaid wages since the change of government in Hungary.

The sociology professor Frank Furedi said he was resigning as the executive director of MCC Brussels with “immediate effect” on Monday over “persistent failure to provide the contractually agreed funds”.
A spokesperson for MCC Brussels confirmed Furedi’s resignation and said no one working for the organisation in the EU capital had been paid in July or August.

MCC Brussels launched in late 2022 with a self-styled mission to shake up political debate in the EU capital, although critics said it defended Orbán’s illiberal rule in Hungary while using a well-funded position to attack civil society groups.

It was an ostensibly independent offshoot of the Mathias Corvinus Collegium Foundation in Budapest, a training ground for Orbán’s Fidesz party that was lavishly funded by his rightwing nationalist government.

The future of MCC Brussels was thrown into doubt when Péter Magyar won a landslide election victory in April pledging to crack down on corruption in Hungary, which numerous independent organisations said had proliferated during Orbán’s 16 years in power. Soon after his victory, Magyar promised to end state financing for MCC Budapest and to investigate a large transfer of state assets to the organisation, which he described as a crime.
Furedi has previously dismissed Magyar’s claims of a criminal transfer of assets to MCC Budapest as “bullshit”, while MCC Brussels said it condemned corruption by all politicians.
after newsletter promotion

In a letter to the senior leadership of MCC Budapest seen by the Guardian, Furedi wrote: “Without the contractually agreed resources, our colleagues cannot function and are facing serious economic hardship. We have been placed in a situation where our individual reputations and the integrity of our intellectual mission are systematically undermined.”
The failure to provide funds, Furedi said, meant MCC Brussels had effectively ceased operations and was unable to pay suppliers or meet conditions under Belgian insolvency law.

Furedi said he intended to ensure, “along with like-minded individuals, the work and intellectual legacy of our institution will continue to flourish in another form”, without elaborating on future plans.
The letter was first reported by Politico. MCC Budapest did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

MCC Budapest has also seen change at the top following the election of the new government. The MCC board was previously led by Viktor Orbán’s chief of staff, Balázs Orbán, who is no relation to the former prime minister. Balázs Orbán, now an MP for the Fidesz party, announced he was standing down as chair in June.

The MCC Brussels spokesperson said after Furedi’s resignation and a round of lay-offs in June and July, MCC Brussels was down to 12 staff and three research fellows. Before the cuts it had employed 25 people and was one of the best-funded thinktanks in Brussels.

articles.title: EXPLAINER: Flood control projects planned for 39 sites across NCR by 2026
articles.summary: In response to severe flooding across the country, Malacañang announced the 39 sites in the National Capital Region (NCR) eyed for flood mitigation projects.

blocks.text: In response to severe flooding across the country, Malacañang announced the 39 sites in the National Capital Region (NCR) eyed for flood mitigation projects.

According to the Palace’s announcement, the types of projects include bioretention areas and detention ponds, river floodplains, and inland wetlands. Several rivers are also being studied for river renaturation.
Following the heavy rains in August 2026, authorities recorded 201.8 millimeters of rainfall in NCR in just five hours.
This is nearly half of the rainfall recorded during Typhoon Ondoy in 2009, when 455 mm of rain fell in Metro Manila over 24 hours.

Historically, a large portion of NCR’s drainage system was completed over 50 years ago. Because Manila had a much smaller population at the time, small pipes and narrow waterways were sufficient back then.
As time goes by, however, population growth, urbanization, and climate change have altered the country's drainage needs.
NCR drainage system upgrade
According to structural engineer Juan Paolo Bersamina, the NCR's drainage problem must be solved holistically.
“To think that drainage should be solved holistically, dapat buo natin siyang sino-solve rather than patche-patche 'yung pagso-solve natin,” Bersamina said.
(To think that drainage should be solved holistically, we should solve it as a whole rather than taking a piecemeal approach.)
He noted that urbanization in Metro Manila presents a massive challenge, adding to the expenses needed to complete the projects.

“Due to urbanization, marami nang nakatayong buildings. Minsan, doon na sa edge nu'ng drainage line so it's really, minsan, iko-consider mo na 'yung cost o pagbubungkal, 'yung maapektuhang building near the drainage,” Bersamina said.

(Due to urbanization, many buildings have already been constructed. Sometimes, they are built right at the edge of the drainage line, so you really have to consider the cost of excavation and the structures that will be affected near the drainage.)
“So sometimes, ‘yun na, nagkakaroon na ng domino effect na mahirap na lalong i-solve because of the urbanization,” he added.
(So sometimes, a domino effect occurs that makes it even harder to solve because of urbanization.)

For example, in Quezon City, P27 billion is needed just to complete its single drainage master plan, according to the local government unit. This represents more than half of the city's annual budget of P40.5 billion.
In the recently proposed flood mitigation projects, what types of structures is the government planning to build?
Detention ponds
A detention pond is a facility where rainwater is temporarily stored to prevent it from rushing into low-lying areas.
“Ang kalupaan natin is mayroong mataas na lugar, may mababang lugar. '’Yung ulan na dumaloy mula sa mataas na lugar, bubulusok 'yan sa mababang lugar,” Bersamina said.
(Our land consists of high areas and low areas. Rain flowing from high elevation will rush down to low-lying areas.)
“The purpose of the detention basin is sasaluhin niya 'yung baha na 'yun so that mapipigilan niya na bumuhos 'yung baha na 'yun further downstream,” he added.
(The purpose of the detention basin is to intercept that floodwater so it does not pour further downstream.)
In a highly urbanized area, a detention pond is considered the best solution to flooding.
However, it is not simply a matter of digging up land, as the area's overall drainage layout must be carefully considered.
Bersamina explained that connecting disconnected or misaligned drainage lines from different locations into a single detention pond presents a major engineering challenge.
River floodplains
A river floodplain is a flat area of land adjacent to a river.
It acts like a sponge that absorbs water whenever the river overflows, preventing floodwaters from surging directly into low-lying communities.
In addition, floodplains help absorb excess nutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen, which negatively impact rivers. They also provide significant benefits to local wildlife.
Inland wetlands
Considered the “Kidneys of the Earth,” inland wetlands purify and filter trapped inland wastewater before it flows into the sea and other bodies of water.
They can absorb large volumes of rainwater, thereby reducing or mitigating floods, and can even help combat drought.
“Hinahayaan mo siyang basa at a certain time. It also serves as a storage of rainwater or flood bago siya dumaloy sa downstream portion ng pampang,” Bersamina explained.
(You allow it to stay wet at a certain time. It also serves as storage for rainwater or floodwater before it flows to downstream banks.)
River Renaturation
In river renaturation, an artificial or damaged waterway is restored to its natural form and function.

“So binabalik mo sa ilog 'yung dapat niyang lapad, and then 'yung dapat niyang characteristics. Let's say, it should have trees on the riverbanks, may mga damo, ibinabalik po natin 'yun. Kasi ‘yung paglalagay ng mga greenery, let’s say mga grass in the riverbanks, that also helps reduce flooding eh,” Bersamina explained.

(So you restore the river's original width and natural characteristics. For example, if it should have trees and grass along the riverbanks, we bring those back. Adding greenery, like grass on riverbanks, also helps reduce flooding.)
The government also plans to add green spaces and green corridors—areas planted with numerous trees and vegetation to preserve biodiversity.
Establishment and rehabilitation of mangrove forests were also included in Malacañang's list.
According to Bersamina, while the projects have good intentions in theory, executing the plan for a place like Metro Manila will be quite challenging.

“Expensive kasi nga po, mag-a-acquire ka ng land. 'Yung iba, tumatanggi kasi nga 'yung mga may-ari ng property are supposed to develop that. Talagang babalik tayo du'n sa konsepto ng land use plan, na dapat, magkasundo lahat ng mga city,” he noted.

(It is expensive because you have to acquire land. Others refuse because property owners are supposed to develop those sites. We really have to return to the concept of a comprehensive land use plan, where all cities must be in agreement.)
According to Malacañang, the sites chosen for the projects were identified by the Dutch engineering consultancy firm Haskoning.

The Palace said its preliminary study has been completed, and authorities are now focusing on detailed engineering plans, which are expected to be finalized before the end of August 2026.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: US singer D4vd's celebrity lawyers withdraw from murder case
articles.summary: The singer, 21, will be now represented by a public defender in the murder trial of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. He has pleaded not guilty.

blocks.text: The celebrity lawyers hired to represent US musician D4vd in his upcoming murder trial have withdrawn from his case.

The star, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, has been appointed a public defender to mount his defence for the murder of Celeste Rivas Hernandez, 14, whose remains were found in September 2025 in a Tesla registered to his address.
Burke, 21, pleaded not guilty to the murder charges in Los Angeles court on Monday.
A judge determined last month that he will stand trial for murder. Prosecutors have alleged he stabbed the teen after years of sexual abuse, before dismembering her body.
A pretrial hearing is set for 19 October.

Lawyers Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski and Regina Peter said in a statement to BBC that the court granted their request to withdraw from the case and has appointed the Los Angeles County Public Defender's to represent the singer.
The statement said that it D4vd "qualified for appointed counsel".

"We continue to support David and his defense against these serious charges," they said. "We are grateful that the Los Angeles County Public Defender's Office has taken over the representation and that David has a highly capable and committed team of attorneys and investigators behind him."
Berk, who led the defence team, has previously represented US actor Mel Gibson and film mogul Harvey Weinstein, as well as singer Britney Spears and actress Lindsay Lohan.
In a statement, deputy public defender Walid Kandeel said Burke "is entitled to a defense that takes his circumstances seriously and carefully examines the evidence".
"We are committed to providing him with that defense," he said.
